links.context: This set of Data Structure Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Searching”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following searching algorithm is fastest?
mcqs.explanation: Binary search has the least time complexity (equal to log n) out of the given searching algorithms. This makes binary search preferable in most cases.

mcqs.question: Where is linear searching used?

options.b: b) When the list has only a few elements
options.c: c) When performing a single search in an unordered list
options.d: d) When the list has only a few elements and When performing a single search in an unordered list

mcqs.answer: d) When the list has only a few elements and When performing a single search in an unordered list
mcqs.explanation: It is practical to implement linear search in the situations mentioned in When the list has only a few elements and When performing a single search in an unordered list, but for larger elements the complexity becomes larger and it makes sense to sort the list and employ binary search or hashing.

mcqs.question: How can Jump Search be improved?

options.a: a) Step size should be other than sqrt(n)
options.c: c) Begin from the kth item, where k is the step size
options.d: d) Start searching from the end

mcqs.answer: c) Begin from the kth item, where k is the step size
mcqs.explanation: This gives a very slight improvement as you are skipping the first k elements.

mcqs.question: Which of the following searching algorithm is used with exponential sort after finding the appropriate range?
mcqs.explanation: In exponential search, we first find a range where the required elements should be present in the array. Then we apply binary search in this range.

mcqs.question: Which of the following searching algorithm is fastest when the input array is not sorted but has uniformly distributed values?
mcqs.explanation: Out of the given options linear search is the only searching algorithm which can be applied to arrays which are not sorted. It has a time complexity of O(n) in the worst case.

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity of Z algorithm for pattern searching (m = length of text, n = length of pattern)?
mcqs.explanation: Z algorithm is an efficient pattern searching algorithm as it searches the pattern in linear time. It has a time complexity of O(m + n) where m is the length of text and n is the length of the pattern.

mcqs.question: In which of the cases uniform binary search fails compared to binary search?

options.b: b) Many searches will be performed on several arrays of the same length
options.c: c) Many searches will be performed on the same array
options.d: d) A table lookup is generally faster than an addition and a shift

mcqs.explanation: Uniform binary search code is more complex to implement than binary search as it involves mid points to be computed in hand before search.

mcqs.question: Interpolation search is a variation of?
mcqs.explanation: Interpolation search is a variation of binary search which gives the best result when the array has uniformly distributed values. Interpolation search goes to different positions depending on the value being searched whereas binary search always goes to the middle element.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an application of binary search?

options.a: a) To search in unordered list
options.d: d) To find the lower/upper bound in an ordered sequence

mcqs.answer: a) To search in unordered list
mcqs.explanation: In Binary search, the elements in the list should be sorted. It is applicable only for ordered list. Hence Binary search in unordered list is not an application.

mcqs.question: Which of the following step is taken after finding an element having value greater than the element being searched in jump search?

options.a: a) binary search takes place in the forward direction
options.b: b) binary search takes place in a backward direction
options.c: c) linear search takes place in the forward direction
options.d: d) linear search takes place in the backward direction

mcqs.answer: d) linear search takes place in the backward direction
mcqs.explanation: First an element having value greater than the element being searched is found. After this linear search is performed in a backward direction.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an advantage of Fibonacci Search?

options.a: a) When the element being searched for has a non uniform access storage
options.b: b) It can be applied efficiently on unsorted arrays
options.c: c) Can be used for large arrays which do not fit in the CPU cache or in the RAM
options.d: d) Can be used in magnetic tapes

mcqs.answer: b) It can be applied efficiently on unsorted arrays
mcqs.explanation: When the speed of access depends on the location previously accessed, Fibonacci search is better compared to binary search as it performs well on those locations which have lower dispersion. Fibonacci search won’t work on unsorted arrays. The input should be a sorted array or array should be sorted before Fibonacci search.

mcqs.question: In which of the following case jump search will be preferred over exponential search?

options.a: a) when the given array is very small in size
options.b: b) when the given array is very large in size
options.c: c) jumping backwards takes significantly more time than jumping forward
options.d: d) jumping forward takes significantly more time than jumping backwards

mcqs.answer: d) jumping forward takes significantly more time than jumping backwards
mcqs.explanation: Jump search only needs to jump backwards once, while an exponential search can jump backwards up to log n times. Thus jump search will be preferred if jumping backwards is expensive.

mcqs.question: What is the best case for linear search?
mcqs.explanation: The element is at the head of the array, hence O(1).

mcqs.question: What is the worst case for linear search?
mcqs.explanation: Worst case is when the desired element is at the tail of the array or not present at all, in this case you have to traverse till the end of the array, hence the complexity is O(n).

{

public static int fibSearch(final int key, final int[] a) 
{
        int low = 0;
        int high = a.length - 1;
        int fibCurrent = 1;
        int fibPrev = 1;
        int N = a.length;
        while (low <= high) 
        {
            while(fibCurrent < N)
            {
                int tmp = fibCurrent + fibPrev;
                fibPrev = fibCurrent;
                fibCurrent = tmp;
                N = N - (fibCurrent - fibPrev);

            final int mid = low + (high - low) - (fibCurrent + fibPrev);
            if      (key < a[mid]) high = mid - 1;
            else if (key > a[mid]) low = mid + 1;
            else return mid;
        }
        return -1;
}

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity of Fibonacci Search?

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Exponential Search”.

mcqs.question: Exponential search algorithm requires which of the following condition to be true?

options.b: b) array should have not be sorted
options.c: c) array should have a less than 128 elements
options.d: d) array should be partially sorted

mcqs.explanation: Exponential sort requires the input array to be sorted. The algorithm would fail to give the correct result if array is not sorted.

mcqs.question: Which of the following searching algorithm is used with exponential sort after finding the appropriate range?
mcqs.explanation: In exponential search, we first find a range where the required elements should be present in the array. Then we apply binary search in this range.

mcqs.question: Exponential search has ____________

options.a: a) neither an exponential space complexity nor exponential time complexity
options.b: b) exponential time complexity but a linear space complexity
options.c: c) exponential space complexity but a linear time complexity
options.d: d) both exponential time and space complexity

mcqs.answer: a) neither an exponential space complexity nor exponential time complexity
mcqs.explanation: Exponential search has neither an exponential space complexity nor exponential time complexity. It is named exponential search because it searches for an element in an exponential manner.

mcqs.question: Choose the correct while loop statement from the following that finds the range where are the element being search is present (x is the element being searched in an array arr of size n)?

options.a:
a)
while (i < n && arr[i] <= x)  
        i = i*2;
options.b:
b)
while (i < n && arr[i] <= x)  
         i = i/2;

mcqs.answer:
a)
while (i < n && arr[i] <= x)  
        i = i*2;
mcqs.explanation: In exponential search we first find the range where the element being searched can be present before applying binary search. We do this by comparing the value of element under search with the array elements present at the positions 1,2,4,8….n.

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity of exponential sort?
mcqs.explanation: In exponential search, we first find a range where the required elements should be present in the array. Then we apply binary search in this range. This takes O(log n) time in the worst case.

mcqs.question: What is the auxiliary space requirement of an exponential sort when used with iterative binary search?
mcqs.explanation: Exponential search does not require any auxiliary space for finding the element being searched. So it has a constant auxiliary space O(1).

mcqs.question: What is the auxiliary space requirement of the exponential sort when used with recursive binary search?
mcqs.explanation: Exponential search requires an auxiliary space of log n when used with recursive binary search. This space is required for the recursion call stack space.

mcqs.question: Which of the following searching algorithm is fastest?
mcqs.explanation: Exponential search has the least time complexity (equal to log n) out of the given searching algorithms. This makes exponential search preferable in most cases.

mcqs.question: In which of the following case jump search will be preferred over exponential search?

options.a: a) jumping backwards takes significantly more time than jumping forward
options.b: b) jumping forward takes significantly more time than jumping backwards
options.c: c) when the given array is very large in size
options.d: d) when the given array is very small in size

mcqs.answer: a) jumping backwards takes significantly more time than jumping forward
mcqs.explanation: Jump search only needs to jump backwards once, while an exponential search can jump backwards up to log n times. Thus jump search will be preferred if jumping backwards is expensive.

mcqs.question: Best case of the exponential search will have time complexity of?
mcqs.explanation: Best case of the exponential search will be when the first element of the array is the element that is being searched. In this case, only one comparison will be required. Thus it will have a time complexity of O(1).

mcqs.question: Jump search has a better time complexity than the exponential search.

mcqs.question: Exponential search performs better than binary search when the element being searched is present near the starting point of the array.
mcqs.explanation: Exponential search first finds the range where binary search needs to be applied. So when the element is present near the starting point of the array then exponential search performs better than standard binary search.

mcqs.question: Choose the incorrect statement about exponential search from the following.

options.a: a) Exponential search is an in place algorithm
options.b: b) Exponential search has a greater time complexity than binary search
options.c: c) Exponential search performs better than binary search when the element being searched is present near the starting point of the array
options.d: d) Jump search has a greater time complexity than an exponential search

mcqs.answer: b) Exponential search has a greater time complexity than binary search
mcqs.explanation: Time complexity of exponential search and binary search are the same. But exponential search performs better than binary search when the element being searched is present near the starting point of the array.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an alternate name of exponential search?
mcqs.explanation: Logarithmic search is not an alternate name of the exponential search. Some alternate names of exponential search are Doubling search, Galloping search and Struzik search.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Interpolation Searching Algorithm”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most desirable condition for interpolation search?

options.b: b) array should not be sorted but the values should be uniformly distributed
options.c: c) array should have a less than 64 elements
options.d: d) array should be sorted and the values should be uniformly distributed

mcqs.answer: d) array should be sorted and the values should be uniformly distributed
mcqs.explanation: Desirable condition for interpolation search is that the array should be sorted and the values should be uniformly distributed. The algorithm would fail to give the correct result if array is not sorted.

mcqs.question: Interpolation search is a variation of?
mcqs.explanation: Interpolation search is a variation of binary search which gives the best result when the array has uniformly distributed values. Interpolation search goes to different positions depending on the value being searched whereas binary search always goes to the middle element.

mcqs.question: Interpolation search performs better than binary search when?

options.a: a) array has uniformly distributed values but is not sorted
options.b: b) array is sorted and has uniform distribution of values
options.c: c) array is sorted but the values are not uniformly distributed

mcqs.answer: b) array is sorted and has uniform distribution of values
mcqs.explanation: Interpolation search is an improvement over a binary search for the case when array is sorted and has uniformly distributed values. Binary search performs better when the values are not distributed uniformly.

mcqs.question: In which of the following case jump search performs better than interpolation search?

options.a: a) When array has uniformly distributed values but is not sorted
options.b: b) when array is sorted and has uniform distribution of values
options.c: c) when array is sorted but the values increases exponentially
options.d: d) when array is not sorted

mcqs.answer: c) when array is sorted but the values increases exponentially
mcqs.explanation: In case of non uniform distribution of values the time complexity of interpolation search is O(n) whereas the average time complexity of jump search is O(n<sup>1/2</sup>). So in such a case jump search has a better performance.

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity of interpolation search when the input array has uniformly distributed values and is sorted?
mcqs.explanation: Interpolation search goes to different positions in the array depending on the value being searched. It is an improvement over binary search and has a time complexity of O(log log n).

mcqs.question: What is the auxiliary space requirement of interpolation search?
mcqs.explanation: Interpolation search does not require any auxiliary space for finding the element being searched. So it has a constant auxiliary space O(1).

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity of exponential search when the input array is sorted but the values are not uniformly distributed?
mcqs.explanation: When an array has non uniformly distributed values then in that case the algorithm of interpolation search fails to work efficiently. As a result, it has a time complexity of O(n) in such a case.

mcqs.question: Which of the following searching algorithm is fastest when the input array is sorted and has uniformly distributed values?
mcqs.explanation: Interpolation search has a time complexity of O( log log n) when the array is sorted and has uniformly distributed values. It has the least time complexity out of the given options for such a case.

mcqs.question: Which of the following searching algorithm is fastest when the input array is sorted but has non uniformly distributed values?
mcqs.explanation: Interpolation search has a time complexity of O(n) when the array does not have uniformly distributed values. So in such a case binary search has the least time complexity out of the given options.

mcqs.question: Which of the following searching algorithm is fastest when the input array is not sorted but has uniformly distributed values?
mcqs.explanation: Out of the given options linear search is the only searching algorithm which can be applied to arrays which are not sorted. It has a time complexity of O(n) in the worst case.

mcqs.question: Interpolation search is an in place algorithm.
mcqs.explanation: Interpolation search has an auxiliary space complexity of O(1). So it qualifies as an in place algorithm.

mcqs.question: Interpolation search has a better time complexity than exponential search for any given array.
mcqs.explanation: The worst case time complexity of interpolation search and exponential search are O(n) and O(log n) respectively. So exponential search is better when the worst case scenario is considered.

mcqs.question: What is the formula used for calculating the position in interpolation search? (x = element being searched, A[] = input array, low and high are the leftmost and rightmost index of A[] respectively)
mcqs.explanation: For calculating the position after each iteration in interpolation search we use the formula low + ((x – A[low]) * (high – low)) / (A[high] – A[low]). Then the value at the calculated position is compared with the element being searched.

mcqs.question: What are the updated values of high and low in the array if the element being searched is greater than the value at calculated index in interpolation search? (pos = current position)

options.a: a) low = pos + 1, high remains unchanged
options.b: b) high = pos – 1, low remains unchanged

mcqs.answer: a) low = pos + 1, high remains unchanged
mcqs.explanation: When the element being searched is greater than the value at the calculated position then in that case we update low and high remains unaltered. Updated value of low is low = pos + 1.

mcqs.question: What are the updated values of high and low in the array if the element being searched is lower than the value at calculated index in interpolation search? (pos = current position)

options.a: a) low = pos + 1, high remains unchanged
options.b: b) high = pos – 1, low remains unchanged

mcqs.answer: b) high = pos – 1, low remains unchanged
mcqs.explanation: When the element being searched is lower than the value at the calculated position then in that case we update high and low remains unaltered. Updated value of high is high = pos – 1.

mcqs.question: Rabin Karp algorithm and naive pattern searching algorithm have the same worst case time complexity.

links.context: This set of Data Structure Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Sorting”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithms is the fastest for sorting small arrays?
mcqs.explanation: For sorting small arrays, insertion sort runs even faster than quick sort. But, it is impractical to sort large arrays.

mcqs.question: What is the advantage of selection sort over other sorting techniques?

options.a: a) It is faster than any other sorting technique
options.c: c) It works best for inputs which are already sorted
options.d: d) It requires no additional storage space

mcqs.answer: d) It requires no additional storage space
mcqs.explanation: Since selection sort is an in-place sorting algorithm, it does not require additional storage.

mcqs.question: Which of the following method is used for sorting in merge sort?
mcqs.explanation: Merge sort algorithm divides the array into two halves and applies merge sort algorithm to each half individually after which the two sorted halves are merged together. Thus its method of sorting is called merging.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithm does not use recursion?
mcqs.explanation: Bottom up merge sort uses the iterative method in order to implement sorting. It begins by merging a pair of adjacent array of size 1 each and then merge arrays of size 2 each in the next step and so on.

mcqs.question: Merge sort uses which of the following method to implement sorting?
mcqs.explanation: Merge sort implements sorting by merging the sorted versions of smaller parts of the array. Thus its method of sorting is called merging.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithms is the fastest?
mcqs.explanation: Quick sort is the fastest known sorting algorithm because of its highly optimized inner loop.

mcqs.question: Shell sort algorithm is an example of?
mcqs.explanation: Shell sort is an example of internal sorting because sorting of elements is done internally using an array.

mcqs.question: Quick sort uses which of the following method to implement sorting?
mcqs.explanation: Quick sort makes partitions of the input array about the pivot in order to implement sorting. Thus its method of sorting is called partitioning.

mcqs.question: In heap sort, after deleting the last minimum element, the array will contain elements in?
mcqs.explanation: By logic, after deleting minimum element, the heap will contain elements in decreasing sorting order. We can change this by altering the ordering property.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithm is used by C++ internally?
mcqs.explanation: Introsort is the in built sorting algorithm used by C++. It is an example of a hybrid sorting algorithm which means it uses more than one sorting algorithm as a routine.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithm is stable?
mcqs.explanation: Out of the given options Tim sort is the only algorithm which is stable. As both constituents of Tim sort (I.e insertion sort and merge sort) are stable so Tim sort also becomes stable.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithm uses the method of insertion?
mcqs.explanation: Cycle sort is the only algorithm from the given ones that uses the method of insertion. Other than this, insertion sort also uses the method of insertion for sorting.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pair of sorting algorithms are stable?

options.a: a) gnome sort and merge sort
options.b: b) heap sort and merge sort
options.c: c) gnome sort and quick sort
options.d: d) merge sort and selection sort

mcqs.answer: a) gnome sort and merge sort
mcqs.explanation: Gnome sort and merge sort are stable sorting algorithms as the elements with identical values appear in the same order in the output array as they were in the input array when any of these sorting algorithms are implemented.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Insertion Sort”.

mcqs.question: How many passes does an insertion sort algorithm consist of?
mcqs.explanation: An insertion algorithm consists of N-1 passes when an array of N elements is given.

mcqs.question: Which of the following algorithm implementations is similar to that of an insertion sort?
mcqs.explanation: Insertion sort is similar to that of a binary heap algorithm because of the use of temporary variable to swap.

mcqs.question: What is the average case running time of an insertion sort algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: The average case analysis of a tight bound algorithm is mathematically achieved to be O(N<sup>2</sup>).

mcqs.question: Any algorithm that sorts by exchanging adjacent elements require O(N<sup>2</sup>) on average.
mcqs.explanation: Each swap removes only one inversion, so O(N<sup>2</sup>) swaps are required.

mcqs.question: What is the average number of inversions in an array of N distinct numbers?
mcqs.explanation: The total number of pairs in a list L is N(N-1)/2. Thus, an average list has half this amount, or N(N-1)/4 inversions.

mcqs.question: What is the running time of an insertion sort algorithm if the input is pre-sorted?
mcqs.explanation: If the input is pre-sorted, the running time is O(N), because the test in the inner for loop always fails immediately and the algorithm will run quickly.

mcqs.question: What will be the number of passes to sort the elements using insertion sort? 14, 12,16, 6, 3, 10
mcqs.explanation:
The number of passes is given by N-1. Here, N=6. Therefore,
6-1=5 passes.

mcqs.question: For the following question, how will the array elements look like after second pass? 34, 8, 64, 51, 32, 21
mcqs.explanation: After swapping elements in the second pass, the array will look like, 8, 34, 64, 51, 32, 21.

mcqs.question: Which of the following real time examples is based on insertion sort?

options.b: b) database scenarios and distributes scenarios
options.c: c) arranging books on a library shelf

mcqs.answer: a) arranging a pack of playing cards
mcqs.explanation: Arranging a pack of cards mimics an insertion sort. Database scenario is an example for merge sort, arranging books is a stack and real-time systems uses quick sort.

mcqs.question: In C, what are the basic loops required to perform an insertion sort?
mcqs.explanation: To perform an insertion sort, we use two basic loops- an outer for loop and an inner while loop.

mcqs.question: Binary search can be used in an insertion sort algorithm to reduce the number of comparisons.
mcqs.explanation: Binary search can be used in an insertion sort algorithm to reduce the number of comparisons. This is called a Binary insertion sort.

mcqs.question: Which of the following options contain the correct feature of an insertion sort algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: An insertion sort is stable, adaptive, in-place and incremental in nature.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithms is the fastest for sorting small arrays?
mcqs.explanation: For sorting small arrays, insertion sort runs even faster than quick sort. But, it is impractical to sort large arrays.

mcqs.question: For the best case input, the running time of an insertion sort algorithm is?
mcqs.explanation: The best case input for an insertion sort algorithm runs in linear time and is given by O(N).

mcqs.question: Which of the following examples represent the worst case input for an insertion sort?

mcqs.answer: b) array sorted in reverse order
mcqs.explanation: The worst case input for an insertion sort algorithm will be an array sorted in reverse order and its running time is quadratic.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is correct with regard to insertion sort?

options.a: a) insertion sort is stable and it sorts In-place
options.b: b) insertion sort is unstable and it sorts In-place
options.c: c) insertion sort is stable and it does not sort In-place
options.d: d) insertion sort is unstable and it does not sort In-place

mcqs.answer: a) insertion sort is stable and it sorts In-place
mcqs.explanation: During insertion sort, the relative order of elements is not changed. Therefore, it is a stable sorting algorithm. And insertion sort requires only O(1) of additional memory space. Therefore, it sorts In-place.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithm is best suited if the elements are already sorted?
mcqs.explanation: The best case running time of the insertion sort is O(n). The best case occurs when the input array is already sorted. As the elements are already sorted, only one comparison is made on each pass, so that the time required is O(n).

mcqs.question: The worst case time complexity of insertion sort is O(n<sup>2</sup>). What will be the worst case time complexity of insertion sort if the correct position for inserting element is calculated using binary search?
mcqs.explanation: The use of binary search reduces the time of finding the correct position from O(n) to O(logn). But the worst case of insertion sort remains O(n<sup>2</sup>) because of the series of swapping operations required for each insertion.

mcqs.question: Insertion sort is an example of an incremental algorithm.
mcqs.explanation: In the incremental algorithms, the complicated structure on n items is built by first building it on n − 1 items. And then we make the necessary changes to fix things in adding the last item. Insertion sort builds the sorted sequence one element at a time. Therefore, it is an example of an incremental algorithm.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is good for sorting arrays having less than 100 elements?
mcqs.explanation: The insertion sort is good for sorting small arrays. It sorts smaller arrays faster than any other sorting algorithm.

mcqs.question: Consider an array of length 5, arr[5] = {9,7,4,2,1}. What are the steps of insertions done while running insertion sort on the array?

mcqs.question: Statement 1: In insertion sort, after m passes through the array, the first m elements are in sorted order. Statement 2: And these elements are the m smallest elements in the array.

options.a: a) Both the statements are true
options.b: b) Statement 1 is true but statement 2 is false
options.c: c) Statement 1 is false but statement 2 is true
options.d: d) Both the statements are false

mcqs.answer: b) Statement 1 is true but statement 2 is false
mcqs.explanation: In insertion sort, after m passes through the array, the first m elements are in sorted order but they are whatever the first m elements were in the unsorted array.

mcqs.question: In insertion sort, the average number of comparisons required to place the 7<sup>th</sup> element into its correct position is ____
mcqs.explanation: On average (k + 1) / 2 comparisons are required to place the k<sup>th</sup> element into its correct position. Therefore, average number of comparisons required for 7th element = (7 + 1)/2 = 4.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an exchange sort?
mcqs.explanation: In Exchange sorts, we compare each element of an array and swap those elements that are not in their proper position. Bubble Sort and Quick Sort are exchange sorts. Quick Sort is also called as Partition-exchange Sort. Insertion sort is not an exchange sort.

mcqs.question: A machine needs a minimum of 200 sec to sort 1000 elements by Quick sort. The minimum time needed to sort 200 elements will be approximately __________
mcqs.explanation: The Quick sort requires nlog2n comparisons in best case, where n is size of input array. So, 1000 * log21000 ≈ 9000 comparisons are required to sort 1000 elements, which takes 200 sec. To sort 200 elements minimum of 200 * log2200 ≈ 1400 comparisons are required. This will take 200 * 1400 / 9000 ≈ 31.11 sec.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following sorting algorithm is best suited to sort an array of 1 million elements?

mcqs.question: What is the typical running time of a heap sort algorithm?

mcqs.question: How many arrays are required to perform deletion operation in a heap?

mcqs.question: How many elements can be sorted in O(logn) time using Heap sort?
mcqs.explanation:
The time complexity of Heap sort is O(klogk) for k input elements,
for k = logn/log(logn),
O(klogk) = O(logn/log(logn) * log(logn/log(logn)))
∴ O(klogk) = O(logn/log(logn) * (log(logn) – log(log(logn))))
= O(logn)
Hence the correct option is O(logn/log(logn)).

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithm is used by C++ internally?
mcqs.explanation: Introsort is the in built sorting algorithm used by C++. It is an example of a hybrid sorting algorithm which means it uses more than one sorting algorithm as a routine.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithm is not a constituent of introsort?
mcqs.explanation: Introsort is a hybrid sorting algorithm which means it uses more than one sorting algorithm as a routine. It may use quick sort or heap sort or insertion sort depending on the given situation.

mcqs.question: Introsort begins sorting the given array by using which of the following sorting algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: Introsort begins sorting any given array by using quick sort. Then it may switch to heap sort or insertion sort or may stick to quick sort depending upon the size of the partition.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithm is NOT stable?
mcqs.explanation: Out of the given options introsort is the only algorithm which is not stable. As it may use quick sort in some case to perform sorting which is itself not stable. Thus stability of introsort is not guaranteed.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithm is in-place?
mcqs.explanation: Introsort may use quick sort or heap sort or insertion sort internally in order to sort the given input. All of the three algorithms are in place, thus making introsort to be an in-place sorting algorithm.

mcqs.question: Introsort sort is a comparison based sort.
mcqs.explanation: Quicksort, heap sort and insertion sort are comparison based sorts. Thus overall introsort also becomes a comparison based sort.

mcqs.question: What is the best case time complexity of introsort?
mcqs.explanation: Introsort is mainly governed by heap sort and quick sort. As the best case of both heap sort and quick sort is O(n log n) so the best case of introsort also becomes O(n log n).

mcqs.question: What is the worst case time complexity of introsort?
mcqs.explanation: Worst case time complexity of quicksort is avoided when we implement introsort. Introsort switches to heap sort when there is a possibility of crossing the maximum depth limit.

mcqs.question: What is the average time complexity of introsort?
mcqs.explanation: Average time complexity of introsort remains to be O(n log n) as for most of the cases quick sort and heap sort are used which have O(n log n) time complexity for an average case.

mcqs.question: What is the auxiliary space requirement of introsort?
mcqs.explanation: Introsort is a hybrid of quick sort, heap sort and insertion sort. So like quick sort it may use O(log n) auxiliary space in the stack to store call statements.

mcqs.question: Why is heap sort preferred over merge sort for introsort implementation?

options.a: a) Because heap sort is faster
options.b: b) Because heap sort requires less space
options.c: c) Because heap sort is easy to implement
options.d: d) Because heap sort is easy to understand

mcqs.answer: b) Because heap sort requires less space
mcqs.explanation: Both heap sort and merge sort have the same time complexity. But heap sort is an in-place sorting algorithm whereas merge sort requires O(n) auxiliary space which makes heap sort a more preferable option.

mcqs.question: Why is insertion sort preferred over other sorting algorithms (like selection sort, bubble sort etc.) for introsort implementation?

options.a: a) Because insertion sort is faster and adaptive
options.b: b) Because insertion sort requires less space
options.c: c) Because insertion sort is easy to implement
options.d: d) Because insertion sort is easy to understand

mcqs.answer: a) Because insertion sort is faster and adaptive
mcqs.explanation: When small arrays need to be sorted then insertion sort proves to be the best choice. Also it is adaptive so it performs better than others when the given array is fully/partially sorted.

mcqs.question: What is the cut-off for switching from quick sort to insertion sort in the implementation of introsort?

mcqs.question: What is the cut-off for switching from quick sort to heap sort in the implementation of introsort?
mcqs.explanation: Quicksort has a worst case time complexity of O(n<sup>2</sup>) which is not preferable. So in order to avoid worst case of quicksort, introsort switches to heap sort when the depth is greater than 2 log(n). This particular value has been deduced experimentally.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithm will be preferred when the size of partition is between 16 and 2 log(n) while implementing introsort?
mcqs.explanation: Quicksort proves to be the best sorting algorithm for mid sized arrays as it has low space and time complexity. Thus quick sort is preferred when size of partition is between 16 and 2 log(n).

mcqs.question: Which of the following is Python’s standard sorting algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: Tim sort has been python’s standard sorting algorithm since its version 2.3. It is an example of hybrid sorting algorithm which means it uses more than one sorting algorithm as a routine.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithm is a constituent of tim sort?
mcqs.explanation: Tim sort is a hybrid sorting algorithm which means it uses more than one sorting algorithm as a routine. It is derived from insertion sort and merge sort.

mcqs.question: Tim sort begins sorting the given array by using which of the following sorting algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: Tim sort begins sorting any given array by using insertion sort for each run. The array is divided into smaller parts for this purpose, each part having a size equal to value of run. Then these small parts called runs are merged in order to obtain sorted array.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithm is stable?
mcqs.explanation: Out of the given options Tim sort is the only algorithm which is stable. As both constituents of Tim sort (I.e insertion sort and merge sort) are stable so Tim sort also becomes stable.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithm is not in-place?
mcqs.explanation: Tim sort is not an in-place sorting algorithm as it requires auxiliary space. It is because it requires to merge sorted runs which requires a third array of the size equal to the sum of the two runs.

mcqs.question: Tim sort is a comparison based sort.
mcqs.explanation: Merge sort and insertion sort are comparison based sorts. Thus overall Tim sort also becomes a comparison based sort.

mcqs.question: What is the best case time complexity of Tim sort?
mcqs.explanation: Best case time complexity of Tim sort occurs when the input array is already sorted. In such a case only one run will be required.

mcqs.question: What is the worst case time complexity of Tim sort?
mcqs.explanation: Worst case time complexity of Tim sort is O(n log n). It is because the worst complexity of merge sort is O(n log n) and insertion sort is only applied for small arrays.

mcqs.question: What is the average time complexity of Tim sort?
mcqs.explanation: Average time complexity of Tim sort remains to be O(n log n). It is the same as the average case complexity of merge sort.

mcqs.question: What is the auxiliary space requirement of Tim sort?
mcqs.explanation: Tim sort is a hybrid of merge sort and insertion sort. It requires to merge sorted runs which require a third array of the size equal to the sum of the two runs. So in worst case the auxiliary space requirement will be O(n).

mcqs.question: Which of the following algorithm is implemented internally in java when we use function arrays.sort()?

options.b: b) Because insertion sort requires less space

options.c: c) when no. of elements are less than size of run
options.d: d) when no. of elements are less than 32

mcqs.answer: c) when no. of elements are less than size of run
mcqs.explanation: Tim sort uses a hybrid of insertion and merge sort. It reduces to insertion sort when the size of array is less than the size of run as insertion sort is efficient in sorting small arrays.

mcqs.question: What is the usual size of a run in tim sort?

options.c: c) 32-64 depending on size of the array

mcqs.answer: c) 32-64 depending on size of the array
mcqs.explanation: Usually the size of the run is chosen somewhere between 32 and 64. The size of run is preferably chosen in powers of 2 in order to maintain balance while merging the sorted runs.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithm is in-place?

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an advantage of cycle sort?

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a disadvantage of library sort when compared to insertion sort?

options.a: a) library sort has greater time complexity
options.b: b) library sort has greater space complexity
options.c: c) library sort makes more comparisons
options.d: d) it has no significant disadvantage

mcqs.answer: b) library sort has greater space complexity
mcqs.explanation: Library sort has a disadvantage that it takes up O(n) auxiliary space whereas insertion sort takes constant auxiliary space.

mcqs.question: Library sort is an online sorting algorithm.
mcqs.explanation: Library sort does not require the entire input data at the beginning itself in order to sort the array. It rather creates a partial solution in every step, so future elements are not required to be considered. Hence it is an online sorting algorithm like insertion sort.

mcqs.question: Library sort is a modified version of which of the following sorting algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: Library sort requires the use of Insertion sort and binary search in its code. So it is a modified version of insertion sort.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithm is stable?

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithm requires the use of binary search in their implementation?
mcqs.explanation: Library sort makes use of a binary search algorithm. It is used to find the correct index in the array where the element should be inserted. Then after the insertion of the element re-balancing of the array takes place.

mcqs.question: Library sort is a comparison based sort.
mcqs.explanation: In library sort, we need to compare elements in order to insert them at the correct index. So we can say that it uses comparisons in order to sort the array. Thus it qualifies as a comparison based sort.

mcqs.question: What is the average case time complexity of library sort?

mcqs.question: What is the best case time complexity of library sort?
mcqs.explanation: The best case time complexity of library sort is O(n). It occurs in the case when the input is already/almost sorted.

mcqs.question: What is the worst case time complexity of library sort?

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an alternate name of library sort?

mcqs.question: What is the advantage of library sort over insertion sort?

options.b: b) Library sort has a better space complexity

options.d: d) Library has better worst case time complexity

mcqs.answer: a) Library sort has a better average time complexity
mcqs.explanation: Library sort has a better average time complexity as compared to insertion sort because it uses binary search for finding the index where the element has to be inserted in the sorted array. This makes the process faster.

mcqs.question: What is the auxiliary space complexity of library sort?
mcqs.explanation: The auxiliary space required by library sort is O(n). This space is taken up by the gaps present in between successive elements.

mcqs.answer: d) it is an in place sorting algorithm

mcqs.explanation: The best case of strand sort occurs when the input array is already sorted. In this case, it has linear time complexity.

mcqs.question: What is the auxiliary space complexity of strand sort?
mcqs.explanation: The auxiliary space complexity of strand sort is O(n). It is because a sub-list of size n has to be maintained.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithm is not in place?
mcqs.explanation: Strand sort has an auxiliary space complexity of O(n). So it is not an in place sorting algorithm.

mcqs.question: Strand sort is a comparison based sorting algorithm.
mcqs.explanation: Pigeonhole sort is an example of a comparison based sorting algorithm. This is because it compares the value of elements present in a list in order to sort them.

mcqs.question: Strand sort is a stable sorting algorithm.
mcqs.explanation: Strand sort is an example of a stable sorting algorithm. It is because the elements with identical values appear in the same order in the output array as they were in the input array.

mcqs.question: What is the average time complexity of strand sort?
mcqs.explanation: Average case time complexity of strand sort is O(n2). So it is not as efficient as quick sort or merge sort.

mcqs.question: What is the best case time complexity of strand sort?
mcqs.explanation: Best case time complexity of strand sort is O(n). It occurs in the case where the input array is already sorted.

mcqs.question: What is the worst case time complexity of strand sort?
mcqs.explanation: Worst case time complexity of strand sort is O(n<sup>2</sup>). It occurs in the case where the input array is in reverse sorted order.

mcqs.question: Strand sort algorithm used which of the following method for sorting a list?
mcqs.explanation: Strand sort uses the method of selection for sorting any given list. This is because it selects the strands of elements from the input list which are sorted.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an adaptive sorting algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: Strand sort is an adaptive sorting algorithm. This is because it gives a better performance when the input list is almost sorted.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Comb Sort”.

mcqs.question: Comb sort is an improved version of _______
mcqs.explanation: Comb sort compares two elements at a variable gap from each other in each iteration unlike bubble sort where the gap remains 1. This reduces the average time complexity of comb sort.

mcqs.question: The gap between two elements being compared shrinks by a factor of _______ after every iteration.
mcqs.explanation: It has been found experimentally that the gap between the two elements should shrink by a factor of 1.3 after each iteration for the most efficient sorting.

mcqs.question: The initial gap between two elements being compared _______

options.a: a) is equal to number of elements in the array
options.c: c) depends on the number of iterations
options.d: d) depends on the compiler being used

mcqs.answer: a) is equal to number of elements in the array
mcqs.explanation: Initial gap is taken to be equal to the number of elements in the array and shrinks by a factor of 1.3 in each iteration, initial gap is independent of the number of iterations and compiler being used.

mcqs.question: What is the worst case time complexity of comb sort?
mcqs.explanation: Worst case complexity is observed when the input array is reverse sorted. This is same as the worst case complexity of bubble sort.

mcqs.question: The gap value after 3 iterations in an array with 6 elements will be _______
mcqs.explanation: Initially the gap value will be 6. For the first iteration, it will be 6/1.3=4 then 4/1.3=3 for second iteration and 3/1.3=2 for the third iteration.

mcqs.question: Auxiliary space used by comb sort is _______
mcqs.explanation: Auxiliary space used by comb sort is O(1) as it does not use any extra space for manipulating the input.

mcqs.question: The given array is arr={7,4,5,8,1,2}. The number of iterations required to sort the array using comb sort and bubble sort respectively will be _______
mcqs.explanation: Comb sort takes 1 iteration less as compared to bubble sort as it makes use of variable gap value whereas bubble sort uses a constant gap value of 1.

mcqs.question: Comb sort is a stable sorting algorithm.
mcqs.explanation: Comb sort is not a stable sorting algorithm as it does not sort the repeated elements in the same order as they appear in the input.

mcqs.question: What is the best case time complexity of comb sort and bubble sort respectively?

options.a: a) O(n<sup>2</sup>) and O(n log n)
options.b: b) O(n log n) and O(n)
options.d: d) O(n<sup>2</sup>/2<sup>a</sup>) (a=number of increment) and O(n<sup>2</sup>)

mcqs.answer: b) O(n log n) and O(n)
mcqs.explanation: Best case complexity for comb sort and bubble sort is O(n log n) and O(n) respectively. It occurs when the input array is already sorted.

mcqs.question: What is the advantage of comb sort over merge sort?

options.a: a) Comb sort is an in place sorting algorithm
options.b: b) Comb sort is a stable sorting algorithm
options.c: c) Comb sort is more efficient

mcqs.answer: a) Comb sort is an in place sorting algorithm
mcqs.explanation: Comb sort does not require auxiliary space for manipulating input so it is an in place sorting algorithm but merge sort does require O(n) of auxiliary space which makes comb sort better in terms of space complexity.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Gnome Sort”.

mcqs.question: Gnome sort is also called __________
mcqs.explanation: Gnome sort was originally named as stupid sort but later on it got renamed as gnome sort.

mcqs.question: How many loops are required to implement gnome sorting algorithm?

options.d: d) It does not require any loop

mcqs.explanation: In this sorting algorithm the variable representing the index number is not incremented in case the adjacent pair of elements are out of place. In such a case its value is decremented instead. Thus it is able to implement sorting using a single loop.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pair of sorting algorithms are stable?

options.a: a) gnome sort and quick sort
options.b: b) merge sort and selection sort
options.c: c) gnome sort and merge sort
options.d: d) heap sort and merge sort

mcqs.answer: c) gnome sort and merge sort
mcqs.explanation: Gnome sort and merge sort are stable sorting algorithms as the elements with identical values appear in the same order in the output array as they were in the input array when any of these sorting algorithms are implemented.

mcqs.question: Auxiliary space used by gnome sort is _________
mcqs.explanation: Auxiliary space used by gnome sort is O(1) as it does not use any extra space for manipulating the input. Thus it also qualifies as an in place sorting algorithm.

mcqs.question: The given array is arr = {1,2,4,3,5}.The number of iterations required to sort the array using gnome sort will be _________
mcqs.explanation: 6 iterations will be required as one pair of elements i.e. {4,3} is out of place which causes the loop to take one step backward.

mcqs.question: Gnome sort uses which of the following method to implement sorting?
mcqs.explanation: Gnome sort implements sorting by exchanging the adjacent elements which are out of order. Thus its method of sorting is called exchanging.

mcqs.question: What is the best case time complexity of gnome sort?
mcqs.explanation: When the input array is already sorted then in that case there will be no need to decrease the value of the index variable at any stage. So only O(n) time is required in this case as we keep on increasing its value after each iteration.

mcqs.question: What is the worst case time complexity of gnome sort?
mcqs.explanation: Worst case occurs when the input array is reverse sorted as it will have the maximum number of decrements while sorting. This causes the algorithm to have a time complexity of O(n<sup>2</sup>) in this case.

mcqs.question: What is the average case time complexity of gnome sort?
mcqs.explanation: In gnome sort the loop has to take one step backwards every time any adjacent pair of elements is out of place which causes it to have time complexity of O(n<sup>2</sup>) on an average.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Bogosort”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an alternative name of bogosort?
mcqs.explanation: Bogosort is also known by names like stupid sort, monkey sort, permutation sort, slow sort and shotgun sort.These names are particularly chosen due to its inefficient algorithm.

mcqs.question: Bogosort works by __________

options.a: a) generating random permutations of its input
options.c: c) dividing the value of input elements
options.d: d) generating permutations according to the value of first element of array

mcqs.answer: a) generating random permutations of its input
mcqs.explanation: Bogosort algorithm successively generates permutations of its input. This process is repeated until the sorted version of the array is found.

mcqs.question: What is the auxiliary space requirement of bogosort?
mcqs.explanation: Bogosort algorithm do not require any extra space for sorting the input array. Thus its auxiliary space requirement is O(1).

mcqs.question: What is the best case time complexity of bogosort?
mcqs.explanation: Best case time complexity of bogosort occurs when the input array is already sorted. So in such a case we only need to check whether all the elements are sorted which can be done in O(n) time.

mcqs.question: What is the worst case time complexity of bogosort?
mcqs.explanation: There is no upper bound to the worst case of this algorithm. It can go on to take very large amount of time if the array has many elements. So the worst case of this algorithm can be taken as O(infinity).

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithm is not stable __________
mcqs.explanation: Out of the given algorithms only bogosort is not stable. This is because it creates permutations of the input array in order to obtain the sorted version. So there is no guarantee that the sorted version obtained by such a method gives a stable output.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an in-place sorting algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: Out of the given algorithms only bogosort is an in-place sorting algorithm. It is because bogosort algorithm do not require any extra space for sorting the input array.

mcqs.question: Sleep sort should be preferred over bogosort as it has better time complexity.
mcqs.explanation: If we sort an array using sleep sort then there is no guarantee that the output we get is correctly sorted. So even though sleep sort is better than bogosort in time complexity but it cannot be preferred due to its inaccuracy.

mcqs.question: What is the average case time complexity of bogosort?
mcqs.explanation: For calculating the average we first need to calculate the number of possible permutations an array of size n can have. This will be equal to n!. As each permutation also needs to be checked whether it is sorted or not so this takes another n time. Thus overall time complexity becomes O(n*n!).

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Sleep Sort”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following header file is a must to implement sleep sort algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: To implement sleep sort algorithm we need functions like WaitForMultipleObjects(), _beginthread(). These are included in the header file windows.h.

mcqs.question: Sleep sort does not work for ___________
mcqs.explanation: Sleep sort algorithm does not work for negative numbers. It is because thread cannot sleep for negative amount of time.

mcqs.question: In how many comparisons does the array arr={1,4,2,3,5} gets sorted if we use sleep sort?
mcqs.explanation: Sleep sort makes different elements of the array to sleep for an amount of time that is proportional to its magnitude. So it does not require to perform any comparison in order to sort the array.

mcqs.question: Sleep sort works by ___________

options.a: a) making elements to sleep for a time that is proportional to their magnitude
options.b: b) making elements to sleep for a time that is inversely proportional to their magnitude
options.d: d) dividing the value of input elements

mcqs.answer: a) making elements to sleep for a time that is proportional to their magnitude
mcqs.explanation: In sleep sort each element is made to sleep for a time that is proportional to its magnitude. Then the elements are printed in the order in which they wake up.

mcqs.question: Sleep sort code cannot compile online because ___________

options.a: a) it has very high time complexity
options.b: b) it has very high space complexity
options.d: d) online compilers are not efficient

mcqs.explanation: Sleep sort requires multithreading process for making the elements to sleep. This process happens in the background at the core of the OS and so cannot be compiled on an online compiler.

mcqs.question: Time complexity of sleep sort can be approximated to be ___________
mcqs.explanation: As the sleep() function creates multiple threads by using priority queue which takes n log n time for insertion. Also the output is obtained when all the elements wake up. This time is proportional to the max(input). So its time complexity is approximately O(n log n + max(input)).

mcqs.question: Sleep sort can be preferred over which of the following sorting algorithms for large number of input elements?

options.d: d) No sorting algorithm is preferred

mcqs.answer: d) No sorting algorithm is preferred
mcqs.explanation: Sleep sort is not preferred over any of the given sorting algorithms as sleep sort does not guarantee a correct output every time. So sleep sort is not a reliable sorting technique.

mcqs.question: Auxiliary space requirement of sleep sort is ___________
mcqs.explanation: All the major processes involved in sleep sort takes place internally in the OS. So it does not require any auxiliary space to sort the elements.

mcqs.question: Sleep sort does gives a correct output when ___________

options.a: a) any input element is negative
options.b: b) input array is reverse sorted
options.c: c) any input element is positive
options.d: d) when there is a very small number to the left of very large number

mcqs.answer: c) any input element is positive
mcqs.explanation: Sleep sort gives a sorted output when the array elements are positive. But when any other case than this occur out of the above given cases then we may not see a correct output. This makes sleep sort very unreliable sorting technique.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithm is most closely related to the OS?
mcqs.explanation: Sleep sort is most closely related to the operating system. It is because most of the major steps of this algorithm takes place at the core of OS.

mcqs.question: Sleep sort is an in-place sorting technique.
mcqs.explanation: Sleep sort is an in-place sorting technique as most of its major steps takes place in the background. So it does not require auxiliary space to sort the input.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Pigeonhole Sort”.

mcqs.question: How many comparisons will be made to sort the array arr={1,5,3,8,2} using pigeonhole sort?
mcqs.explanation: As pigeonhole sort is an example of a non-comparison sort so it is able to sort an array without making any comparison. So 0 comparisons are required.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a non-comparison sort?
mcqs.explanation: Heap sort, merge sort and quick sort are examples of comparison sort as it needs to compare array elements in order to sort an array. Whereas pigeonhole sort is a non-comparison based sort.

mcqs.question: In which of the following case pigeonhole sort is most efficient?

options.a: a) when range of input is less than number of elements
options.b: b) when range of input is more than number of elements
options.c: c) when range of input is comparable to the number of elements
options.d: d) when the given array is almost sorted

mcqs.answer: c) when range of input is comparable to the number of elements
mcqs.explanation: Pigeonhole sort is a non-comparison based sort. It is most efficient in the case where the number of elements are comparable to the input range.

mcqs.question: What is the space complexity of pigeonhole sort (k=range of input)?
mcqs.explanation: Pigeonhole sort algorithm requires two arrays. The first one is required to store the input elements so its size is n. The second one is the pigeonhole array and has a size equal to range k. Overall space complexity becomes O(n+k).

mcqs.question: The auxiliary array used in pigeonhole sorting is called ______________
mcqs.explanation: The auxiliary array used in pigeonhole sorting is called pigeonhole. It is used to store every element in its corresponding hole.

mcqs.question: Pigeonhole sort is a stable sorting algorithm.
mcqs.explanation: Pigeonhole sort is an example of a stable sorting algorithm. It is because the elements with identical values appear in the same order in the output array as they were in the input array.

mcqs.question: Pigeonhole sort is an in place sorting algorithm.
mcqs.explanation: Pigeonhole sort requires space of O(n+k). So it does not qualify to be an in place sorting algorithm.

mcqs.question: What is the average time complexity of pigeonhole sort (k=range of input)?
mcqs.explanation: Time complexity of pigeonhole sort is O(n+k). It has two loops. One of the loops runs from 0 to range(k) and the other one runs from 0 to n so the time complexity becomes O(n+k).

mcqs.question: The complexity of which of the following sorting algorithms remains to be the same in its best, average and worst case?
mcqs.explanation: The time complexity of pigeonhole remains unvaried in all three cases. It is given by O(n+k). But it is efficient only when the number of elements is comparable to the input range.

mcqs.question: Choose the correct statement from the following.

options.a: a) pigeonhole sort is a comparison based sort
options.b: b) any comparison based sorting can be made stable
options.c: c) quick sort is not a comparison based sort
options.d: d) any comparison based sort requires at least O(n<sup>2</sup>) time

mcqs.answer: b) any comparison based sorting can be made stable
mcqs.explanation: Any comparison based sorting technique can be made stable by considering the position as criteria while making comparisons. Pigeonhole sort is a stable sort.

mcqs.question: What is the advantage of pigeonhole sort over merge sort?

options.a: a) pigeonhole sort has lesser time complexity when range is comparable to number of input elements
options.b: b) pigeonhole sort has lesser space complexity
options.c: c) counting sort is not a comparison based sorting technique

mcqs.answer: a) pigeonhole sort has lesser time complexity when range is comparable to number of input elements
mcqs.explanation: Pigeonhole sort is efficient in the cases where the range is comparable to a number of input elements as it performs sorting in linear time. Whereas merge sort takes O(n log n) in any case.

mcqs.question: Which of the following algorithm takes linear time for sorting?
mcqs.explanation: Pigeonhole sort has a linear time complexity of O(n+k). Whereas all other given options have a non linear time complexity. But it should be noted that pigeonhole sort may not be efficient in every case.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “LSD Radix Sort”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the distribution sort?
mcqs.explanation: In Distribution sort the inputted values are distributed to multiple intermediate structures which are then combined and placed on the output. And LSD radix sort distributes values into buckets based on the digits within values, so it is a distribution sort.

mcqs.question: What is the worst case time complexity of LSD radix sort?
mcqs.explanation: Time complexity of LSD radix sort depends upon the word size and the number on items. It runs in O(wn) time in worst case, where n is the number of inputted elements and w is the number of digits in the largest number.

mcqs.question: LSD radix sort requires _____ passes to sort N elements.
mcqs.explanation: LSD radix sort sorts the N elements in  (w/logR) passes where w is the number of digits in largest number and R(radix) is extra space required for performing the sorting operation.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is false?

options.a: a) LSD radix sort is an integer sorting algorithm
options.b: b) LSD radix sort is a comparison sorting algorithm
options.c: c) LSD radix sort is a distribution sort
options.d: d) LSD radix sort uses bucket sort

mcqs.answer: b) LSD radix sort is a comparison sorting algorithm
mcqs.explanation: LSD radix sort uses bucket sort for grouping the keys based on the digits at that value. And as it grouped the keys based on the digits at that values, it is integer sorting algorithm.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithm is stable?
mcqs.explanation: In LSD radix sort after sorting the multiple elements with the same key will be in the same order as they were in the input array. So LSD radix sort is stable sort.

mcqs.question: LSD radix sort is faster than comparison sorts.
mcqs.explanation: LSD radix sort is faster than comparison sorts when the word size is less than logn. But LSD radix sort runs slowly for elements with larger word size and smaller radix.

mcqs.question: Which of the following should be used to sort a huge database on a fixed-length key field?
mcqs.explanation: LSD radix requires only w passes to sort a fixed-length string, where w is a length of the strings. So, LSD radix sort is best suited to sort a huge database on a fixed-length key field.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a combination of LSD and MSD radix sorts?
mcqs.explanation: Forward radix sort combines the advantages of LSD and MSD radix sort. Forward radix sort inspects a complete horizontal strip at a time just like LSD radix sort.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is true for the LSD radix sort?

options.a: a) works best for variable length strings
options.c: c) inner loop has less instructions
options.d: d) sorts the keys in left-to-right order

mcqs.explanation: LSD radix sort sorts the keys in right-to-left order, working with Least Significant Digit first. The inner loop has a lot of instructions and LSD radix sort is used to sort fixed-length strings.

mcqs.question: LSD radix sort is in-place sorting algorithm.
mcqs.explanation: LSD radix is not an in-place sorting algorithm. It needs extra memory to store the elements in bucket and its worst case space complexity is O(w + R).

mcqs.question: What is the full form of MSD in MSD radix sort?
mcqs.explanation: MSD stands for Most Significant Digit. It is named so because in this algorithm the processing begins from the most significant digit.

mcqs.question: Which of the following combines qualities of MSD radix sort and LSD radix sort?
mcqs.explanation: Forward radix sort combines the qualities of MSD and LSD radix sort. The sorting is done by separating the strings into groups.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most suitable definition of radix sort?

options.b: b) It is a comparison based integer sort

options.d: d) It is a comparison based non integer sort

mcqs.answer: a) It is a non comparison based integer sort
mcqs.explanation: Radix sort is a non-comparison based integer sort. It sorts the given data by grouping keys which share the same significant position value.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an alternate name of MSD radix sort?
mcqs.explanation: Top down radix sort is an alternate name of MSD radix sort. It is because in this algorithm the processing starts from the most significant digit and end at least significant digit.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true about MSD radix sort?

options.a: a) its processing starts from the most significant digit
options.b: b) it is not a stable sort

mcqs.answer: c) it is an in place sorting algorithm
mcqs.explanation: MSD radix sort takes non constant time for sorting the input data. So it is not an in place sorting algorithm.

mcqs.question: MSD radix sort should be preferred over LSD radix sort when we have to maintain the original relative order.
mcqs.explanation: MSD radix sort is not a stable sort whereas LSD radix sort is stable. So when we require to preserve the original order then in that case we should prefer LSD radix sort.

mcqs.question: What is the average time complexity of MSD radix sort (w= bits required to store each key)?
mcqs.explanation: Time complexity of radix sort is O(n.w). It performs better than quick sort when we have log n bits for every digit.

mcqs.question: MSD radix sort is an in place sorting algorithm.
mcqs.explanation: MSD radix sort takes non constant time for sorting the input data. So it is not an in place sorting algorithm.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statement is not a stable sorting algorithm?

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true about radix sort?

options.b: b) Radix sort has better cache performance than quick sort

mcqs.question: What is the advantage of radix sort over quick sort?

options.a: a) radix sort performs better than quick sort when we have log n bits for every digit

mcqs.answer: a) radix sort performs better than quick sort when we have log n bits for every digit

mcqs.question: What will be the order of elements of the array arr = {23, 67, 143, 654, 43} after first iteration of MSD sort is complete?

mcqs.explanation: As counting sort is an example of non comparison sort so it is able to sort an array without making any comparison.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an example of non comparison sort?
mcqs.explanation: Bubble sort is not an example of non comparison sort as it needs to compare array elements in order to sort an array.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting techniques is most efficient if the range of input data is not significantly greater than a number of elements to be sorted?
mcqs.explanation: Time complexity of counting sort is given as O(n+k) where n is the number of input elements and k is the range of input. So if range of input is not significantly larger than number of elements in the array then it proves to be very efficient.

mcqs.question: What is the auxiliary space requirement of counting sort?
mcqs.explanation: Counting sort uses two extra arrays to get the input array sorted. First array is required to store the count of all the elements which fall in the range of input data elements, so its size is k. The second array is required to store the input elements in sorted manner, so its size is n. Thus overall auxiliary space required becomes O(n+k).

mcqs.question: It is not possible to implement counting sort when any of the input element has negative value.
mcqs.explanation: It is possible to extend the counting sort algorithm for negative numbers as well. In such a case we store the minimum element at the 0th index.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting techniques is stable?
mcqs.explanation: Counting sort is an example of stable sorting algorithm as the elements with identical values appear in the same order in the output array as they were in the input array.

mcqs.question: Which of the following uses the largest amount of auxiliary space for sorting?
mcqs.explanation: Counting sort requires auxiliary space of O(n+k) whereas quick sort, bubble sort and heap sort are in place sorting techniques. Thus counting sort requires most auxiliary space.

mcqs.question: What is the average time complexity of counting sort?
mcqs.explanation: Time complexity of counting sort is O(n+k) as counting the occurrence of each element in the input range takes k time and then finding the correct index value of each element in the sorted array takes n time.

mcqs.question: The complexity of which of the following sorting algorithms remains to be the same in its best, average and worst case?
mcqs.explanation: The time complexity of counting sort remains unvaried in all the three cases. It is given by O(n+k).

mcqs.question: What is the disadvantage of counting sort?

mcqs.question: Which of the following algorithm takes non linear time for sorting?

mcqs.question: How many comparisons will be made to sort the array arr={1, 5, 3, 8, 2} using bucket sort?
mcqs.explanation: As bucket sort is an example of a non-comparison sort so it is able to sort an array without making any comparison. So the answer should be 0.

mcqs.question: What is the alternate name of bucket sort?
mcqs.explanation: Bucket sort is also known as bin sort. It is an example of a non-comparison sort.

mcqs.question: Which of the following non-comparison sort can also be considered as a comparison based sort?
mcqs.explanation: Bucket sort can also be considered as a comparison based sort. It is because it can also be implemented with comparisons.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true about bucket sort?

options.a: a) It is a non comparison based integer sort
options.b: b) It is a distribution sort
options.c: c) It can also be considered as comparison based sort
options.d: d) It is in place sorting algorithm

mcqs.answer: d) It is in place sorting algorithm
mcqs.explanation: Bucket sort is a non comparison based integer sort. It sorts the given data by distributing the array elements into a number of buckets. It is not an in place sorting technique.

mcqs.question: Which of the following don’t affect the time complexity of bucket sort?

options.a: a) algorithm implemented for sorting individual buckets

mcqs.explanation: Time complexity of bucket sort is affected by various factors. These include algorithm implemented for sorting individual buckets, number of buckets used and distribution of input. It doesnot depend on the input value. It can be either positive or negative or zero.

mcqs.question: Bucket sort is most efficient in the case when __________

options.a: a) the input is non uniformly distributed
options.b: b) the input is uniformly distributed
options.c: c) the input is randomly distributed
options.d: d) the input range is large

mcqs.answer: b) the input is uniformly distributed
mcqs.explanation: Bucket sort works by distributing the array elements into a number of buckets. So bucket sort is most efficient in the case when the input is uniformly distributed.

mcqs.question: Bucket sort is a generalization of which of the following sort?
mcqs.explanation: Pigeonhole sort is a particular case of bucket sort. Bucket sort is also closely related to MSD radix sort.

mcqs.question: What is the worst case time complexity of bucket sort (k = number of buckets)?
mcqs.explanation: Time complexity of bucket sort is O(n<sup>2</sup>) in the worst case. So if bucket sort does not get the inputs in the desired manner then it becomes very inefficient.

mcqs.question: What is the best time complexity of bucket sort (k= number of buckets)?
mcqs.explanation: Time complexity of bucket sort is O(n+k). It performs better than any comparison based sort if there is a uniform input distribution.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not necessarily a stable sorting algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: Bucket sort is not necessarily a stable sorting algorithm. This is because its stability depends on the stability of the algorithm that we have used to sort the individual buckets.

mcqs.question: Bucket sort is an in place sorting algorithm.

mcqs.question: What is the worst space complexity of bucket sort (k = number of buckets)?
mcqs.explanation: Worst case space complexity of bucket sort is O(n.k). So it is not an in place sorting algorithm.

mcqs.question: What is the auxiliary space complexity of bead sort?

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity for a given pancake sort given it undergoes “n” flip operations?
mcqs.explanation: Most sorting algorithms try to sort making the least number of comparisons but in pancake sort we try to sort using as few reversals as possible. Because the total number of flip operations performed in a pancake sort is O(n), the overall time complexity is O(n<sup>2</sup>).

mcqs.question: Which operation is most essential to the process of pancake sort?

options.b: b) Find the largest of given data
options.c: c) Finding the least of given data
options.d: d) Inserting something into the given data

mcqs.explanation: When we use pancake sort, we sort the array to find the largest, and then flip the array at that point to bring that value to the bottom of the pancake stack. The size of the array that we are dealing with is then reduced and the process continues. Flip operation is the most important function in the pancake sort technique.

mcqs.explanation: Although any given solution to an NP-complete problem can be validated quickly in polynomial time; there is no way to efficiently locate a solution to begin with. mcqs.question: Odd-even sort is also known as ____________
mcqs.explanation: Odd-even sort is also known by the name of a brick sort. This algorithm was first proposed by Habermann in 1972 and was initially invented for parallel computation of local interconnection.

mcqs.question: Odd-even sort is a variation of ___________
mcqs.explanation: Odd-even sort is very similar to bubble sort. It works by applying bubble sort in two phases I.e odd phase and even phase. In odd phase bubble sort is applied on odd indexed elements and in even phase bubble sort is applied on even indexed elements.

mcqs.question: Auxiliary space requirement of odd-even sort is ___________
mcqs.explanation: In odd-even sort manipulation is done on the input array itself. So no extra space is required to perform sorting. Thus it requires constant auxiliary space.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithm is NOT stable?
mcqs.explanation: Out of the given options quick sort is the only algorithm which is not stable. Brick sort like bubble sort is a stable sorting algorithm.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithm is in place?
mcqs.explanation: Brick sort is an in place sorting technique as it only requires constant auxiliary space for manipulating the input array.

mcqs.question: Odd-even sort is a comparison based sort.
mcqs.explanation: Odd-even sort compares the value of different elements in the array for sorting. Thus, it is a comparison based sort.

mcqs.question: Brick sort uses which of the following methods for sorting the input?
mcqs.explanation: Brick sort uses the method of exchanging as it swaps the elements which are out of order. This swapping is done in two phases i.e. odd phase and even phase.

mcqs.question: What is the worst case time complexity of odd-even sort?
mcqs.explanation: Worst case complexity is observed when the input array is reverse sorted. This is the same as the worst case complexity of bubble sort.

mcqs.question: What is the best case time complexity of odd-even sort?
mcqs.explanation: Best case complexity is observed when the input array is already sorted. This is the same as the best case complexity of bubble sort.

mcqs.question: What is the average case time complexity of odd-even sort?
mcqs.explanation: Odd-even sort takes O(n<sup>2</sup>) time on average as it keeps on applying bubble sort on the elements in two phases until they are sorted.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following sorting algorithm requires recursion?

mcqs.question: What is the recurrence relation for stooge sort?
mcqs.explanation: In stooge sort recursion is applied to 2/3 part of the array 3 times. Rest of the portion of code has a constant time complexity. So the overall recurrence relation becomes T(n) = 3T(2/3n) + O(1).

mcqs.question: What is the space complexity of stooge sort?
