mcqs.question: Bellmann Ford Algorithm is an example for ____________
mcqs.explanation: In Bellmann Ford Algorithm the shortest paths are calculated in bottom up manner which is similar to other dynamic programming problems.

mcqs.question: A graph is said to have a negative weight cycle when?

options.a: a) The graph has 1 negative weighted edge
options.b: b) The graph has a cycle
options.c: c) The total weight of the graph is negative
options.d: d) The graph has 1 or more negative weighted edges

mcqs.answer: c) The total weight of the graph is negative
mcqs.explanation: When the total weight of the graph sums up to a negative number then the graph is said to have a negative weight cycle. Bellmann Ford Algorithm provides no solution for such graphs.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Floyd-Warshall Algorithm”.

mcqs.question: Floyd Warshall’s Algorithm is used for solving ____________

options.a: a) All pair shortest path problems
options.b: b) Single Source shortest path problems

mcqs.answer: a) All pair shortest path problems
mcqs.explanation: Floyd Warshall’s Algorithm is used for solving all pair shortest path problems. It means the algorithm is used for finding the shortest paths between all pairs of vertices in a graph.

mcqs.question: Floyd Warshall’s Algorithm can be applied on __________
mcqs.explanation: Floyd Warshall Algorithm can be applied in directed graphs. From a given directed graph, an adjacency matrix is framed and then all pair shortest path is computed by the Floyd Warshall Algorithm.

mcqs.question: What is the running time of the Floyd Warshall Algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: The running time of the Floyd Warshall algorithm is determined by the triply nested for loops. Since each execution of the for loop takes O(1) time, the algorithm runs in time Theta(V<sup>3</sup>).

mcqs.question: What approach is being followed in Floyd Warshall Algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: Floyd Warshall Algorithm follows dynamic programming approach because the all pair shortest paths are computed in bottom up manner.

mcqs.question: Floyd Warshall Algorithm can be used for finding _____________
mcqs.explanation: One of the ways to compute the transitive closure of a graph in Theta(N<sup>3</sup>) time is to assign a weight of 1 to each edge of E and then run the Floyd Warshall Algorithm.

mcqs.question: What procedure is being followed in Floyd Warshall Algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: Bottom up procedure is being used to compute the values of the matrix elements dij(k). The input is an n x n matrix. The procedure returns the matrix D(n) of the shortest path weights.

mcqs.question: Floyd- Warshall algorithm was proposed by ____________

options.a: a) Robert Floyd and Stephen Warshall
options.b: b) Stephen Floyd and Robert Warshall
options.c: c) Bernad Floyd and Robert Warshall
options.d: d) Robert Floyd and Bernad Warshall

mcqs.answer: a) Robert Floyd and Stephen Warshall
mcqs.explanation: Floyd- Warshall Algorithm was proposed by Robert Floyd in the year 1962. The same algorithm was proposed by Stephen Warshall during the same year for finding the transitive closure of the graph.

mcqs.question: Who proposed the modern formulation of Floyd-Warshall Algorithm as three nested loops?
mcqs.explanation: The modern formulation of Floyd-Warshall Algorithm as three nested for-loops was proposed by Peter Ingerman in the year 1962.

mcqs.question:
Complete the program. 
n=rows[W]
D(0)=W
for k=1 to n
     do for i=1 to n
          do for j=1 to n
                 do ________________________________
return D(n)
mcqs.explanation: In order to compute the shortest path from vertex i to vertex j, we need to find the minimum of 2 values which are dij(k-1) and sum of dik(k-1) and dkj(k-1).

mcqs.question: What happens when the value of k is 0 in the Floyd Warshall Algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: When k=0, a path from vertex i to vertex j has no intermediate vertices at all. Such a path has at most one edge and hence dij(0) = wij.

mcqs.question: Using logical operator’s instead arithmetic operators saves time and space.
mcqs.explanation: In computers, logical operations on single bit values execute faster than arithmetic operations on integer words of data.

mcqs.question: The time taken to compute the transitive closure of a graph is Theta(n<sup>2</sup>).
mcqs.explanation: The time taken to compute the transitive closure of a graph is Theta(n<sup>3</sup>). Transitive closure can be computed by assigning weight of 1 to each edge and by running Floyd Warshall Algorithm.

mcqs.question: In the given graph, what is the minimum cost to travel from vertex 1 to vertex 3?
mcqs.explanation:
The minimum cost required to travel from node 1 to node 5 is -3.
1-5, cost is -4
5-4, cost is 6
4-3, cost is -5
Hence total cost is -4 + 6 + -5 = -3.

mcqs.question: In the given graph, how many intermediate vertices are required to travel from node a to node e at a minimum cost?
mcqs.explanation:
The minimum cost to travel from node a to node e is 1 by passing via nodes b and c.
a-b, cost 5
b-c, cost 3
c-e, cost -7
Hence the total cost is 1.

mcqs.question: What is the formula to compute the transitive closure of a graph?

options.a: a) tij(k) = tij(k-1) AND (tik(k-1) OR tkj(k-1))
options.b: b) tij(k) = tij(k-1) OR (tik(k-1) AND tkj(k-1))
options.c: c) tij(k) = tij(k-1) AND (tik(k-1) AND tkj(k-1))
options.d: d) tij(k) = tij(k-1) OR (tik(k-1) OR tkj(k-1))

mcqs.answer: b) tij(k) = tij(k-1) OR (tik(k-1) AND tkj(k-1))
mcqs.explanation:
Transitive closure of a graph can be computed by using Floyd Warshall algorithm. This method involves substitution of logical operations (logical OR and logical AND) for arithmetic operations min and + in Floyd Warshall Algorithm.
Floyd Warshall Algorithm: dij(k)=min(dij(k-1), dik(k-1) + dkj(k-1))
Transitive closure: tij(k)= tij(k-1) OR (tik(k-1) AND tkj(k-1)).

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Maximum Flow Problem”.

mcqs.question: What does Maximum flow problem involve?

options.a: a) finding a flow between source and sink that is maximum
options.b: b) finding a flow between source and sink that is minimum
options.c: c) finding the shortest path between source and sink
options.d: d) computing a minimum spanning tree

mcqs.answer: a) finding a flow between source and sink that is maximum
mcqs.explanation: The maximum flow problem involves finding a feasible flow between a source and a sink in a network that is maximum and not minimum.

mcqs.question: A network can have only one source and one sink.
mcqs.explanation: A network can have only one source and one sink inorder to find the feasible flow in a weighted connected graph.

mcqs.question: What is the source?

options.a: a) Vertex with no incoming edges
options.b: b) Vertex with no leaving edges
options.d: d) Vertex with the least weight

mcqs.answer: a) Vertex with no incoming edges
mcqs.explanation: Vertex with no incoming edges is called as a source. Vertex with no leaving edges is called as a sink.

mcqs.question: Which algorithm is used to solve a maximum flow problem?
mcqs.explanation: Ford-fulkerson algorithm is used to compute the maximum feasible flow between a source and a sink in a network.

mcqs.question: Does Ford- Fulkerson algorithm use the idea of?
mcqs.explanation: Ford-Fulkerson algorithm uses the idea of residual graphs which is an extension of naïve greedy approach allowing undo operations.

mcqs.question: The first step in the naïve greedy algorithm is?

options.b: b) calculating the maximum flow using trial and error
options.c: c) adding flows with higher values

mcqs.explanation: The first step in the naïve greedy algorithm is to start with the zero flow followed by adding edges with higher values.

mcqs.question: Under what condition can a vertex combine and distribute flow in any manner?

options.a: a) It may violate edge capacities
options.b: b) It should maintain flow conservation
options.c: c) The vertex should be a source vertex
options.d: d) The vertex should be a sink vertex

mcqs.answer: b) It should maintain flow conservation
mcqs.explanation: A vertex can combine and distribute flow in any manner but it should not violate edge capacities and it should maintain flow conservation.

mcqs.question: Find the maximum flow from the following graph.
mcqs.explanation: Initially, zero flow is computed. Then, computing flow= 7+1+5+2=15. Hence, maximum flow=15.

mcqs.question: A simple acyclic path between source and sink which pass through only positive weighted edges is called?
mcqs.explanation: Augmenting path between source and sink is a simple path without cycles. Path consisting of zero slack edges is called critical path.

mcqs.question: In what time can an augmented path be found?
mcqs.explanation: An augmenting path can be found in O(|E|) mathematically by an unweighted shortest path algorithm.

mcqs.question: Dinic’s algorithm runs faster than the Ford-Fulkerson algorithm.
mcqs.explanation: Dinic’s algorithm includes construction of level graphs and resLidual graphs and finding of augmenting paths along with blocking flow and is faster than the Ford-Fulkerson algorithm.

mcqs.question: What is the running time of an unweighted shortest path algorithm whose augmenting path is the path with the least number of edges?
mcqs.explanation: Each augmenting step takes O(|E|) using an unweighted shortest path algorithm yielding a O(|E|2|V|) bound on the running time.

mcqs.question: Who is the formulator of Maximum flow problem?

options.a: a) Lester R. Ford and Delbert R. Fulkerson
options.b: b) T.E. Harris and F.S. Ross

mcqs.answer: b) T.E. Harris and F.S. Ross
mcqs.explanation: The first ever people to formulate Maximum flow problem were T.E. Harris and F.S. Ross. Lester R. Ford and Delbert R. Fulkerson formulated Ford- Fulkerson algorithm.

mcqs.question: What is the running time of Dinic’s blocking flow algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: The running time of Dinic’s blocking flow algorithm is O(V<sup>2</sup>E). The running of Ford-Fulkerson algorithm is O(E max |f|).

mcqs.question: How many constraints does flow have?
mcqs.explanation: A flow is a mapping which follows two constraints- conservation of flows and capacity constraints.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Matching”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following refers to a set of edges with no shared endpoints?
mcqs.explanation: In a simple graph G, a matching or any edge set in a graph, is a set of edges with no vertices in common. It can also be an entire graph consisting of edges with no common vertices. Hence, matching refers to a set of edges with no shared endpoints.

mcqs.question: In a perfect matching of graph G, every vertex is connected to how many edges?
mcqs.explanation: In a graph G, perfect matching is said to be the matching, that saturates every vertex of the graph. It is a maximal matching set such that it induces the degree of all the vertices as exactly one. Every perfect matching is a maximal matching set.

mcqs.question: In a graph G, the total number of edges in maximum matching is called?
mcqs.explanation: In a graph G, maximum matching is a matching of maximum size among all matchings in the graph. It is also known as the largest maximal matching. The cardinality of the maximum matching set is the matching number.

mcqs.question: Which of the following refers to the perfect matching for the graph given below?

options.a: a)
options.b: b)
options.c: c)
options.d: d)

mcqs.answer: c)
mcqs.explanation: In a graph G, a perfect matching is a maximal matching set such that it induces the degree of all the vertices as exactly one. Hence, from all the given graphs, the graph with degree of all the vertices as 1 and covering all the vertices of the graph will be an appropriate perfect matching.

mcqs.question: In a graph, perfect matching exists only if the number of vertices is even.
mcqs.explanation: In a graph G, perfect matching saturates every vertex of the graph. All the vertices are to be covered in it. So the number of edges in perfect matching is half the number of vertices. Hence, perfect matching exists if the number of vertices is even.

mcqs.question: Which of the following refers to the maximal matching graph for the graph given below?

options.a: a)
options.b: b)
options.c: c)
options.d: d)

mcqs.answer: b)
mcqs.explanation: In a graph, maximal matching means a matching of maximal cardinality, which cannot be increased by adding any edge. If we add any edge to the graph, it violates the matching of the graph. Hence, from all the given graphs, the graph which doesn’t violates the matching by adding any vertex will be an appropriate maximal matching.

mcqs.question: In a graph, every maximum matching is a maximal matching.
mcqs.explanation: A maximal matching in a graph is a matching, which cannot be increased by adding any edge and a maximum matching is a matching of maximum size among all matchings in the graph. Hence, we can say that the given statement is correct.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is an application of graph matching?
mcqs.explanation: One of the applications of graph matching is graph coloring. In graph coloring, all the vertices of the graph are labeled with colors, such that two adjacent vertices do not share the same color. Apart from vertex coloring, it is used in scheduling, flow networks, stable marriage problem and many more.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Stable Marriage Problem”.

mcqs.question: Stable marriage problem is an example of?
mcqs.explanation: Stable marriage problem is an example for recursive algorithm because it recursively uses backtracking algorithm to find an optimal solution.

mcqs.question: Which of the following algorithms does Stable marriage problem uses?
mcqs.explanation: Stable marriage problem uses Gale-Shapley algorithm. Maximum flow problem uses Ford-Fulkerson algorithm. Prim’s algorithm involves minimum spanning tree.

mcqs.question: An optimal solution satisfying men’s preferences is said to be?
mcqs.explanation: An optimal solution satisfying men’s preferences are said to be man optimal. An optimal solution satisfying woman’s preferences are said to be woman optimal.

mcqs.question: When a free man proposes to an available woman, which of the following happens?

options.a: a) She will think and decide
options.c: c) She will replace her current mate

mcqs.explanation: When a man proposes to an available woman, she will accept his proposal irrespective of his position on his preference list.

mcqs.question: If there are n couples who would prefer each other to their actual marriage partners, then the assignment is said to be unstable.
mcqs.explanation: If there are n couples such that a man and a woman are not married, and if they prefer each other to their actual partners, the assignment is unstable.

mcqs.question: How many 2*2 matrices are used in this problem?
mcqs.explanation: Two 2*2 matrices are used. One for men representing corresponding woman and ranking and the other for women.

mcqs.question: What happens when a free man approaches a married woman?

options.b: b) She simply replaces her mate with him
options.c: c) She goes through her preference list and accordingly, she replaces her current mate with him

mcqs.answer: c) She goes through her preference list and accordingly, she replaces her current mate with him
mcqs.explanation: If the preference of the man is greater, she replaces her current mate with him, leaving her current mate free.

mcqs.question: In case of stability, how many symmetric possibilities of trouble can occur?
mcqs.explanation: Possibilities- There might be a woman pw, preferred to w by m, who herself prefers m to be her husband and the same applies to man as well.

mcqs.question: Consider the following ranking matrix. Assume that M1 and W2 are married. Now, M2 approaches W2. Which of the following happens?

options.a: a) W2 replaces M1 with M2
options.c: c) W2 accepts both M1 and M2
options.d: d) W2 rejects both M1 and M2

mcqs.answer: a) W2 replaces M1 with M2
mcqs.explanation: W2 is married to M1. But the preference of W2 has M2 before M1. Hence, W2 replaces M1 with M2.

mcqs.question: Consider the following ranking matrix. Assume that M1 and W1 are married and M2 and W3 are married. Now, whom will M3 approach first?
mcqs.explanation: M3 will approach W3 first. Since W3 is married and since her preference list has her current mate before M3, she rejects his proposal.

mcqs.question: Who formulated a straight forward backtracking scheme for stable marriage problem?
mcqs.explanation: McVitie and Wilson formulated a much faster straight forward backtracking scheme for stable marriage problem. Ford and Fulkerson formulated Maximum flow problem.

mcqs.question: Can stable marriage cannot be solved using branch and bound algorithm.
mcqs.explanation: Stable marriage problem can be solved using branch and bound approach because branch and bound follows backtracking scheme with a limitation factor.

mcqs.question: What is the prime task of the stable marriage problem?

options.a: a) To provide man optimal solution
options.b: b) To provide woman optimal solution
options.c: c) To determine stability of marriage

mcqs.answer: c) To determine stability of marriage
mcqs.explanation: The prime task of stable marriage problem is to determine stability of marriage (i.e) finding a man and a woman who prefer each other to others.

mcqs.question: Which of the following problems is related to stable marriage problem?

options.a: a) Choice of school by students
options.c: c) Arranging data in a database

mcqs.answer: a) Choice of school by students
mcqs.explanation: Choice of school by students is the most related example in the given set of options since both school and students will have a preference list.

mcqs.question: What is the efficiency of Gale-Shapley algorithm used in stable marriage problem?
mcqs.explanation: The time efficiency of Gale-Shapley algorithm is mathematically found to be O(N<sup>2</sup>) where N denotes stable marriage problem.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Maximum Bipartite Matching”.

mcqs.question: _____________ is a matching with the largest number of edges.
mcqs.explanation: Maximum bipartite matching matches two elements with a property that no two edges share a vertex.

mcqs.question: Maximum matching is also called as maximum cardinality matching.
mcqs.explanation: Maximum matching is also called as maximum cardinality matching (i.e.) matching with the largest number of edges.

mcqs.question: How many colours are used in a bipartite graph?
mcqs.explanation: A bipartite graph is said to be two-colourable so that every edge has its vertices coloured in different colours.

mcqs.question: What is the simplest method to prove that a graph is bipartite?

options.a: a) It has a cycle of an odd length
options.b: b) It does not have cycles
options.c: c) It does not have a cycle of an odd length
options.d: d) Both odd and even cycles are formed

mcqs.answer: c) It does not have a cycle of an odd length
mcqs.explanation: It is not difficult to prove that a graph is bipartite if and only if it does not have a cycle of an odd length.

mcqs.question: A matching that matches all the vertices of a graph is called?
mcqs.explanation: A matching that matches all the vertices of a graph is called perfect matching.

mcqs.question: What is the length of an augmenting path?
mcqs.explanation: The length of an augmenting path in a bipartite graph is always said to be always odd.

mcqs.question: In a bipartite graph G=(V,U,E), the matching of a free vertex in V to a free vertex in U is called?
mcqs.explanation: A simple path from a free vertex in V to a free vertex in U whose edges alternate between edges not in M and edges in M is called a augmenting path.

mcqs.question: A matching M is maximal if and only if there exists no augmenting path with respect to M.
mcqs.explanation: According to the theorem discovered by the French mathematician Claude Berge, it means that the current matching is maximal if there is no augmenting path.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is an application for matching?

options.b: b) Pairing boys and girls for a dance
options.c: c) Arranging elements in a set
options.d: d) Finding the shortest traversal path

mcqs.answer: b) Pairing boys and girls for a dance
mcqs.explanation: Pairing boys and girls for a dance is a traditional example for matching. Proposal of marriage is an application of stable marriage problem.

mcqs.question: Which is the correct technique for finding a maximum matching in a graph?
mcqs.explanation: The correct technique for finding a maximum matching in a bipartite graph is by using a Breadth First Search(BFS).

mcqs.question: The problem of maximizing the sum of weights on edges connecting matched pairs of vertices is?
mcqs.explanation: The problem is called as maximum weight matching which is similar to a bipartite matching. It is also called as assignment problem.

mcqs.question: What is the total number of iterations used in a maximum- matching algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: The total number of iterations cannot exceed [n/2]+1 where n=|V|+|U| denoting the number of vertices in the graph.

mcqs.question: What is the efficiency of algorithm designed by Hopcroft and Karp?
mcqs.explanation: The efficiency of algorithm designed by Hopcroft and Karp is mathematically found to be O(√n(n+m)).

mcqs.question: Who was the first person to solve the maximum matching problem?
mcqs.explanation: Jack Edmonds was the first person to solve the maximum matching problem in 1965.

mcqs.question: From the given graph, how many vertices can be matched using maximum matching in bipartite graph algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: One of the solutions of the matching problem is given by a-w,b-v,c-x,d-y,e-z. Hence the answer is 5.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Cut Vertices”.

mcqs.question: A vertex in a graph, on the removal of whose increases the number of connected components is called?
mcqs.explanation: In a simple graph G with V vertices and E edges, there exist a vertex on removal of who’s the graph gets disconnected, this vertex is called the articulation point of the graph. Corresponding edges of the vertices are also removed from the graph.

mcqs.question: Which of the following algorithm can be used for finding articulation points in a graph?
mcqs.explanation: Tarjan’s algorithm: We can use a simple DFS algorithm and make small changes. Let us consider the first case where we apply the DFS algorithm from a vertex v, which is root and if and only if v has more than one child in the DFS tree, it is said to be the articulation point. In the second case, we apply the DFS algorithm from a vertex v which is not the root. If the current edge (v, e) is such a way that neither e nor its descendants have a back edge to any of the ancestors of v, then vertex v is said to be the articulation point.

mcqs.question: What will be the cut vertex set of the graph given below?
mcqs.explanation: Removal of a set of vertices from a graph will make a graph disconnected, this is called a cut vertex set of a graph. The edges are also deleted along with the vertices. The removal of the vertex C and F along with their edges will make the graph disconnected. Hence, the cut vertex set of the graph will be {C, F}. The removal of the vertex D and B will also make the graph disconnected.

mcqs.question:
What will be the time complexity of the brute force approach used to find the articulation points in a given graph? 
For every vertex V, do: 
Remove V from the graph  
See if the graph remains connected 
If graph is disconnected, add V to the resultant set  
Add V back to the graph
mcqs.explanation: In a graph G with V vertices and E edges, this brute force approach removes all vertices one by one and checks whether the removal of a vertex gives a disconnected graph or not. Hence, if the graph is represented using the adjacency list, then the time complexity of this approach will be O(V*(V + E)).

mcqs.question: The pendant vertex of the graph can also be an articulation point of the graph.
mcqs.explanation: A vertex with degree one is called a pendant vertex or end vertex. A vertex of which the deletion disconnects the graph is called a cut vertex. The deletion of the end vertex doesn’t lead the graph to be disconnected. Hence, end vertices cannot be cut vertices.

mcqs.question: A connected graph has a maximum of (n – 2) cut vertices.
mcqs.explanation: Removal of a cut vertex from a graph, may give a disconnected graph. This increases the number of connected components in the graph. The leaves of any tree of order n has at least two vertices that are not cut vertices. Hence, any spanning tree of the graph has a maximum of n – 2 articulation points.

mcqs.question: In which of the following applications can we use the concept of articulation points?
mcqs.explanation: The concept of articulation points can be used to design a network, to find vulnerabilities in a network. If there is a point in a network, which divides the whole network into more than two parts, then the failure of this point might lead to vulnerabilities in a network. Hence, they are very useful in designing a reliable network.

mcqs.question: Which among the following best represents the time complexity to find articulate points in a graph?
mcqs.explanation: To find articulate points in a graph, we use the DFS algorithm with additional arrays. Time required for DFS is O(V+E) when the graph is stored in the adjacency list. Hence, the time complexity to find articulate points is O(V + E).

mcqs.question: A biconnected graph contains how many cut vertices?
mcqs.explanation: There are no cut vertices for a biconnected graph. It is a non-separable graph, if any vertex is removed from the graph, the graph will remain connected. Such types of graphs are called a biconnected graph.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Minimum Cut”.

mcqs.question: Which algorithm is used to solve a minimum cut algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: Minimum cut algorithm is solved using Stoer-Wagner algorithm. Maximum flow problem is solved using Ford-Fulkerson algorithm. Stable marriage problem is solved using Gale-Shapley algorithm.

mcqs.question: ___________ is a partition of the vertices of a graph in two disjoint subsets that are joined by atleast one edge.
mcqs.explanation: Minimum cut is a partition of the vertices in a graph 4. in two disjoint subsets joined by one edge. It is a cut that is minimal in some sense.

mcqs.question: Minimum cut algorithm comes along with the maximum flow problem.
mcqs.explanation: Minimum cut algorithm is considered to be an extension of the maximum flow problem. Minimum cut is finding a cut that is minimal.

mcqs.question: What does the given figure depict?
mcqs.explanation: The given figure is a depiction of min cut problem since the graph is partitioned to find the minimum cut.

mcqs.question: ______________ separates a particular pair of vertices in a graph.
mcqs.explanation: A cut separates a particular pair of vertices in a weighted undirected graph and has minimum possible weight.

mcqs.question: What is the minimum number of cuts that a graph with ‘n’ vertices can have?
mcqs.explanation: The mathematical formula for a graph with ‘n’ vertices can at the most have n(n-1)/2 distinct vertices.

mcqs.question: What is the running time of Karger’s algorithm to find the minimum cut in a graph?
mcqs.explanation: The running time of Karger’s algorithm to find the minimum cut is mathematically found to be O(|V|<sup>2</sup>).

mcqs.question: _____________ is a family of combinatorial optimization problems in which a graph is partitioned into two or more parts with constraints.
mcqs.explanation: Graph partition is a problem in which the graph is partitioned into two or more parts with additional conditions.

mcqs.question: The weight of the cut is not equal to the maximum flow in a network.
mcqs.explanation: According to max-flow min-cut theorem, the weight of the cut is equal to the maximum flow that is sent from source to sink.

mcqs.question: __________ is a data structure used to collect a system of cuts for solving min-cut problem.
mcqs.explanation: Gomory-Hu tree is a weighted tree that contains the minimum cuts for all pairs in a graph. It is constructed in |V|-1 max-flow computations.

mcqs.question: In how many ways can a Gomory-Hu tree be implemented?
mcqs.explanation: Gomory-Hu tree can be implemented in two ways- sequential and parallel.

mcqs.question: The running time of implementing naïve solution to min-cut problem is?
mcqs.explanation: The running time of min-cut algorithm using naïve implementation is mathematically found to be O(N<sup>2</sup>).

mcqs.question: What is the running time of implementing a min-cut algorithm using bidirected edges in a graph?
mcqs.explanation: The running time of a min-cut algorithm using Ford-Fulkerson method of making edges birected in a graph is mathematically found to be O(N<sup>4</sup>).

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is not an application of max-flow min-cut algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: Network reliability, connectivity and bipartite matching are all applications of min-cut algorithm whereas closest pair is a different kind of problem.

mcqs.question: What is the minimum cut of the following network?
mcqs.explanation: The minimum cut of the given graph network is found to be ({1,3},{4,3},{4,5}) and its capacity is 23.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Karger’s Algorithm”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following algorithm can be used to find the minimum cut of a connected graph?
mcqs.explanation: In a given undirected and unweighted graph, the Karger’s algorithm can be used to find the minimum cut of the graph. It gives the minimum number of edges, on the removal of whose the graph gets disconnected into two different components.

mcqs.question: Karger’s algorithm is which type of algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: Randomized algorithms are characterized by their random behavior. For better efficiency in all cases including the average case, we randomly select all the possible outcomes. In Karger’s algorithm, we randomly choose the edges. Hence, randomness plays a huge role in its implementation and it is a randomized algorithm.

mcqs.question: On removal of which of the following edges gives the minimum cut for the graph given below?
mcqs.explanation: Minimum cut is the removal of a set of edges, in such a way that it makes the graph disconnected in two different components. From the given option, removing the edge C-E and D-E will make the graph disconnected in two different components.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following algorithm of Karger’s algorithm given below. Which of the following best suits the blank? 
Let G=(V, E)
while (V > 2)
  pick any edge e from E randomly
  __________________________
  remove self-loops
return the cut left with last 2 vertices

options.a: a) merge or contract both vertices in a single vertex
options.c: c) delete both the vertex connected to it

mcqs.answer: a) merge or contract both vertices in a single vertex
mcqs.explanation: In a graph G with V vertices and E edges, pick up any edge from the graph and merge both the connected vertices into a single vertex and keep changing the graph accordingly. Remove all the self-loops from the graph and return when the graph is left with the last two final vertices.

mcqs.question: Karger’s algorithm always gives a minimum cut for a connected graph.
mcqs.explanation: Karger’s algorithm gives the minimum cut of a connected graph with the success probability of greater than or equal to 1/(n2). Suppose there are 5 nodes in a graph, the probability that it gives the minimum cut is only 1/25. Hence, Karger’s algorithm doesn’t always give the minimum cut for a connected graph.

mcqs.question: The success probability of Karger’s algorithm can be increased.
mcqs.explanation: The success probability of Karger’s algorithm to find the minimum cut of a connected graph is only 1/(n2), where n is the number of nodes in the graph. By running the basic algorithm repeatedly and returning the minimum cuts found, the success probability of Karger’s algorithm can be increased.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best represents the time complexity of Karger’s algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: The Karger’s algorithm to find the minimum cut, if the graph uses adjacency list or adjacency matrix, the implementation of edge contractions can be done with linear updates in the adjacency list or adjacency matrix. Hence, it takes O(n2) time, where n is the number of nodes in the graph.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an application of the minimum cut problem?

options.b: b) To find strongly connected components
options.c: c) To study the reliability of a network
options.d: d) Detecting cycle in a graph

mcqs.answer: c) To study the reliability of a network
mcqs.explanation: The minimum cut problem of a graph minimizes the sum of the weights of the edges crossing the partition. To find whether the network is reliable or not, the concept of minimum cut can be used. It detects the smallest number of edges that may fail in the network.

mcqs.question: Given G is a bipartite graph and the bipartitions of this graphs are U and V respectively. What is the relation between them?

options.a: a) Number of vertices in U = Number of vertices in V
options.b: b) Sum of degrees of vertices in U = Sum of degrees of vertices in V
options.c: c) Number of vertices in U > Number of vertices in V

mcqs.answer: b) Sum of degrees of vertices in U = Sum of degrees of vertices in V
mcqs.explanation: We can prove this by induction. By adding one edge, the degree of vertices in U is equal to 1 as well as in V. Let us assume that this is true for n-1 edges and add one more edge. Since the given edge adds exactly once to both U and V we can tell that this statement is true for all n vertices.

mcqs.explanation: We know that in a bipartite graph sum of degrees of vertices in U=sum of degrees of vertices in V. Given that the graph is a k-regular bipartite graph, we have k*(number of vertices in U)=k*(number of vertices in V).

mcqs.question: There are four students in a class namely A, B, C and D. A tells that a triangle is a bipartite graph. B tells pentagon is a bipartite graph. C tells square is a bipartite graph. D tells heptagon is a bipartite graph. Who among the following is correct?

There exists an edge from ‘1’ to ‘2’, ‘2’ to ‘3’ and ‘3’ to ‘1’. The latter case (‘3’ to ‘1’) makes an edge to exist in a bipartite set X itself. Therefore telling us that graphs with odd cycles are not bipartite.

mcqs.question: How many spanning trees does a complete bipartite graph contain?
mcqs.explanation: Spanning tree of a given graph is defined as the subgraph or the tree with all the given vertices but having minimum number of edges. So, there are a total of m<sup>n-1</sup> * n<sup>n-1</sup> spanning trees for a complete bipartite graph.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Eulerian Tour”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following refers to the circuit that uses every edge exactly once, also starts and ends at the same vertex?
mcqs.explanation: Eulerian tour is also called eulerian circuit or eulerian cycle. In a graph G, an eulerian cycle is a cycle that uses all the edges only once. The eulerian tour is a closed trail, which covers all the edges of the graph, also starts and ends at the same vertex.

mcqs.question: Which algorithm can be used to find an eulerian cycle in a graph?
mcqs.explanation: In a given connected graph G, fleury’s algorithm can be used to find an eulerian cycle. Bridges are the edges that connect two connected components of the graph. The basic idea of this algorithm is to cross the bridge edge as the last edge we have to cross.

mcqs.question: For an euler tour of a tree, how many vertices are required to store euler tour?
mcqs.explanation: To find an euler tour in a tree with V vertices, we use DFS traversal to traverse the tree in such a way that every vertex, when visited is added to the tour. It starts from the root and moves towards the child or starts from the child vertex, returning to the root. To store euler tour, it requires 2 * V – 1 vertices.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is the eulerian tour for the graph given below?
mcqs.explanation: In a graph G, an eulerian circuit or eulerian tour covers all the edges of the graph. The degree of all the vertices must be even as well as the edges shouldn’t repeat. Hence, the appropriate eulerian tour is A→B→C→E→D→C→A.

mcqs.question: An undirected graph has an eulerian cycle if and only if all the vertices have an odd degree.
mcqs.explanation: In an undirected graph, an eulerian cycle is a closed trail, which covers all the edges of the graph. It starts from one vertex and ends at the same vertex. Hence, if all the vertices have an even degree, then the eulerian tour exists for that graph.

mcqs.question:
Consider the given pseudocode for eulerizing a graph. Which of the following best suits the blank? 
Pick up all the vertices of _______  
Repeat edges between the vertices until the graph has no odd degree  
Repeat only pre-existing edges
mcqs.explanation: In a graph, the number of odd degree vertices will always be even. Eulerizing a graph is a process to make the degree of all the vertices even in the graph. It is done by adding a duplicate copy of edges to the odd degree vertices in the previous graph.

mcqs.question: The graph which contains eulerian tour, is called an euler graph.
mcqs.explanation: A trail in a graph is an alternate sequence of vertices and edges where vertices can be repeated but edges can’t. If a connected graph G contains a trail, whose starting and ending vertex are the same and covers all the edges of the graph (eulerian tour) is called an euler graph.

mcqs.question: Which among the following best represents the time complexity to find an euler tour of a tree?
mcqs.explanation: A connected graph with N vertices and N – 1 edges is called a tree. For all the pair of vertices, there is only one edge between them. Starting from the root it will use a DFS traversal to traverse the tree and add the vertex every time it visits and reaches back to the root. Hence, if the tree is represented by an adjacency list, the time complexity to find an euler tour of a tree will be O(n).

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Fleury’s Algorithm”.

mcqs.question: Fleury’s algorithm can be used to print which type of paths or circuits?
mcqs.explanation: In an undirected graph G, an eulerian circuit is a closed trail, which starts and ends at the same vertex. To find such a circuit in the given graph, fleury’s algorithm can be used. Before applying this algorithm, make sure that the given graph is connected.

mcqs.question: What among the following is the basic idea of fleury’s algorithm?

options.a: a) Never travel across a bridge of untraveled part of the graph
options.b: b) Never travel across a bridge
options.c: c) Travel across the bridge of untraveled part, if there is no other choice
options.d: d) Travel across a bridge again over the traveled part of the graph

mcqs.answer: c) Travel across the bridge of untraveled part, if there is no other choice
mcqs.explanation: The basic idea of fleury’s algorithm is that the last edge we cross should be the bridge edge. Bridge edge is the edge, that connects two connected components of the graph. Hence, it should travel across the bridge of the untraveled part, only if there is no other alternative.

mcqs.question: To find an eulerian cycle by fleury’s algorithm, from which vertex you should start if the graph has no odd vertices?

options.b: b) Any vertex of the graph
options.c: c) Vertex with the highest degree
options.d: d) Vertex with the lowest degree

mcqs.answer: b) Any vertex of the graph
mcqs.explanation: The first step in fleury’s algorithm says that, if there are 2 odd degree vertices in the graph, always start with a vertex having an odd degree. But if there are no odd vertices in the graph, you can start with any of the vertex, which will give you an eulerian circuit.

mcqs.question:
Consider the fleury’s algorithm given below. Which of the following best suits the blank? 
Graph must have 0 or 2 odd vertices  
if there are 0 odd vertices, start from any vertex 
if there are 2 odd vertices, start from any one of them 
follow any of the edge, always choose the ______________  
repeat for all the edges of the graph
mcqs.explanation: The idea of fleury’s algorithm is to cover the bridge edge as the last edge to be covered. The degree of all the vertices must be even or 0 or only 2 odd degree vertices. If there are no odd degree vertices, start from anywhere. If there are 2 odd vertices, start from any of these vertices. Starting traversing from any of the edges in such a way it shouldn’t divide the graph into two disconnected components. Hence, always choose the non-bridge edge over the bridge edge.

mcqs.question: The fleury’s algorithm can be applied to a graph if the degree of all the vertices is even or two vertices with an odd degree.
mcqs.explanation: In a graph, the number of odd degree vertices are always even. Fleury’s algorithm is used to find the eulerian circuit for the given graph. The graph will contain an euler circuit if and only if all the vertices of the graph has an even degree or 2 vertices of odd degree.

mcqs.question: Consider the graph given below, print the eulerian circuit of the graph using fleury’s algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: Eulerian circuit is a closed trail, which covers all the edges of the graph. In fleury’s algorithm we always start with the vertex having an odd degree if exists. If there are no odd degree vertices in the graph, we can start from anywhere. In the given graph, vertex D and C are the vertices having an odd degree. Always choose the edge which is non-bridge over bridge edge. Hence, this algorithm gives the eulerian tour D→A→B→D→C.

mcqs.question: To find an eulerian circuit in the graph by fleury’s algorithm, always begin with the vertex having an odd degree.
mcqs.explanation: Fleury’s algorithm to find an eulerian circuit in the given graph says that always start with vertices having an odd degree. Traverse through any edge, in such a way that the edge wouldn’t separate the graph and make it disconnected.

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity of fleury’s algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: Fleury’s algorithm is used to print eulerian path in a graph. In order to do so, we need to check whether each and every edge is bridge or not. To traverse through the graph which is stored in the form of adjacency list, O(V + E) time is required. At every edge DFS is performed to check if it is a bridge which requires O(V + E) time. Therefore, to print eulerian path using fleury’s algorithm, O((V + E)2) time is required.

links.context: This set of Data Structure Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Recursion”.

mcqs.question: Recursion is a method in which the solution of a problem depends on ____________

options.a: a) Larger instances of different problems
options.b: b) Larger instances of the same problem
options.c: c) Smaller instances of the same problem
options.d: d) Smaller instances of different problems

mcqs.answer: c) Smaller instances of the same problem
mcqs.explanation: In recursion, the solution of a problem depends on the solution of smaller instances of the same problem.

mcqs.question: Which of the following problems can’t be solved using recursion?
mcqs.explanation: Problems without base case leads to infinite recursion call. In general, we will assume a base case to avoid infinite recursion call. Problems like finding Factorial of a number, Nth Fibonacci number and Length of a string can be solved using recursion.

mcqs.question: Recursion is similar to which of the following?
mcqs.explanation: Recursion is similar to a loop.

mcqs.question: In recursion, the condition for which the function will stop calling itself is ____________

options.d: d) There is no such condition

mcqs.explanation: For recursion to end at some point, there always has to be a condition for which the function will not call itself. This condition is known as base case.

mcqs.question:
What will happen when the below code snippet is executed? 
void my_recursive_function()
{
   my_recursive_function();
}
int main()
{
   my_recursive_function();
   return 0;
}

options.a: a) The code will be executed successfully and no output will be generated
options.b: b) The code will be executed successfully and random output will be generated
options.c: c) The code will show a compile time error
options.d: d) The code will run for some time and stop when the stack overflows

mcqs.answer: d) The code will run for some time and stop when the stack overflows
mcqs.explanation: Every function call is stored in the stack memory. In this case, there is no terminating condition(base case). So, my_recursive_function() will be called continuously till the stack overflows and there is no more space to store the function calls. At this point of time, the program will stop abruptly.

mcqs.question: Which of the following forms a sequence of natural numbers that occur in different counting problems?
mcqs.explanation: In different counting problems like counting the number of binary search trees with n keys and counting the number of full binary trees, Catalan numbers can be used. They form a sequence of natural numbers.

mcqs.question: What are the values of Catalan numbers for n = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5?
mcqs.explanation: The recursive formula for Catalan numbers is given by C0 = 1 and Cn+1 = Σi=0n(Ci Cn-1) for all n >= 0. Hence, by solving the given formula for n = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5, we get the Catalan numbers as 1, 1, 2, 5, 14 and 42.

options.a: a) Traverse the array from 2 to n one by one and update the value as c[j] * c[i-j-1]
options.b: b) Traverse the array from 2 to n one by one and update the value as c[i] * c[i-j-1]
options.c: c) Traverse the array from 2 to n one by one and update the value as c[j] * c[i-1]
options.d: d) Traverse the array from 2 to n one by one and update the value as c[i] * c[j-1]

mcqs.answer: a) Traverse the array from 2 to n one by one and update the value as c[j] * c[i-j-1]
mcqs.explanation: For finding the nth Catalan number using dynamic approach, first initialize a variable and an array, which will store the Catalan numbers. Initialize the first two values of the array as 1 and then traverse the array till n, starting from 2 and update the value as c[j] * c[i-j-1]. In the end, simply return the value of nth value of the array.

mcqs.question: Dynamic programming approach can be used to implement Catalan numbers.
mcqs.explanation: In the recursive implementation of Catalan numbers, the work is repeated many times. We keep on calculating the same values again and again. Hence, the dynamic programming approach can be used as there are overlapping subproblems.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the time complexity of implementing Catalan numbers using dynamic programming?
mcqs.explanation: To implement Catalan numbers using the dynamic programming approach, we use an array or a vector to store the intermediate results. Here, the space complexity will be O(n). Hence, it will take O(n2) time using the iterative approach.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the time complexity of finding n<sup>th</sup> Catalan numbers using binomial coefficient?
mcqs.explanation: To find the nth Catalan numbers using binomial coefficient, the following formula can be used Cn = 1n+1(2nn). The loop runs starting from 0 till n. Hence, the time complexity to find nth Catalan number using binomial coefficient will take O(n) time.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an application of the Catalan numbers?

options.c: c) Counting the number of possible BST
options.d: d) Detecting cycle in a graph

mcqs.answer: c) Counting the number of possible BST
mcqs.explanation: The Catalan number = (2n)! / ((n + 1)! * n!), is equal to the number of the possible binary search trees that can be formed using n different keys. Hence, the Catalan number can be used to find the number of possible BST.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “GCD and LCM using Recursion – 1”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not another name for GCD(Greatest Common Divisor)?
mcqs.explanation: : LCM (Least Common Multiple) and GCD are not same. GCM (Greatest Common Measure), GCF (Greatest Common Factor), HCF (Highest Common Factor) are other names for GCD.

mcqs.question: What is the GCD of 8 and 12?
mcqs.explanation: GCD is largest positive integer that divides each of the integer. So the GCD of 8 and 12 is 4.

mcqs.question: If GCD of two number is 8 and LCM is 144, then what is the second number if first number is 72?
mcqs.explanation: As A * B = GCD (A, B) * LCM (A, B). So B = (144 * 8)/72 = 16.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is also known as GCD?
mcqs.explanation: GCM (Greatest Common Measure), GCF (Greatest Common Factor), HCF (Highest Common Factor) and HCF (Highest Common Divisor) are also known as GCD.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is coprime number?
mcqs.explanation: Coprime numbers have GCD 1. So 9 and 28 are coprime numbers. While 54 and 24 have GCD 6, 4 and 8 have GCD 4, 6 and 12 have GCD 6.

mcqs.question: In terms of Venn Diagram, which of the following expression gives GCD (Given A ꓵ B ≠ Ø)?

options.a: a) Multiplication of A U B terms
options.b: b) Multiplication of A ꓵ B terms

mcqs.answer: b) Multiplication of A ꓵ B terms
mcqs.explanation: In terms of Venn Diagram, the GCD is given by the intersection of two sets. So A ꓵ B gives the GCD. While A U B gives the LCM.

mcqs.question: What is the GCD according to the given Venn Diagram?
mcqs.explanation: In terms of Venn Diagram, the GCD is given by the intersection of two sets. So A ꓵ B gives the GCD. While A U B gives the LCM. So here A ꓵ B is 5.

mcqs.question: What is the GCD of a and b?
mcqs.explanation: As per Euclid’s Algorithm, gcd (a, b) = gcd (a-b, b) if a > b or gcd (a, b) = gcd (a, b-a) if b > a.

mcqs.question: What is the GCD of 48, 18, 0?
mcqs.explanation: GCD is largest positive integer that divides each of the integer. So the GCD of 48, 18, 0 is 6.

mcqs.question: Is 9 and 28 coprime number?
mcqs.explanation: Coprime numbers have GCD 1. So 9 and 28 are coprime numbers.

mcqs.question: If gcd (a, b) is defined by the expression, d=a*p + b*q where d, p, q are positive integers and a, b is both not zero, then what is the expression called?
mcqs.explanation: If gcd (a, b) is defined by the expression, d=a*p + b*q where d, p, q are positive integers and a, b is both not zero, then the expression is called Bezout’s Identity and p, q can be calculated by extended form of Euclidean algorithm.

mcqs.question: Is gcd an associative function.
mcqs.explanation: The gcd function is an associative function as gcd (a, gcd (b, c)) = gcd (gcd (a, b), c).

mcqs.question: Which is the correct term of the given relation, gcd (a, b) * lcm (a, b) =?
mcqs.explanation: The gcd is closely related to lcm as gcd (a, b) * lcm (a, b) = |a*b|.

mcqs.question: Who gave the expression for the probability and expected value of gcd?
mcqs.explanation: In the year 1972, James E. Nymann showed some result to show the probability and expected value of gcd.

mcqs.question: What is the computational complexity of Binary GCD algorithm where a and b are integers?
mcqs.explanation: From the Binary GCD algorithm, it is found that the computational complexity is O (log a + log b)<sup>2</sup>) as the total number of steps in the execution is at most the total sum of number of bits of a and b.

mcqs.question: LCM is also called as ________

mcqs.explanation: 104 is the smallest positive integer that is divisible by both 8 and 12.

mcqs.explanation: LCM of 2, 4, 8 is 8. So check for the number that is divisible by 8. So 104 is the smallest number that is divisible by 2, 4, 8.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is also known as LCM?
mcqs.explanation: Least Common Multiple is also known as LCM or Lowest Common Multiple.

options.d: d) Multiplication of two coprime numbers

mcqs.answer: d) Multiplication of two coprime numbers
mcqs.explanation: Coprime numbers have GCD 1. While LCM of coprime numbers is the product of those two coprime numbers.

mcqs.question: In terms of Venn Diagram, which of the following expression gives LCM (Given A ꓵ B ≠ Ø)?

options.a: a) Multiplication of A U B terms

mcqs.answer: a) Multiplication of A U B terms

mcqs.explanation: In terms of Venn Diagram, the LCM is given by the Union of two sets. So A U B gives the LCM. So product of all the terms is 180.

mcqs.question: What is the lcm (a, b)?
mcqs.explanation: Since the LCM function is commutative, so lcm (a, b) = lcm (b, a).

mcqs.question: What is the LCM of 48, 18, 6?
mcqs.explanation: The LCM of 48, 18, 6 is 144 and 12<sup>2</sup> is 144.

mcqs.question: Is 9 and 28 coprime number.
mcqs.explanation: Coprime numbers have GCD 1 and LCM is the product of the two given terms. So 9 and 28 are coprime numbers.

mcqs.question: What is the following expression, lcm (a, lcm (b, c) equal to?
mcqs.explanation: Since LCM function follows associativity, hence lcm (a, lcm (b, c) is equal to lcm (lcm (a, b), c).

mcqs.question: Is lcm an associative function.
mcqs.explanation: The lcm function is an associative function as lcm (a, lcm (b, c) is equal to lcm (lcm (a, b), c).

mcqs.question: Which is the correct term of the given relation, lcm (a, b) * gcd (a, b) =?
mcqs.explanation: The lcm is closely related to gcd as lcm (a, b) * gcd (a, b) = |a*b|.

mcqs.question: What is the following expression, lcm (a, gcd (a, b)) equal to?
mcqs.explanation: Since the lcm function follows absorption laws so lcm (a, gcd (a, b)) equal to a.

mcqs.question: Which algorithm is the most efficient numerical algorithm to obtain lcm?
mcqs.explanation: The most efficient way of calculating the lcm of a given number is using Euclid’s algorithm which computes the lcm in much lesser time compared to other algorithms.

mcqs.question: If Matrix A is of order X*Y and Matrix B is of order M*N, then what is the order of the Matrix A*B given that Y=M?
mcqs.explanation: The Matrix A*B is of order X*N as it is given that Y=M i.e. number of columns in Matrix A is equal to total number of rows in matrix B. So the Matrix A*B must have X number of rows and N number of columns.

mcqs.question: How many recursive calls are there in Recursive matrix multiplication through Simple Divide and Conquer Method?

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity of matrix multiplied recursively by Divide and Conquer Method?

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity of matrix multiplied recursively by Strassen’s Method?
mcqs.explanation: The time complexity of recursive multiplication of two square matrices by Strassen’s Method is found to be O(n<sup>log7</sup>) since there are total 7 recursive calls.

mcqs.question: How many recursive calls are there in Recursive matrix multiplication by Strassen’s Method?

mcqs.question: Matrix A is of order 3*4 and Matrix B is of order 4*5. How many elements will be there in a matrix A*B multiplied recursively.

mcqs.question: If Matrix X is of order A*B and Matrix Y is of order C*D, and B=C then the order of the Matrix X*Y is A*D?

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity of the fastest known matrix multiplication algorithm?

mcqs.question: Is Coppersmith-Winograd algorithm better than Strassen’s algorithm in terms of time complexity?

The time complexity of recursive multiplication of two square matrices by Strassen’s Method is found to be O(n<sup>2.80</sup>). 	if(s.size()==0) s.push(x);
	else
	{
		int a = s.top();
		s.pop();
		BottomInsert(x);
		s.push(a);
	}
}

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithm has best case time complexity of O(n<sup>2</sup>)?
mcqs.explanation: Selection sort is not an adaptive sorting algorithm. It finds the index of minimum element in each iteration even if the given array is already sorted. Thus its best case time complexity becomes O(n<sup>2</sup>).

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the biggest advantage of selection sort?

options.a: a) its has low time complexity
options.b: b) it has low space complexity
options.c: c) it is easy to implement
options.d: d) it requires only n swaps under any condition

mcqs.answer: d) it requires only n swaps under any condition
mcqs.explanation: Selection sort works by obtaining least value element in each iteration and then swapping it with the current index. So it will take n swaps under any condition which will be useful when memory write operation is expensive.

mcqs.question: What will be the recurrence relation of the code of recursive selection sort?
mcqs.explanation: Function to find the minimum element index takes n time.The recursive call is made to one less element than in the previous call so the overall recurrence relation becomes T(n) = T(n-1) + n.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sorting algorithm is NOT stable?
mcqs.explanation: Out of the given options selection sort is the only algorithm which is not stable. It is because the order of identical elements in sorted output may be different from input array.

mcqs.question: What will be the best case time complexity of recursive selection sort?
mcqs.explanation: Selection sort’s algorithm is such that it finds the index of minimum element in each iteration even if the given array is already sorted. Thus its best case time complexity becomes O(n<sup>2</sup>).

mcqs.question: Recursive selection sort is a comparison based sort.
mcqs.explanation: In selection sort we need to compare elements in order to find the minimum element in each iteration. So we can say that it uses comparisons in order to sort the array. Thus it qualifies as a comparison based sort.

mcqs.question: What is the average case time complexity of recursive selection sort?
mcqs.explanation: The overall recurrence relation of recursive selection sort is given by T(n) = T(n-1) + n. It is found to be equal to O(n<sup>2</sup>). It is unvaried throughout the three cases.

mcqs.question: What is the bidirectional variant of selection sort?
mcqs.explanation: A bidirectional variant of selection sort is called cocktail sort. It’s an algorithm which finds both the minimum and maximum values in the array in every pass. This reduces the number of scans of the array by a factor of 2.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Towers of Hanoi using Recursion”.

mcqs.question: What is the objective of tower of hanoi puzzle?

options.a: a) To move all disks to some other rod by following rules
options.b: b) To divide the disks equally among the three rods by following rules
options.c: c) To move all disks to some other rod in random order
options.d: d) To divide the disks equally among three rods in random order

mcqs.answer: a) To move all disks to some other rod by following rules
mcqs.explanation: Objective of tower of hanoi problem is to move all disks to some other rod by following the following rules-1) Only one disk can be moved at a time. 2) Disk can only be moved if it is the uppermost disk of the stack. 3) No disk should be placed over a smaller disk.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is NOT a rule of tower of hanoi puzzle?

options.a: a) No disk should be placed over a smaller disk
options.b: b) Disk can only be moved if it is the uppermost disk of the stack
options.c: c) No disk should be placed over a larger disk
options.d: d) Only one disk can be moved at a time

mcqs.answer: c) No disk should be placed over a larger disk
mcqs.explanation: The rule is to not put a disk over a smaller one. Putting a smaller disk over larger one is allowed.

mcqs.question: The time complexity of the solution tower of hanoi problem using recursion is _________
mcqs.explanation: Time complexity of the problem can be found out by solving the recurrence relation: T(n)=2T(n-1)+c. Result of this relation is found to be equal to 2<sup>n</sup>. It can be solved using substitution.

mcqs.question: Recurrence equation formed for the tower of hanoi problem is given by _________
mcqs.explanation: As there are 2 recursive calls to n-1 disks and one constant time operation so the recurrence relation will be given by T(n) = 2T(n-1)+c.

mcqs.question: Minimum number of moves required to solve a tower of hanoi problem with n disks is __________
mcqs.explanation: Minimum number of moves can be calculated by solving the recurrence relation – T(n)=2T(n-1)+c. Alternatively we can observe the pattern formed by the series of number of moves 1,3,7,15…..Either way it turn out to be equal to 2<sup>n</sup>-1.

mcqs.question: Space complexity of recursive solution of tower of hanoi puzzle is ________
mcqs.explanation: Space complexity of tower of hanoi problem can be found out by solving the recurrence relation T(n)=T(n-1)+c. Result of this relation is found out to be n. It can be solved using substitution.

mcqs.explanation: The recursive approach uses divide and conquer algorithm as we break the problem into smaller parts and then solve the smaller parts and finally combine their results to get the overall solution.

mcqs.question: Minimum time required to solve tower of hanoi puzzle with 4 disks assuming one move takes 2 seconds, will be __________
mcqs.explanation:
Number of moves = 24-1=16-1=15
Time for 1 move = 2 seconds
Time for 15 moves = 15×2 = 30 seconds.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Master Theorem”.

mcqs.question: Master’s theorem is used for?

options.d: d) calculating the time complexity of any code

mcqs.explanation: Master’s theorem is a direct method for solving recurrences. We can solve any recurrence that falls under any one of the three cases of master’s theorem.

mcqs.question: How many cases are there under Master’s theorem?
mcqs.explanation: There are primarily 3 cases under master’s theorem. We can solve any recurrence that falls under any one of these three cases.

mcqs.question: What is the result of the recurrences which fall under first case of Master’s theorem (let the recurrence be given by T(n)=aT(n/b)+f(n) and f(n)=n<sup>c</sup>?
mcqs.explanation: In first case of master’s theorem the necessary condition is that c < log<sub>b</sub>a. If this condition is true then T(n) = O(n^log<sub>b</sub>a).

mcqs.question: What is the result of the recurrences which fall under second case of Master’s theorem (let the recurrence be given by T(n)=aT(n/b)+f(n) and f(n)=n<sup>c</sup>?
mcqs.explanation: In second case of master’s theorem the necessary condition is that c = log<sub>b</sub>a. If this condition is true then T(n) = O(n<sup>c</sup> log n)

mcqs.question: What is the result of the recurrences which fall under third case of Master’s theorem (let the recurrence be given by T(n)=aT(n/b)+f(n) and f(n)=n<sup>c</sup>?
mcqs.explanation: In third case of master’s theorem the necessary condition is that c > log<sub>b</sub>a. If this condition is true then T(n) = O(f(n)).

mcqs.question: We can solve any recurrence by using Master’s theorem.
mcqs.explanation: No we cannot solve all the recurrences by only using master’s theorem. We can solve only those which fall under the three cases prescribed in the theorem.

mcqs.question: Under what case of Master’s theorem will the recurrence relation of merge sort fall?

options.d: d) It cannot be solved using master’s theorem

mcqs.explanation: The recurrence relation of merge sort is given by T(n) = 2T(n/2) + O(n). So we can observe that c = Log<sub>b</sub>a so it will fall under case 2 of master’s theorem.

mcqs.question: Under what case of Master’s theorem will the recurrence relation of stooge sort fall?

options.d: d) It cannot be solved using master’s theorem

mcqs.explanation: The recurrence relation of stooge sort is given as T(n) = 3T(2/3n) + O(1). It is found too be equal to O(n<sup>2.7</sup>) using master’s theorem first case.

mcqs.question: Which case of master’s theorem can be extended further?

options.d: d) No case can be extended

mcqs.explanation: The second case of master’s theorem can be extended for a case where f(n) = n<sup>c</sup> (log n)<sup>k</sup> and the resulting recurrence becomes T(n)= O(n<sup>c</sup> (log n))<sup>k+1</sup>.

mcqs.question: What is the result of the recurrences which fall under the extended second case of Master’s theorem (let the recurrence be given by T(n)=aT(n/b)+f(n) and f(n)=n<sup>c</sup>(log n)k?
mcqs.explanation: In the extended second case of master’s theorem the necessary condition is that c = log<sub>b</sub>a. If this condition is true then T(n)= O(n<sup>c</sup>(log n))<sup>k+1</sup>.

mcqs.question: Under what case of Master’s theorem will the recurrence relation of binary search fall?

options.d: d) It cannot be solved using master’s theorem

mcqs.explanation: The recurrence relation of binary search is given by T(n) = T(n/2) + O(1). So we can observe that c = Log<sub>b</sub>a so it will fall under case 2 of master’s theorem.

mcqs.explanation:

So the solution becomes T(n) = O(n2log n).
