mcqs.question: The first step in the naïve greedy algorithm is?

options.a: a) adding flows with higher values
options.d: d) calculating the maximum flow using trial and error

mcqs.explanation: The first step in the naïve greedy algorithm is to start with the zero flow followed by adding edges with higher values.

mcqs.question: Suppose you have coins of denominations 1,3 and 4. You use a greedy algorithm, in which you choose the largest denomination coin which is not greater than the remaining sum. For which of the following sums, will the algorithm produce an optimal answer?
mcqs.explanation: Using the greedy algorithm, three coins {4,1,1} will be selected to make a sum of 6. But, the optimal answer is two coins {3,3}. Similarly, four coins {4,4,1,1} will be selected to make a sum of 10. But, the optimal answer is three coins {4,3,3}. Also, five coins {4,4,4,1,1} will be selected to make a sum of 14. But, the optimal answer is four coins {4,4,3,3}. For a sum of 100, twenty-five coins {all 4’s} will be selected and the optimal answer is also twenty-five coins {all 4’s}.

mcqs.question: Choose the correct statement from the following.

options.a: a) branch and bound is not suitable where a greedy algorithm is not applicable
options.b: b) branch and bound divides a problem into at least 2 new restricted sub problems
options.c: c) backtracking divides a problem into at least 2 new restricted sub problems
options.d: d) branch and bound is more efficient than backtracking

mcqs.answer: b) branch and bound divides a problem into at least 2 new restricted sub problems
mcqs.explanation: Both backtracking as well as branch and bound are problem solving algorithms. Branch and bound is less efficient than backtracking. Branch and bound divides a problem into at least 2 new restricted sub problems.

mcqs.question: Dijkstra’s Algorithm is the prime example for ___________
mcqs.explanation: Dijkstra’s Algorithm is the prime example for greedy algorithms because greedy algorithms generally solve a problem in stages by doing what appears to be the best thing at each stage.

mcqs.question: Bellmann Ford Algorithm is an example for ____________
mcqs.explanation: In Bellmann Ford Algorithm the shortest paths are calculated in bottom up manner which is similar to other dynamic programming problems.

mcqs.question: Which of the following algorithms is the best approach for solving Huffman codes?
mcqs.explanation: Greedy algorithm is the best approach for solving the Huffman codes problem since it greedily searches for an optimal solution.

mcqs.question: Fractional knapsack problem is solved most efficiently by which of the following algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: Greedy algorithm is used to solve this problem. We first sort items according to their value/weight ratio and then add item with highest ratio until we cannot add the next item as a whole. At the end, we add the next item as much as we can.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is false about the Kruskal’s algorithm?

options.a: a) It constructs MST by selecting edges in increasing order of their weights
options.b: b) It is a greedy algorithm
options.c: c) It uses union-find data structure
options.d: d) It can accept cycles in the MST

mcqs.answer: d) It can accept cycles in the MST
mcqs.explanation: Kruskal’s algorithm is a greedy algorithm to construct the MST of the given graph. It constructs the MST by selecting edges in increasing order of their weights and rejects an edge if it may form the cycle. So, using Kruskal’s algorithm is never formed.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Fractional Knapsack Problem”.

mcqs.question: Fractional knapsack problem is also known as __________
mcqs.explanation: Fractional knapsack problem is also called continuous knapsack problem. Fractional knapsack is solved using dynamic programming.

mcqs.question: Fractional knapsack problem is solved most efficiently by which of the following algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: Greedy algorithm is used to solve this problem. We first sort items according to their value/weight ratio and then add item with highest ratio until we cannot add the next item as a whole. At the end, we add the next item as much as we can.

mcqs.question: What is the objective of the knapsack problem?

options.a: a) To get maximum total value in the knapsack
options.b: b) To get minimum total value in the knapsack
options.c: c) To get maximum weight in the knapsack
options.d: d) To get minimum weight in the knapsack

mcqs.answer: a) To get maximum total value in the knapsack
mcqs.explanation: The objective is to fill the knapsack of some given volume with different materials such that the value of selected items is maximized.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statement about 0/1 knapsack and fractional knapsack problem is correct?

options.a: a) In 0/1 knapsack problem items are divisible and in fractional knapsack items are indivisible
options.c: c) 0/1 knapsack is solved using a greedy algorithm and fractional knapsack is solved using dynamic programming
options.d: d) In 0/1 knapsack problem items are indivisible and in fractional knapsack items are divisible

mcqs.answer: d) In 0/1 knapsack problem items are indivisible and in fractional knapsack items are divisible
mcqs.explanation: In fractional knapsack problem we can partially include an item into the knapsack whereas in 0/1 knapsack we have to either include or exclude the item wholly.

mcqs.question: Time complexity of fractional knapsack problem is ____________
mcqs.explanation: As the main time taking a step is of sorting so it defines the time complexity of our code. So the time complexity will be O(n log n) if we use quick sort for sorting.

mcqs.question: Fractional knapsack problem can be solved in time O(n).
mcqs.explanation: It is possible to solve the problem in O(n) time by adapting the algorithm for finding weighted medians.

mcqs.question: Given items as {value,weight} pairs {{40,20},{30,10},{20,5}}. The capacity of knapsack=20. Find the maximum value output assuming items to be divisible.
mcqs.explanation:
The value/weight ratio are-{2,3,4}. So we include the second and third items wholly into the knapsack. This leaves only 5 units of volume for the first item. So we include the first item partially.
Final value = 20+30+(40/4)=60.

mcqs.question: The result of the fractional knapsack is greater than or equal to 0/1 knapsack.
mcqs.explanation: As fractional knapsack gives extra liberty to include the object partially which is not possible with 0/1 knapsack, thus we get better results with a fractional knapsack.

mcqs.question: The main time taking step in fractional knapsack problem is ___________
mcqs.explanation: The main time taking step is to sort the items according to their value/weight ratio. It defines the time complexity of the code.

mcqs.question: Given items as {value,weight} pairs {{60,20},{50,25},{20,5}}. The capacity of knapsack=40. Find the maximum value output assuming items to be divisible and nondivisible respectively.
mcqs.explanation:
Assuming items to be divisible-
The value/weight ratio are {3, 2, 4}.So we include third and first items wholly. So, now only 15 units of volume are left for second item. So we include it partially.
Final volume = 20+60+50x(15/25)=80+30=110
Assuming items to be indivisible- In this case we will have to leave one item due to insufficient capacity.
Final volume = 60 + 20 = 80.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Activity Selection Problem”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following approach should be used to find the solution of the activity selection problem?
mcqs.explanation: To find the solution of the activity selection problem, greedy approach should be used. Since we want to find the maximum number of activities that can be carried out in a particular time interval, this approach will greedily choose and give an optimal solution.

mcqs.question: Suppose two activities A and B, having start and finish time as S<sub>A</sub>, F<sub>A</sub> and S<sub>B</sub>, F<sub>B</sub> respectively. Both the activities are said to be compatible, under which of the following condition?

options.c: c) S<sub>A</sub> >= F<sub>B</sub> or S<sub>B</sub> >= F<sub>A</sub>
options.d: d) S<sub>A</sub> >= F<sub>B</sub> and S<sub>B</sub> = F<sub>A</sub>

mcqs.answer: c) S<sub>A</sub> >= F<sub>B</sub> or S<sub>B</sub> >= F<sub>A</sub>
mcqs.explanation: Two activities A and B are said to be compatible if the intervals [SA, FA) and [SB, FB) do not overlap, i.e., they are disjoint. The activity-selection problem optimizes to select a maximum size subset of mutually compatible activities. Hence, A and B are said to be compatible, if SA >= FB or SB >= FA.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following algorithm to find the solution of the activity selection problem. Which of the following option is best suited to fill the blank? 
Sort the given activity List 
display the first activity 
set i = 1
for j = 1 to n-1 do
  if begin time of activity[j] >= completion of activity[i] then
      ___________
      i = j
mcqs.explanation: To find the solution of the activity selection problem, firstly, sort the given activities in ascending order according to their finish time. Display the first activity. Select and display the new activity only if its starting time is greater than or equal to the previously selected activity’s finish time. Repeat till all the activities are checked.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following number of activities with their start and finish time given below. In which sequence will the activity be selected in order to maximize the number of activities, without any conflicts?
Activity Starting time Finish time
A1 1 2
A2 2 5
A3 1 5
A4 3 6
A5 6 8
A6 4 9
mcqs.explanation: Following activities should be selected: A1 – activity started at 1 and ends at 2. A2 – activity started at 2 and ends at 5. A5 – activity started at 6 and ends at 8.

mcqs.question: Time complexity to find the solution of activity selection problem takes O(n log n) time, when the list is not sorted.
mcqs.explanation: The first step to find the solution of activity selection problem is to sort the activities according to the finish time, which takes O(log n) time. After sorting, we can find the solution using the greedy approach, by checking all the activities once. Hence, for n activities, it takes O(n log n) time if the list is not sorted.

mcqs.question: The solution of the activity selection problem can have two overlapping activities in a particular time interval.
mcqs.explanation: Given a set of activities, with start and finish time, each activity should use a common resource (for e.g. lecture hall). Its objective is to maximize the number of compatible activities that use the resource. Hence, it cannot have two overlapping activities in a particular time interval.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following number of activities with their start and finish time given below. Which of following activity will be left out?
Activity Starting time Finish time
A1 1 2
A2 3 5
A3 4 6
A4 5 8
mcqs.explanation: The activities should be selected are: A1 – activity started at: 1 and ends at 2. A2 – activity started at: 3 and ends at 5. A4 – activity started at: 5 and ends at 8. Hence, activity A3 wouldn’t be selected because it starts at 4 but the previous activity ended at 5.

mcqs.question: Which among the following represents best-case time complexity for activity selection problem?
mcqs.explanation: Suppose, n activities with their start and finish time are given. We have to select the maximum number of activities, but at the same time only one activity can be carried out in a particular time interval. The best-case occurs when the given list is already sorted, which only requires checking all the activities once. Hence, the best-case time complexity for the activity selection problem will be O(n).

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Huffman Code”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following algorithms is the best approach for solving Huffman codes?
mcqs.explanation: Greedy algorithm is the best approach for solving the Huffman codes problem since it greedily searches for an optimal solution.

mcqs.question: How many printable characters does the ASCII character set consists of?
mcqs.explanation: Out of 128 characters in an ASCII set, roughly, only 100 characters are printable while the rest are non-printable.

mcqs.question: Which bit is reserved as a parity bit in an ASCII set?
mcqs.explanation: In an ASCII character set, seven bits are reserved for character representation while the eighth bit is a parity bit.

mcqs.question: How many bits are needed for standard encoding if the size of the character set is X?
mcqs.explanation: If the size of the character set is X, then [log X] bits are needed for representation in a standard encoding.

mcqs.question: The code length does not depend on the frequency of occurrence of characters.
mcqs.explanation: The code length depends on the frequency of occurrence of characters. The more frequent the character occurs, the less is the length of the code.

mcqs.question: In Huffman coding, data in a tree always occur?
mcqs.explanation: In Huffman encoding, data is always stored at the leaves of a tree inorder to compute the codeword effectively.

mcqs.question: From the following given tree, what is the code word for the character ‘a’?
mcqs.explanation: By recording the path of the node from root to leaf, the code word for character ‘a’ is found to be 011.

mcqs.question: From the following given tree, what is the computed codeword for ‘c’?
mcqs.explanation: By recording the path of the node from root to leaf, assigning left branch as 0 and right branch as 1, the codeword for c is 110.

mcqs.question: What will be the cost of the code if character c<sub>i</sub> is at depth d<sub>i</sub> and occurs at frequency f<sub>i</sub>?
mcqs.explanation: If character c<sub>i</sub> is at depth d<sub>i</sub> and occurs at frequency f<sub>i</sub>, the cost of the codeword obtained is ∑f<sub>i</sub>d<sub>i</sub>.

mcqs.question: An optimal code will always be present in a full tree.
mcqs.explanation: An optimal tree will always have the property that all nodes are either leaves or have two children. Otherwise, nodes with one child could move up a level.

mcqs.question: The type of encoding where no character code is the prefix of another character code is called?
mcqs.explanation: Even if the character codes are of different lengths, the encoding where no character code is the prefix of another character code is called prefix encoding.

mcqs.question: What is the running time of the Huffman encoding algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: If we maintain the trees in a priority queue, ordered by weight, then the running time is given by O(C log C).

mcqs.question: What is the running time of the Huffman algorithm, if its implementation of the priority queue is done using linked lists?
mcqs.explanation: If the implementation of the priority queue is done using linked lists, the running time of Huffman algorithm is O(C<sup>2</sup>).

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Backtracking”.

mcqs.question: Which of the problems cannot be solved by backtracking method?
mcqs.explanation: N-queen problem, subset sum problem, Hamiltonian circuit problems can be solved by backtracking method whereas travelling salesman problem is solved by Branch and bound method.

mcqs.question: Backtracking algorithm is implemented by constructing a tree of choices called as?
mcqs.explanation: Backtracking problem is solved by constructing a tree of choices called as the state-space tree. Its root represents an initial state before the search for a solution begins.

mcqs.question: What happens when the backtracking algorithm reaches a complete solution?

options.a: a) It backtracks to the root
options.b: b) It continues searching for other possible solutions
options.c: c) It traverses from a different route
options.d: d) Recursively traverses through the same route

mcqs.answer: b) It continues searching for other possible solutions
mcqs.explanation: When we reach a final solution using a backtracking algorithm, we either stop or continue searching for other possible solutions.

mcqs.question: A node is said to be ____________ if it has a possibility of reaching a complete solution.
mcqs.explanation: If a node has a possibility of reaching the final solution, it is called a promising node. Otherwise, it is non-promising.

mcqs.question: In what manner is a state-space tree for a backtracking algorithm constructed?
mcqs.explanation: A state-space tree for a backtracking algorithm is constructed in the manner of depth-first search so that it is easy to look into.

mcqs.question: The leaves in a state-space tree represent only complete solutions.
mcqs.explanation: The leaves in a state space tree can either represent non-promising dead ends or complete solutions found by the algorithm.

mcqs.question: In general, backtracking can be used to solve?
mcqs.explanation: Backtracking approach is used to solve complex combinatorial problems which cannot be solved by exhaustive search algorithms.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is an application of the backtracking algorithm?

options.b: b) Finding the efficient quantity to shop

mcqs.explanation: Crossword puzzles are based on backtracking approach whereas the rest are travelling salesman problem, knapsack problem and dice game.

mcqs.question: Backtracking algorithm is faster than the brute force technique
mcqs.explanation: Backtracking is faster than brute force approach since it can remove a large set of answers in one test.

mcqs.question: Which of the following logical programming languages is not based on backtracking?
mcqs.explanation: Backtracking algorithm form the basis for icon, planner and prolog whereas fortran is an ancient assembly language used in second generation computers.

mcqs.question: The problem of finding a list of integers in a given specific range that meets certain conditions is called?
mcqs.explanation: Constraint satisfaction problem is the problem of finding a list of integers under given constraints. Constraint satisfaction problem is solved using a backtracking approach.

mcqs.question: Who coined the term ‘backtracking’?
mcqs.explanation: D.H. Lehmer was the first person to coin the term backtracking. Initially, the backtracking facility was provided using SNOBOL.

mcqs.question: ___________ enumerates a list of promising nodes that could be computed to give the possible solutions of a given problem.
mcqs.explanation: Backtracking is a general algorithm that evaluates partially constructed candidates that can be developed further without violating problem constraints.

mcqs.question: The problem of finding a subset of positive integers whose sum is equal to a given positive integer is called as?
mcqs.explanation: Subset sum problem is the problem of finding a subset using the backtracking algorithm when summed, equals a given integer.

mcqs.question: The problem of placing n queens in a chessboard such that no two queens attack each other is called as?
mcqs.explanation: The problem of placing n-queens in a chessboard such that no two queens are vertical or horizontal or diagonal to each other is an n-queen problem. The problem only exists for n = 1, 4, 8.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Eight Queens Problem”.

mcqs.question: Who published the eight queens puzzle?
mcqs.explanation: The first Eight Queen Puzzle was published by Max Friedrich William Bezzel, who was a chess composer by profession in 1848. He was a German chess composer and the first person to publish the puzzle.

mcqs.question: When was the Eight Queen Puzzle published?
mcqs.explanation: The first Eight Queen Puzzle was published by Max Friedrich William Bezzel, who was a German chess composer by profession. He published the puzzle in 1848.

mcqs.question: Who published the first solution of the eight queens puzzle?
mcqs.explanation: The first solution to the Eight Queen Puzzle was given by Franz Nauck in 1850. While the first Eight Queen Puzzle was published by Max Friedrich William Bezzel, who was a German chess composer.

mcqs.question: When was the first solution to Eight Queen Puzzle published?
mcqs.explanation: The first solution to the Eight Queen Puzzle was given by Franz Nauck in 1850. Max Friedrich William Bezzel, who was a German chess composer by profession published the puzzle in 1848.

mcqs.question: Who published the extended version of eight queens puzzle?
mcqs.explanation: The first extended version to the Eight Queen Puzzle was given by Franz Nauck in 1850. Max Friedrich William Bezzel published the puzzle in 1848.

mcqs.question: For how many queens was the extended version of Eight Queen Puzzle applicable for n*n squares?
mcqs.explanation: The extended version given by Franz Nauck of the Eight Queen Puzzle was for n queens on n*n square chessboard. Earlier the puzzle was proposed with 8 queens on 8*8 board.

mcqs.question: Who was the first person to find the solution of Eight Queen Puzzle using determinant?
mcqs.explanation: S. Gunther was the first person to propose a solution to the eight queen puzzle using determinant. Max Friedrich William Bezzel published the puzzle and the first solution to the Eight Queen Puzzle was given by Franz Nauck.

mcqs.question: Who proposed the depth first backtracking algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: In 1972, depth first backtracking algorithm was proposed by Edsger Dijkshtra to illustrate the Eight Queen Puzzle. Max Friedrich William Bezzel published the puzzle and the first solution to the Eight Queen Puzzle was given by Franz Nauck.

mcqs.question: How many solutions are there for 8 queens on 8*8 board?

mcqs.question: Who publish the bitwise operation method to solve the eight queen puzzle?

mcqs.question: Is it possible to have no four queens in a straight line as the part of one of the solution to the eight queen puzzle.
mcqs.explanation: No three queens lie in a straight line in one of the fundamental solution of the eight queen puzzle.

mcqs.question: How many fundamental solutions are the for 3 queens on a 3*3 board?
mcqs.explanation: There are in total zero solution to the 3 queen puzzle for 3*3 chess board. Hence there are no fundamental solutions. For 8*8 chess board with 8 queens there are total of 12 fundamental solutions for the puzzle.

mcqs.question: The six queen puzzle has a fewer solution than the five queen puzzle.
mcqs.explanation: There are total 4 solutions for the six queen puzzle and one fundamental solution while there are total of 10 solutions for 5 queen puzzle and 2 fundamental solutions.

mcqs.question: Which ordered board is the highest enumerated board till now?
mcqs.explanation: The 27*27 board has the highest order board with total 234,907,967,154,122,528 solutions. It also has total of 29,363,495,934,315,694 fundamental solution.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “N Queens Problem”.

mcqs.question: In how many directions do queens attack each other?
mcqs.explanation: Queens attack each other in three directions- vertical, horizontal and diagonal.

mcqs.question: Placing n-queens so that no two queens attack each other is called?
mcqs.explanation: Placing n queens so that no two queens attack each other is n-queens problem. If n=8, it is called as 8-queens problem.

mcqs.question: Where is the n-queens problem implemented?

mcqs.question: Not more than 2 queens can occur in an n-queens problem.

mcqs.question: In n-queen problem, how many values of n does not provide an optimal solution?
mcqs.explanation: N-queen problem does not provide an optimal solution of only three values of n (i.e.) n=2,3.

mcqs.question: Which of the following methods can be used to solve n-queen’s problem?
mcqs.explanation: Of the following given approaches, n-queens problem can be solved using backtracking. It can also be solved using branch and bound.

mcqs.question: Of the following given options, which one of the following is a correct option that provides an optimal solution for 4-queens problem?
mcqs.explanation: Of the following given options for optimal solutions of 4-queens problem, (3, 1, 4, 2) is the right option.

mcqs.question: How many possible solutions occur for a 10-queen problem?

mcqs.question: What is the domination number for 8-queen’s problem?
mcqs.explanation: The minimum number of queens needed to occupy every square in n-queens problem is called domination number. While n=8, the domination number is 5.

mcqs.question: Of the following given options, which one of the following does not provides an optimal solution for 8-queens problem?
mcqs.explanation: The following given options for optimal solutions of 8-queens problem, (1,6,3,8,3,2,4,7) does not provide an optimal solution.

links.context: This set of Data Structure Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Dynamic Programming”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is/are property/properties of a dynamic programming problem?

options.d: d) Both optimal substructure and overlapping subproblems

mcqs.answer: d) Both optimal substructure and overlapping subproblems
mcqs.explanation: A problem that can be solved using dynamic programming possesses overlapping subproblems as well as optimal substructure properties.

mcqs.question: If an optimal solution can be created for a problem by constructing optimal solutions for its subproblems, the problem possesses ____________ property.
mcqs.explanation: Optimal substructure is the property in which an optimal solution is found for the problem by constructing optimal solutions for the subproblems.

mcqs.question: If a problem can be broken into subproblems which are reused several times, the problem possesses ____________ property.
mcqs.explanation: Overlapping subproblems is the property in which value of a subproblem is used several times.

mcqs.question: If a problem can be solved by combining optimal solutions to non-overlapping problems, the strategy is called _____________
mcqs.explanation: In divide and conquer, the problem is divided into smaller non-overlapping subproblems and an optimal solution for each of the subproblems is found. The optimal solutions are then combined to get a global optimal solution. For example, mergesort uses divide and conquer strategy.

mcqs.question: When dynamic programming is applied to a problem, it takes far less time as compared to other methods that don’t take advantage of overlapping subproblems.
mcqs.explanation: Dynamic programming calculates the value of a subproblem only once, while other methods that don’t take advantage of the overlapping subproblems property may calculate the value of the same subproblem several times. So, dynamic programming saves the time of recalculation and takes far less time as compared to other methods that don’t take advantage of the overlapping subproblems property.

mcqs.question: A greedy algorithm can be used to solve all the dynamic programming problems.
mcqs.explanation: A greedy algorithm gives optimal solution for all subproblems, but when these locally optimal solutions are combined it may NOT result into a globally optimal solution. Hence, a greedy algorithm CANNOT be used to solve all the dynamic programming problems.

mcqs.question: In dynamic programming, the technique of storing the previously calculated values is called ___________
mcqs.explanation: Memoization is the technique in which previously calculated values are stored, so that, these values can be used to solve other subproblems.

mcqs.question: When a top-down approach of dynamic programming is applied to a problem, it usually _____________

options.a: a) Decreases both, the time complexity and the space complexity
options.b: b) Decreases the time complexity and increases the space complexity
options.c: c) Increases the time complexity and decreases the space complexity
options.d: d) Increases both, the time complexity and the space complexity

mcqs.answer: b) Decreases the time complexity and increases the space complexity
mcqs.explanation: The top-down approach uses the memoization technique which stores the previously calculated values. Due to this, the time complexity is decreased but the space complexity is increased.

mcqs.question: Which of the following problems is NOT solved using dynamic programming?
mcqs.explanation: The fractional knapsack problem is solved using a greedy algorithm.

mcqs.question: Which of the following problems should be solved using dynamic programming?
mcqs.explanation: The longest common subsequence problem has both, optimal substructure and overlapping subproblems. Hence, dynamic programming should be used the solve this problem.

links.context: This set of Data Structure Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Fibonacci using Dynamic Programming”.

mcqs.question:
The following sequence is a fibonacci sequence: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21,…..
Which technique can be used to get the nth fibonacci term?

options.d: d) Recursion, Dynamic Programming, For loops

mcqs.answer: d) Recursion, Dynamic Programming, For loops
mcqs.explanation: Each of the above mentioned methods can be used to find the nth fibonacci term.

mcqs.question:
Consider the recursive implementation to find the nth fibonacci number: 
int fibo(int n)
    if n <= 1
	return n
    return __________
Which line would make the implementation complete?
mcqs.explanation:
Consider the first five terms of the fibonacci sequence: 0,1,1,2,3. The 6th term can be found by adding the two previous terms, i.e. fibo(6) = fibo(5) + fibo(4) = 3 + 2 = 5. Therefore,the nth term of a fibonacci sequence would be given by:
fibo(n) = fibo(n-1) + fibo(n-2).

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity of the recursive implementation used to find the nth fibonacci term?
mcqs.explanation:
The recurrence relation is given by fibo(n) = fibo(n – 1) + fibo(n – 2). So, the time complexity is given by:
T(n) = T(n – 1) + T(n – 2)
Approximately,
T(n) = 2 * T(n – 1)
= 4 * T(n – 2)
= 8 * T(n – 3)
:
:
:
= 2k * T(n – k)
This recurrence will stop when n – k = 0
i.e. n = k
Therefore, T(n) = 2n * O(0) = 2n
Hence, it takes exponential time.
It can also be proved by drawing the recursion tree and counting the number of leaves.

mcqs.question:
Suppose we find the 8th term using the recursive implementation. The arguments passed to the function calls will be as follows: 
fibonacci(8)
fibonacci(7) + fibonacci(6)
fibonacci(6) + fibonacci(5) + fibonacci(5) + fibonacci(4)
fibonacci(5) + fibonacci(4) + fibonacci(4) + fibonacci(3) + fibonacci(4) 
+ fibonacci(3)	+ fibonacci(3) + fibonacci(2)
:
:
:
Which property is shown by the above function calls?
mcqs.explanation: From the function calls, we can see that fibonacci(4) is calculated twice and fibonacci(3) is calculated thrice. Thus, the same subproblem is solved many times and hence the function calls show the overlapping subproblems property.

mcqs.question:
What is the output of the following program? 
#include<stdio.h>
int fibo(int n)
{
      if(n<=1)
	 return n;
      return fibo(n-1) + fibo(n-2);
}
int main()
{   
      int r = fibo(50000);
      printf("%d",r); 
      return 0;
}
mcqs.explanation: The value of n is 50000. The function is recursive and it’s time complexity is exponential. So, the function will be called almost 2<sup>50000</sup> times. Now, even though NO variables are stored by the function, the space required to store the addresses of these function calls will be enormous. Stack memory is utilized to store these addresses and only a particular amount of stack memory can be used by any program. So, after a certain function call, no more stack space will be available and it will lead to stack overflow causing runtime error.

mcqs.question: What is the space complexity of the recursive implementation used to find the nth fibonacci term?
mcqs.explanation: The recursive implementation doesn’t store any values and calculates every value from scratch. So, the space complexity is O(1).

mcqs.question:
Consider the following code to find the nth fibonacci term:

Complete the above code.

What is the time complexity of the following for loop method used to compute the nth fibonacci term? 
int fibo(int n)
    if n == 0
       return 0 
    else
       prevFib = 0
       curFib = 1

mcqs.question:
What is the time complexity of the following naive method used to find the maximum sub-array sum in an array containing n elements? 
#include<stdio.h>
int main()
{
     int arr[1000]={2, -1, 3, -4, 1, -2, -1, 5, -4}, len=9;

     cur_max = arr[0];
     for(strt_idx = 0; strt_idx < len; strt_idx++)
     {
	  tmp_max=0;
	  for(sub_arr_idx = strt_idx; sub_arr_idx < len; sub_arr_idx++)
	  {
	       tmp_max +=arr[sub_arr_idx];
	       if(tmp_max > cur_max)
		 _____________;
	  }
     }
     printf("%d",cur_max);
     return 0;
}
mcqs.explanation:
The naive method uses two for loops. The outer loop runs from 0 to n,
i.e. i = 0 : n.
The inner loop runs from i to n, i.e. j = i : n.
Therefore, the inner loop runs:
n times when the outer loop runs the first time.
(n-1) times when the outer loop runs the second time.
:
:
:
2 times when the outer loop runs (n-1)th time.
1 time when the outer loop runs nth time.
Therefore, time complexity = n + (n-1) + (n-2) + …… + 2 + 1 = n * (n + 1) /2 = O(n2).

mcqs.question: The edit distance satisfies the axioms of a metric when the costs are non-negative.
mcqs.explanation:
d(s,s) = 0, since each string can be transformed into itself without any change.
d(s1, s2) > 0 when s1 != s2, since the transformation would require at least one operation.
d(s1, s2) = d(s2, s1)
d(s1, s3) <= d(s1, s2) + d(s2, s3)
Thus, the edit distance satisfies the axioms of a metric.

Catalan numbers are given by: (2n!)/((n+1)!n!).
For n = 0, we get C0 = 1.
For n = 3, we get C3 = 5.
For n = 4, we get C4 = 14.
For n = 5, we get C3 = 42.

mcqs.question: Which of the following numbers is the 6th Catalan number?

Catalan numbers are given by: (2n!)/((n+1)!n!).
First Catalan number is given by n = 0.
So the 6th Catalan number will be given by n = 5, which is 42.

links.context: This set of Data Structure Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Minimum Insertions to form a Palindrome”.

mcqs.question: Given a string, you have to find the minimum number of characters to be inserted in the string so that the string becomes a palindrome. Which of the following methods can be used to solve the problem?

options.d: d) Both recursion and dynamic programming

mcqs.answer: d) Both recursion and dynamic programming
mcqs.explanation: Dynamic programming and recursion can be used to solve the problem.

mcqs.question: In which of the following cases the minimum no of insertions to form palindrome is maximum?

options.b: b) String with all same characters

mcqs.explanation: In string of length one, string with all same characters and a palindromic string the no of insertions is zero since the strings are already palindromes. To convert a non-palindromic string to a palindromic string, the minimum length of string to be added is 1 which is greater than all the other above cases. Hence the minimum no of insertions to form palindrome is maximum in non-palindromic strings.

mcqs.question: In the worst case, the minimum number of insertions to be made to convert the string into a palindrome is equal to the length of the string.
mcqs.explanation: In the worst case, the minimum number of insertions to be made to convert the string into a palindrome is equal to length of the string minus one. For example, consider the string “abc”. The string can be converted to “abcba” by inserting “a” and “b”. The number of insertions is two, which is equal to length minus one.

mcqs.question: Consider the string “efge”. What is the minimum number of insertions required to make the string a palindrome?
mcqs.explanation: The string can be converted to “efgfe” by inserting “f” or to “egfge” by inserting “g”. Thus, only one insertion is required.

mcqs.question: Consider the string “abbccbba”. What is the minimum number of insertions required to make the string a palindrome?
mcqs.explanation: The given string is already a palindrome. So, no insertions are required.

mcqs.explanation: A variation of longest common subsequence can be used to solve the minimum number of insertions to form a palindrome problem.

links.text: Maximum Sum Rectangle in a 2D Matrix
links.context: This set of Data Structure Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Maximum Sum Rectangle in a 2D Matrix”.

mcqs.question: Given a 2D matrix, find a submatrix that has the maximum sum. Which of the following methods can be used to solve this problem?

options.d: d) Brute force, Recursion, Dynamic programming

mcqs.answer: d) Brute force, Recursion, Dynamic programming
mcqs.explanation: Brute force, Recursion and Dynamic programming can be used to find the submatrix that has the maximum sum.

mcqs.question: In which of the following cases, the maximum sum rectangle is the 2D matrix itself?

options.a: a) When all the elements are negative
options.b: b) When all the elements are positive
options.c: c) When some elements are positive and some negative
options.d: d) When diagonal elements are positive and rest are negative

mcqs.answer: a) When all the elements are negative
mcqs.explanation: When all the elements of a matrix are positive, the maximum sum rectangle is the 2D matrix itself.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements and select which of the following statement are true. Statement 1: The maximum sum rectangle can be 1X1 matrix containing the largest element If the matrix size is 1X1
Statement 2: The maximum sum rectangle can be 1X1 matrix containing the largest element If all the elements are zero
Statement 3: The maximum sum rectangle can be 1X1 matrix containing the largest element If all the elements are negative

options.b: b) Only statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct
options.c: c) Only statement 1 and Statement 3 are correct
options.d: d) Statement 1, Statement 2 and Statement 3 are correct

mcqs.answer: d) Statement 1, Statement 2 and Statement 3 are correct
mcqs.explanation: If the matrix size is 1×1 then the element itself is the maximum sum of that 1×1 matrix. If all elements are zero, then the sum of any submatrix of the given matrix is zero. If all elements are negative, then the maximum element in that matrix is the highest sum in that matrix which is again 1X1 submatrix of the given matrix. Hence all three statements are correct.

mcqs.question: Consider a matrix in which all the elements are non-zero(at least one positive and at least one negative element). In this case, the sum of the elements of the maximum sum rectangle cannot be zero.
mcqs.explanation: If a matrix contains all non-zero elements with at least one positive and at least on negative element, then the sum of elements of the maximum sum rectangle cannot be zero.

mcqs.question: Consider the 2×3 matrix {{1,2,3},{1,2,3}}. What is the sum of elements of the maximum sum rectangle?
mcqs.explanation: Since all the elements of the 2×3 matrix are positive, the maximum sum rectangle is the matrix itself and the sum of elements is 12.

mcqs.question: Consider the 2×2 matrix {{-1,-2},{-3,-4}}. What is the sum of elements of the maximum sum rectangle?
mcqs.explanation: Since all the elements of the 2×2 matrix are negative, the maximum sum rectangle is {-1}, a 1×1 matrix containing the largest element. The sum of elements of the maximum sum rectangle is -1.

mcqs.question: Consider the 3×3 matrix {{2,1,-3},{6,3,4},{-2,3,0}}. What is the sum of the elements of the maximum sum rectangle?
mcqs.explanation: The complete matrix represents the maximum sum rectangle and it’s sum is 14.

mcqs.question: Given an array, check if the array can be divided into two subsets such that the sum of elements of the two subsets is equal. This is the balanced partition problem. Which of the following methods can be used to solve the balanced partition problem?

options.d: d) Dynamic programming, Recursion, Brute force

mcqs.answer: d) Dynamic programming, Recursion, Brute force

mcqs.question: In which of the following cases, it is not possible to have two subsets with equal sum?

mcqs.answer: c) When the sum of elements is odd

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity of the brute force algorithm used to solve the balanced partition problem?
mcqs.explanation: In the brute force implementation, all the possible subsets will be formed. This takes exponential time.

mcqs.question: Consider a variation of the balanced partition problem in which we find two subsets such that |S1 – S2| is minimum. Consider the array {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}. Which of the following pairs of subsets is an optimal solution for the above problem?

mcqs.question: You are given n dice each having f faces. You have to find the number of ways in which a sum of S can be achieved. This is the dice throw problem. Which of the following methods can be used to solve the dice throw problem?

options.d: d) Brute force, Recursion and Dynamic Programming

mcqs.answer: d) Brute force, Recursion and Dynamic Programming
mcqs.explanation: Brute force, Recursion and Dynamic Programming can be used to solve the dice throw problem.

mcqs.question: You have n dice each having f faces. What is the number of permutations that can be obtained when you roll the n dice together?
mcqs.explanation: Each die can take f values and there are n dice. So, the total number of permutations is f*f*f…n times.

mcqs.question: You have 3 dice each having 6 faces. What is the number of permutations that can be obtained when you roll the 3 dice together?
mcqs.explanation: The total number of permutations that can be obtained is 6 * 6 * 6 = 216.

mcqs.question: You have 2 dice each of them having 6 faces numbered from 1 to 6. What is the number of ways in which a sum of 11 can be achieved?
mcqs.explanation: The sum of 11 can be achieved when the dice show {6, 5} or {5, 6}.

mcqs.question: There are n dice with f faces. The faces are numbered from 1 to f. What is the minimum possible sum that can be obtained when the n dice are rolled together?
mcqs.explanation: The sum will be minimum when all the faces show a value 1. The sum in this case will be n.

mcqs.question: There are n dice with f faces. The faces are numbered from 1 to f. What is the maximum possible sum that can be obtained when the n dice are rolled together?
mcqs.explanation: The sum will be maximum when all the faces show a value f. The sum in this case will be n*f.

mcqs.question: There are 10 dice having 5 faces. The faces are numbered from 1 to 5. What is the number of ways in which a sum of 4 can be achieved?
mcqs.explanation: Since there are 10 dice and the minimum value each die can take is 1, the minimum possible sum is 10. Hence, a sum of 4 cannot be achieved.

links.context: This set of Data Structure Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Counting Boolean Parenthesizations”.

mcqs.question: You are given a boolean expression which consists of operators &, | and ∧ (AND, OR and XOR) and symbols T or F (true or false). You have to find the number of ways in which the symbols can be parenthesized so that the expression evaluates to true. This is the boolean parenthesization problem. Which of the following methods can be used to solve the problem?

options.d: d) Dynamic programming, Recursion and Brute force

mcqs.answer: d) Dynamic programming, Recursion and Brute force
mcqs.explanation: Dynamic programming, Recursion and Brute force can be used to solve the Boolean parenthesization problem.

mcqs.question: Consider the expression T & F | T. What is the number of ways in which the expression can be parenthesized so that the output is T (true)?
mcqs.explanation: The expression can be parenthesized as T & (F | T) and (T & F) | T so that the output is T.

mcqs.question: Consider the expression T & F ∧ T.  What is the number of ways in which the expression can be parenthesized so that the output is T (true)?
mcqs.explanation: The expression can be parenthesized as (T & F) ∧ T  or  T & (F ∧ T), so that the output is T.

mcqs.question: Consider the expression T | F ∧ T. In how many ways can the expression be parenthesized so that the output is F (false)?
mcqs.explanation: The expression can be parenthesized as (T | F) ∧ T, so that the output is F (false).

mcqs.question: Which of the following gives the total number of ways of parenthesizing an expression with n + 1 terms?
mcqs.explanation: The nth Catalan number gives the total number of ways of parenthesizing an expression with n + 1 terms.

mcqs.question: What is the maximum number of ways in which a boolean expression with n + 1 terms can be parenthesized, such that the output is true?
mcqs.explanation: The number of ways will be maximum when all the possible parenthesizations result in a true value. The number of possible parenthesizations is given by the nth catalan number.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Gronsfeld Cipher”.

mcqs.question: Gronsfeld cipher is an example of _____________
mcqs.explanation: Gronsfeld cipher is a substitution cipher. It falls under the category of poly alphabetic cipher as it uses multiple substitutions at different positions in order to cipher the plain text.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about encryption in gronsfeld cipher?

options.a: a) It replaces letters with numbers
options.b: b) It shifts the letters of plain text on the basis of key value
options.c: c) It makes substitutions by using tabula recta
options.d: d) It makes substitutions on the basis of a mathematical formula

mcqs.answer: b) It shifts the letters of plain text on the basis of key value
mcqs.explanation: Encryption of plain text in gronsfeld cipher is done by shifting the letters of plain text on the basis of key value. So it is similar to caesar cipher.

mcqs.question: Gronsfeld cipher is similar to?
mcqs.explanation: In gronsfeld cipher we shift the letters of the plain text on the basis of the key value. So it becomes a modified version of the caesar cipher.

mcqs.question: Which of the following cipher uses a numeric key?
mcqs.explanation: Gronsfeld cipher is a variation of vigenere cipher. The difference is that vigenere cipher uses an alphabetical key whereas gronsfeld cipher uses numeric key.

mcqs.question: Which of the following cipher does not require the use of tabula recta?
mcqs.explanation: Ciphers like running key cipher, vigenere cipher, trithemius cipher etc. makes use of tabula recta. Whereas gronsfeld cipher does not require tabula recta for encryption of plain text.

mcqs.question: Gronsfeld cipher is a variation of ____________
mcqs.explanation: Gronsfeld cipher is a variation of vigenere cipher. The difference is that vigenere cipher uses an alphabetical key whereas the key of gronsfeld cipher consists of numbers.

mcqs.question: Gronsfeld cipher is harder to crack than caesar cipher.
mcqs.explanation: In gronsfeld cipher we shift the letters of the plain text on the basis of the key value. So it becomes a more complex version of the caesar cipher and thus harder to crack.

mcqs.question: What will be the plain text corresponding to cipher text “EETPEG” if gronsfeld cipher is used with key “4321”?
mcqs.explanation: Encryption in gronsfeld cipher takes place by shifting the letters of the plain text by a number given by the numeric key. So by applying the reverse of this method, we get the deciphered text to be “ABROAD”.

mcqs.question: What will be the ciphered text corresponding to “SANFOUNDRY” if gronsfeld cipher is used for encryption with key as “1234”?

mcqs.question: What will be the ciphered text corresponding to “ALGORITHM” if gronsfeld cipher is used for encryption with key “4321”?

mcqs.question: What will be the plain text corresponding to cipher text “SCEFJV” if gronsfeld cipher is used with key “1234”?
mcqs.explanation: Encryption in gronsfeld cipher takes place by shifting the letters of the plain text by a number given by the numeric key. So by applying the reverse of this method, we get the deciphered text to be “RABBIT”.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Beaufort Cipher”.

mcqs.question: Beaufort cipher is an example of ____________
mcqs.explanation: Beaufort cipher is a substitution cipher. It falls under the category of poly alphabetic cipher as it uses multiple substitutions at different positions in order to cipher the plain text.

mcqs.question: Encryption in beaufort cipher is done using ____________
mcqs.explanation: Encryption of plain text in beaufort cipher is done by making use of tabula recta. The same table is also used for encryption in vigenere cipher and running key cipher.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is reciprocal cipher?
mcqs.explanation: A reciprocal cipher is a cipher in which if we try to encrypt the cipher text (using the same cipher) then we gets the plain text as a result. In other words, the process of decryption and encryption is exactly the same.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a difference between beaufort cipher and vigenere cipher?

options.a: a) they use different tables for encryption
options.b: b) vigenere cipher is poly alphabetic whereas beaufort cipher is mono alphabetic
options.c: c) vigenere cipher uses a key whereas no key is required for using beaufort cipher
options.d: d) they use the same table for encryption, but in a different manner

mcqs.answer: d) they use the same table for encryption, but in a different manner
mcqs.explanation: Beaufort cipher is a variation of vigenere cipher. They use the same table i.e. tabula recta for encryption but the table is used in a different manner.

mcqs.question: Beaufort cipher is a variant of ____________
mcqs.explanation: Beaufort cipher is a variant of vigenere cipher. The difference is that beaufort cipher uses tabula recta in a different manner for encryption.

mcqs.question: The process of decryption is exactly same as that of encryption in beaufort cipher.
mcqs.explanation: Beaufort cipher is an example of reciprocal cipher. So that is why the process of decryption is exactly same as that of encryption in beaufort cipher.

mcqs.question: What will be the plain text corresponding to cipher text “SEDGKG” if beaufort cipher is used with key as “KEY”?
mcqs.explanation: The process of decryption and encryption are exactly the same in beaufort cipher. So the corresponding plain text would be “SAVEUS”.

mcqs.question: Beaufort cipher and variant beaufort cipher are same ciphers.
mcqs.explanation: Beaufort cipher is different from variant beaufort cipher. Variant beaufort cipher is a variant of beaufort cipher.

mcqs.question: What will be the ciphered text corresponding to “SANFOUNDRY” if beaufort cipher is used for encryption with key as “KEY”?
mcqs.explanation: For encrypting plain text choose the first letter of plain text (i.e. S) in the first horizontal row. Then find the first letter of key (i.e. K) in the column obtained in the first step. Finally, choose the leftmost letter of the row (i.e. S) obtained in the previous step. So the corresponding cipher text is “SELFQEXBHM”.

mcqs.question: What will be the ciphered text corresponding to “ALGORITHM” if beaufort cipher is used for encryption with key as “KEY”?
mcqs.explanation: For encrypting plain text choose the first letter of plain text (i.e. A) in the first horizontal row. Then find the first letter of key (i.e. K) in the column obtained in the first step. Finally, choose the leftmost letter of the row (i.e. K) obtained in the previous step. So the corresponding cipher text is “KTSWNQRXM”.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Autokey Cipher”.

mcqs.question: What is the meaning of cipher in cryptography?

options.a: a) an algorithm that performs encryption
options.b: b) an algorithm that generates a secret code
options.c: c) an algorithm that performs encryption or decryption

mcqs.answer: c) an algorithm that performs encryption or decryption
mcqs.explanation: Cipher is an algorithm for performing encryption or decryption. In cryptography, a set of defined steps are followed to generate ciphers. These are necessary to prevent a data breach.

mcqs.question: Autokey cipher is an example of ___________
mcqs.explanation: Autokey cipher is a substitution cipher. It falls under the category of poly alphabetic cipher as it uses multiple substitutions at different positions in order to cipher the plain text.

mcqs.question: Encryption in Autokey cipher is done using ___________
mcqs.explanation: Encryption of plain text in Autokey cipher is done using the same table which is used for encryption in vigenere cipher. It is known as vigenere table.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly defines poly alphabetic cipher?

options.a: a) a substitution based cipher which uses multiple substitution at different positions
options.b: b) a substitution based cipher which uses fixed substitution over entire message
options.c: c) a transposition based cipher which uses multiple substitution at different positions
options.d: d) a transposition based cipher which uses fixed substitution over entire message

mcqs.answer: a) a substitution based cipher which uses multiple substitution at different positions
mcqs.explanation: Poly alphabetic cipher is a type of substitution cipher. It uses multiple substitution at different positions in order to cipher the plain text.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a type of poly alphabetic cipher?
mcqs.explanation: In poly alphabetic cipher each symbol of plain text is replaced by a different cipher text regardless of its occurrence. Out of the given options only additive cipher is not a poly alphabetic cipher.

mcqs.question: Autokey cipher is closely related to ___________
mcqs.explanation: Autokey cipher like vigenere cipher uses vigenere table in order to encrypt the plain text. The difference in these cipher is the usage of the keyword.

mcqs.question: Autokey cipher is harder to crack than keyword cipher.
mcqs.explanation: Keyword cipher is less secure than Autokey cipher. It is due to the fact that keyword cipher is mono alphabetic and thus can be cracked using frequency analysis. But Autokey cipher being a poly alphabetic cipher cannot be cracked using this method.

mcqs.question: What will be the plain text corresponding to cipher text “ZEYQC” if autokey cipher is used with keyword as “SANFOUNDRY”?
mcqs.explanation: Autokey cipher is a type of poly alphabetic substitution which uses vigenere table for making substitutions in the plain text after generating key using plain text. Using the table we find the plain text to be “HELLO”.

mcqs.question: Autokey cipher is also known as?
mcqs.explanation: Autoclave cipher is an alternative name given to autokey cipher. It is because the encrypted text is formed using a key that is generated from a message(plain text) itself.

mcqs.question: In which of the following cipher the plain text and the ciphered text does not have same number of letters?
mcqs.explanation: In transposition cipher and mono alphabetic cipher the number of letters remain same in ciphered and deciphered text. But in poly alphabetic cipher the number of letters are different. So here as autokey cipher is the only poly alphabetic cipher so it will be the answer.

mcqs.question: What will be the ciphered text if the string “SECRET” is given as input to the code of autokey cipher with keyword as “SANFOUNDRY”?
mcqs.explanation: For encrypting a plain text in autokey cipher we first add the keyword at the beginning of the plain text in order to obtain the key for encryption. Then we use the vigenere table for making respective substitutions.

mcqs.question: Vigenere cipher is harder to crack than autokey cipher.
mcqs.explanation: Autokey cipher is harder to crack than vigenere cipher. It is because in autokey cipher the key is formed using the plain text itself whereas in vigenere cipher the key is independent of the plain text. This makes autokey cipher more secure.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Playfair Cipher”.

mcqs.question: What is the alternative name of playfair cipher?
mcqs.explanation: Playfair cipher is also known by the name of Wheatstone playfair cipher. It is because it was discovered by Charles Wheatstone but was promoted by Lord Playfair.

mcqs.question: Playfair cipher is an example of __________
mcqs.explanation: Playfair cipher is a substitution cipher. It falls under the category of poly alphabetic cipher as it uses multiple substitution at different positions in order to cipher the plain text.

mcqs.question: Encryption in Autokey cipher is done using __________
mcqs.explanation: Encryption of plain text in playfair cipher is done using a 5×5 table. In this table, all the alphabets of the keyword are arranged row wise by eliminating any duplicates then the remaining letters of the alphabet are placed. One of the alphabet has to be omitted in order to fit all the alphabets in the table.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly defines poly graphic substitution cipher?

options.a: a) a substitution based cipher which uses multiple substitutions at different positions
options.b: b) a substitution based cipher which uses fixed substitution over entire plain text
options.c: c) a substitution based cipher in which substitution is performed over a block of letters
options.d: d) a transposition based cipher which uses fixed substitution over entire plain text

mcqs.answer: c) a substitution based cipher in which substitution is performed over a block of letters
mcqs.explanation: Poly graphic cipher is a type of substitution cipher in which substitution is performed over a block of letters. Playfair cipher is an example of poly graphic cipher.

mcqs.question: Which of the following was the first diagram substitution cipher?
mcqs.explanation: Poly graphic cipher is a type of substitution cipher in which substitution is performed over a block of letters. In diagram substitution, two adjacent letters are substituted simultaneously. Playfair cipher was the first diagram substitution cipher.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is hardest to break using frequency analysis?
mcqs.explanation: Out of the given options playfair cipher is the hardest cipher to break using frequency analysis. It is because it does not substitute letters of the word individually but it encrypts them in pairs of two.

mcqs.question: Playfair cipher is harder to crack than keyword cipher.
mcqs.explanation: Keyword cipher is less secure than playfair cipher. It is due to the fact that keyword cipher is mono alphabetic and thus can be cracked using frequency analysis. But playfair cipher being a poly graphic substitution cipher is harder to break using this method.

mcqs.question: What will be the plain text corresponding to cipher text “BPKYFS” if playfair cipher is used with keyword as “SECRET” (assuming j is combined with i)?
mcqs.explanation: To decrypt the message we follow the reverse procedure. The table is formed in the same manner. Applying this we get the plain text to be “DOLLAR”.

mcqs.question: What is the rule for encryption in playfair cipher if the letters in a pair are identical?

options.a: a) then that pair is neglected
options.b: b) a null is added in between the letters
options.c: c) one of the identical letter is replaced by some other letter
options.d: d) then both of the letters are replaced by the letter appearing just next in the row

mcqs.answer: b) a null is added in between the letters
mcqs.explanation: In playfair cipher if the letters in a pair are identical then a null is added in between the letters. Any letter can be used as a null as long as that letter is not the one being repeated.

mcqs.question: What is the rule for encryption in playfair cipher if the letters in a pair appear in same row?

options.a: a) they are replaced by the letter appearing immediately below them respectively
options.b: b) they are replaced by the letter appearing immediately right to them respectively
options.c: c) they are replaced by the letter at the corner of the row

mcqs.answer: b) they are replaced by the letter appearing immediately right to them respectively
mcqs.explanation: If the letters in a pair appear in same row then they are replaced by the letters appearing immediately right to them respectively. If the element to be replaced appears at the corner of the row then we wrap around to the left side of that row.

mcqs.question: What will be the ciphered text if the string “SANFOUNDRY” is given as input to the code of playfair cipher with keyword as “SECRET” (assuming j is combined with i)?
mcqs.explanation:
For encrypting the plain text using playfair cipher we use a 5×5 table that is constructed by using keyword. Then we apply rules for encryption in order to get the ciphered text. Table is given as under-

S E C R T
A B D F G
H I K L M
N O P Q U
V W X Y Z

mcqs.question: What is the rule for encryption in playfair cipher if the letters in a pair appear in same column?

options.a: a) they are replaced by the letter appearing immediately below them respectively
options.b: b) they are replaced by the letter appearing immediately right to them respectively
options.c: c) they are replaced by the letters at the corner of the row

mcqs.answer: a) they are replaced by the letter appearing immediately below them respectively
mcqs.explanation: If the letters in a pair appear in the same column then they are replaced by the letters appearing immediately below them respectively. If the element to be replaced appears at the corner of the column then we wrap around to the top side of that column.

mcqs.question: What is the rule for encryption in playfair cipher if the letters in a pair does not appear in same row or column?

options.a: a) they are replaced by the letter appearing immediately below them respectively
options.b: b) they are replaced by the letter appearing immediately right to them respectively
options.c: c) they are replaced by the letter of the same row at the corner of the rectangle defined by the original pair respectively

mcqs.answer: c) they are replaced by the letter of the same row at the corner of the rectangle defined by the original pair respectively
mcqs.explanation: If the letters in a pair does not appear in same row or column then they are replaced by the letters of the same row at the corner of the rectangle defined by the original pair respectively. The order of letters should be maintained.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Hill Cipher”.

mcqs.question: Hill cipher requires prerequisite knowledge of?
mcqs.explanation: Hill cipher uses matrix multiplication in order to encrypt the given plain text. So it requires prerequisite knowledge of matrix algebra.

mcqs.question: Hill cipher is an example of ____________
mcqs.explanation: Hill cipher is a substitution cipher. It falls under the category of poly alphabetic cipher as it uses multiple substitutions at different positions in order to cipher the plain text.

mcqs.question: Encryption in hill cipher is done using ______________
mcqs.explanation: Encryption of plain text in playfair cipher is done using matrix multiplication. Then modulo 26 of the resulting matrix is taken so as to get the ciphered text.

mcqs.question: What is poly graphic substitution cipher?

options.a: a) a substitution based cipher which uses multiple substitutions at different positions
options.b: b) a substitution based cipher which uses fixed substitution over entire plain text
options.c: c) a substitution based cipher in which substitution is performed over a block of letters
options.d: d) a transposition based cipher which uses fixed substitution over entire plain text

mcqs.answer: c) a substitution based cipher in which substitution is performed over a block of letters
mcqs.explanation: Poly graphic cipher is a type of substitution cipher in which substitution is performed over a block of letters. Hill cipher is an example of poly graphic cipher.

mcqs.question: Which of the following was the first poly graphic cipher to be able to operate on more than 3 letters at once?
mcqs.explanation: Poly graphic cipher is a type of substitution cipher in which substitution is performed over a block of letters. Hill cipher was the first poly graphic cipher to be able to operate on more than 3 letters at once.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is hardest to break using frequency analysis?
mcqs.explanation: Out of the given options hill cipher is the hardest cipher to break using frequency analysis. Although it is quite vulnerable to other forms of attack.

mcqs.question: Hill cipher is harder to crack than playfair cipher.
mcqs.explanation: Both hill cipher and playfair cipher are less vulnerable to frequency analysis. But hill cipher is quite vulnerable to other forms of attack and thus less secure than playfair cipher.

mcqs.question: What will be the plain text corresponding to cipher text “YGQ“ if hill cipher is used with keyword as “GYBNQKURP”?
mcqs.explanation: To decrypt the message we follow the reverse procedure. We first find the inverse of the keyword matrix then multiply it with cipher matrix.

mcqs.question: What will be the size of a key matrix if the plain text is “SECRET”?
mcqs.explanation: Hill cipher uses a n x n matrix in order to cipher the plain text. In this case n=6 so a 6×6 matrix will be used.

mcqs.question: A key matrix used for encryption in hill cipher must be?
mcqs.explanation: A key matrix used for encryption in hill cipher must be invertible matrix. Otherwise it will be impossible to decipher the message.

mcqs.question: What will be the ciphered text if the plain text “SAN” is encrypted using hill cipher with keyword as “GYBNQKURP”?
mcqs.explanation: We first convert the keyword and plain text into their corresponding matrix respectively. Then we multiply those matrix and take modulo 26 of the resulting matrix to get the ciphered text.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Rail Fence”.

mcqs.question: What is the alternative name given to Rail fence cipher?
mcqs.explanation: Rail fence cipher is also known as zig zag cipher. It is so because the plain text gets ciphered by arranging the letters in a zig zag fashion.

mcqs.question: Rail fence cipher is an example of ___________
mcqs.explanation: Rail fence cipher is a transposition cipher. It falls under the category of transposition cipher as it encrypts the plain text by rearranging its letters.

mcqs.question: Encryption in Rail fence cipher is done using _____________

options.a: a) by arranging the letters in a zig zag fashion in a table
options.c: c) by arranging letters in vigenere table

mcqs.answer: a) by arranging the letters in a zig zag fashion in a table
mcqs.explanation: Rail fence cipher is a transposition cipher. It encrypts a given plain text by arranging the letters in a zig zag fashion in a table.

mcqs.question: Which of the following ciphers are created by shuffling the letters of a word?
mcqs.explanation: There are two types of traditional ciphers- Transposition and substitution cipher. In transposition cipher the letters of the given data are shuffled in a particular order, fixed by a given rule.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a type of poly alphabetic cipher?
mcqs.explanation: In poly alphabetic cipher each symbol of plain text is replaced by a different cipher text regardless of its occurrence. Out of the given options, only additive cipher is not a poly alphabetic cipher.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is are two types of traditional cipher?

options.a: a) transposition cipher and replacement cipher
options.b: b) transposition cipher and substitution cipher
options.c: c) transforming cipher and substitution cipher
options.d: d) transforming cipher and replacement cipher

mcqs.answer: b) transposition cipher and substitution cipher
mcqs.explanation: There are two types of a traditional cipher. First is transposition cipher and the second is substitution cipher.

mcqs.question: The number of columns in the table used for encryption in rail fence cipher depends upon the given key value.
mcqs.explanation: The number of columns in the table of rail fence cipher is always equal to the number of letters in the plain text. It is independent of the given key value.

mcqs.question: What will be the plain text corresponding to cipher text “SCSEMG” if rail fence cipher is used with key value 2?

For decryption we reverse the process used in encryption.

S C S
E M G

mcqs.question: Rail fence cipher is more secure than one time pad cipher.
mcqs.explanation: One time pad cipher is one of the most secure traditional cipher as it is almost impossible to crack. Rail fence cipher is not very hard to crack. Thus rail fence cipher is less secure than one time pad cipher.

mcqs.question: In which of the following cipher the plain text and the ciphered text have same letters?
mcqs.explanation: In transposition cipher the letters remain the same in ciphered and plain text. Their position is only changed whereas in substitution cipher the letters become different in encrypted text. So rail fence cipher will be the correct option.

mcqs.question: What will be the ciphered text if rail fence cipher is used for encrypting the plain text “SANFOUNDRY” with the key value given to be 2?

For encrypting a plain text using rail fence cipher we use a table having the number of rows equal to key value as shown below. Then we read along the rows to get the ciphered text.

S N O N R
A F U D Y

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Route Cipher”.

mcqs.question: What is route cipher?

options.a: a) a transposition cipher that performs encryption by following an imaginary pattern on a grid
options.b: b) a substitution cipher that performs encryption by following an imaginary pattern on a grid
options.c: c) a transposition cipher that performs encryption by following a zig zag pattern on a grid
options.d: d) a substitution cipher that performs encryption by following a zig zag pattern on a grid

mcqs.answer: a) a transposition cipher that performs encryption by following an imaginary pattern on a grid
mcqs.explanation: Route cipher is a transposition cipher. It encrypts the plain text by following an imaginary pattern on a grid. This pattern can vary from one version of route cipher to others.

mcqs.question: Route cipher is an example of ____________
mcqs.explanation: Route cipher is a transposition cipher. It falls under the category of transposition cipher as it encrypts the plain text by rearranging its letters.

mcqs.question: Encryption in Route cipher is done ___________

options.a: a) by arranging the letters in a zig zag fashion in a table
options.c: c) by following an imaginary pattern drawn on a grid

mcqs.answer: c) by following an imaginary pattern drawn on a grid
mcqs.explanation: Route cipher is a transposition cipher. It encrypts the plain text by following an imaginary pattern on a grid.

mcqs.question: Which of the following ciphers are created by shuffling the letters of a word?
mcqs.explanation: In transposition cipher the letters of the given data are shuffled in a particular order, fixed by a given rule. Route cipher is the only transposition cipher out of the given options.

mcqs.question: Route cipher is closely related to?
mcqs.explanation: Route cipher is closely related to rail fence cipher. In rail fence cipher the plain text is written in a zig zag fashion in a grid whereas in route cipher the plain text is written horizontally.

mcqs.question: Rail fence cipher is more secure as compared to route cipher?
mcqs.explanation: Rail fence is cipher is less secure than route cipher. It is because the key of route cipher not only defines the size of the grid but also the path that is to be followed.

mcqs.question: Router cipher becomes less secure when we have to encrypt longer messages.

mcqs.question:
What will be the output of the following C++ code? 
#include <cmath> 
#include <iostream> 
using namespace std; 
void Cipher(string str) 
{ 
    int r, c; 
    for (int i = 0; str[i]; i++) 
    { 
 
	r = ceil((str[i] - 'a') / 5) + 1; 
 
 
	c = ((str[i] - 'a') % 5) + 1; 
 
 
	if (str[i] == 'k') 
        { 
	    r = r - 1; 
	    c = 5 - c + 1; 
	} 
 
 
	else if (str[i] >= 'j') 
        {

		r = r - 1; 
	    }

    }

} 
 
int main()

}
