mcqs.explanation: Although columnar transposition cipher is a weak cipher in itself. But it can be combined with other substitution ciphers so as to improve its security. The probability of error remains high while decoding columnar cipher as it is a lengthy process.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Affine Cipher”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following cipher makes use of linear algebra for encrypting data?
mcqs.explanation: Affine cipher is the only cipher out of the given options that make use of linear algebra for the purpose of encryption. It is a type of mono alphabetic cipher.

mcqs.question: Which of the following cipher requires only one key for decoding the ciphered text?
mcqs.explanation: Asymmetric cipher makes use of 2 keys for the purpose of encryption. As affine cipher is the only symmetric cipher out of the given options so it requires only one key.

mcqs.question: Choose the weakest cipher from the following?
mcqs.explanation: Affine cipher is the weakest cipher out of the given options as it is a mono alphabetic cipher and other options are poly alphabetic ciphers. So it is quite vulnerable to frequency analysis.

mcqs.question: What is the formula used for encryption of data using affine cipher(a,b are constants and x is the numerical equivalent of a letter to be encrypted)?
mcqs.explanation: Affine cipher uses linear algebra for the purpose of encryption. It uses the formula (ax+b)%26 for this purpose.

mcqs.question: What is the formula used for decoding the ciphered text using affine cipher(a,b are constants and x is the numerical equivalent of a letter to be encrypted)?
mcqs.explanation: Affine cipher uses linear algebra for the purpose of encryption. It uses the formula  a<sup>-1</sup>(x-b)%26 for decryption of ciphered text.

mcqs.question: Affine cipher is an example of?
mcqs.explanation: Affine cipher falls in the category of mono alphabetic substitution cipher. It uses linear algebra for encrypting the plain text.

mcqs.question: Affine cipher is less secure than caesar cipher.
mcqs.explanation: Affine cipher is more secure as compared to caesar cipher. But affine cipher is a very weak cipher as it can be easily broken using frequency analysis.

mcqs.question: Affine cipher is not susceptible to frequency analysis.
mcqs.explanation: Affine cipher is a very weak cipher as it can be easily broken using frequency analysis. It can be easily cracked even if 2 characters are known.

mcqs.question: What will be the ciphered text corresponding to plain text “sanfoundry” if an affine cipher is used with key values as a=5, b=10?
mcqs.explanation: Affine cipher uses linear algebra for the purpose of encryption. It uses the formula  (ax+b)%26 for this purpose. So the ciphered text will be “wkxjcgxzra”.

mcqs.question: What will be the plain text corresponding to ciphered text “rmw ” if an affine cipher is used with key values as a=5, b=10?
mcqs.explanation: Affine cipher uses linear algebra for the purpose of encryption It uses the formula a<sup>-1</sup>(x-b)%26 for decryption of ciphered text. So the plain text will be “srt”.

mcqs.question: While choosing the value of a and m (m is the no. of alphabets) in affine cipher it must be ensured that?

options.a: a) a and m are prime numbers
options.b: b) a and m are odd numbers
options.c: c) a and m are coprime
options.d: d) a and m are even numbers

mcqs.answer: c) a and m are coprime
mcqs.explanation: While choosing the values of a and m it should be ensured that a and m are coprime. Otherwise decoding the ciphered text would be difficult.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Coalesced Hashing”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following hashing technique is a combination of both separate chaining and open addressing techniques?
mcqs.explanation: Hashing is a searching technique, which takes constant time for operations like search, insert and delete. Coalesced hashing is one of the hashing techniques, which is a combination of both separate chaining and open addressing.

mcqs.question: By using which of the following data structure, the hash sequence is implemented within the hash table in coalesced hashing?
mcqs.explanation: In the hash table of coalesced hashing, the hash sequence is implemented as a linked list within the hash table. The next hash position is the next available position in the linked list. It takes extra space for the list.

mcqs.question: Which of the following fields are included in the hash table of coalesced hashing?
mcqs.explanation: The hash table of the coalesced hashing consists of three fields h(key), data and next. The h(key) stores all the values for a key of any particular hash function. Data field stores all the keys that need to be stored. Next points to the colliding elements.

mcqs.question: In the coalesced hashing, the collided element is placed in the first empty place of the hash table.
mcqs.explanation: Coalesced hashing is a combination of both separate chaining and open addressing. If a collision occurs, then just like linear probing, it tries to find the first empty place, but from the bottom of the hash table.

mcqs.question: Coalesced hashing is better than separate chaining.
mcqs.explanation: Coalesced hashing has the advantages of both separate chaining and linear probing. In coalesced hashing, the colliding elements are inserted in the hash table itself instead of creating a separate chain. Hence, it is better than separate chaining.

mcqs.question: A hash table contains 10 slots and uses coalesced hashing to resolve collisions. The hash function used is key % 10. If the values 67, 23, 45, 11, 95 are inserted in the table, in what location would the key value 95 be inserted?
mcqs.explanation: In the coalescing hashing, if a collision occurs then the element is added in the empty place from the bottom of the hash table. (67 % 10) = 7, 67 will be placed at slot 7. (23 % 10) = 3, 23 will be placed at slot 3. (45 % 10) = 5, 45 will be placed at slot 5. (11 % 10) = 1, 11 will be placed at slot 1. (95 % 10) = 5, slot 5 is already full, hence 95 will be inserted in the empty place from the bottom of the hash table that is 9.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best represents the time complexity for inserting an element in coalesced hashing?
mcqs.explanation: The best case for inserting an element in hashing occurs when we want to insert an element at a particular position, after calculating the hash value and that position is available. Hence, inserting an element takes constant time in the best case.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is the worst case time complexity for deleting an element in coalesced hashing?
mcqs.explanation: In coalesced hashing, if there occurs a collision in any slot, the element is added in the empty place from the bottom and it is mapped with the previous colliding element. When we want to delete an element, the worst case occurs when we have to scan the whole table for that element. Hence, in worst case it will take O(n) time.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Hamming Code”.

mcqs.question: The most common hamming codes are a generalized version of?
mcqs.explanation: The most common hamming codes generalize to form hamming(7, 4) code. It encodes four bits of data into seven bits by adding three parity bits.

mcqs.question: What is the minimal Hamming distance between any two correct codewords?
mcqs.explanation: Since we use a generalized version of Hamming(7, 4) code, the minimal hamming distance is 3. It cannot correct burst errors.

mcqs.question: Why do we require hamming codes?
mcqs.explanation: Hamming codes are used for the purpose of error detection and correction. It is also used for channel encoding and decoding. They are linear-error correcting codes.

mcqs.question: Hamming codes can be used for both single-bit error and burst error detection and correction.
mcqs.explanation: Hamming bits are suitable only for single-bit error detection and correction and two bit error detection. It is very unlikely to detect burst errors.

mcqs.question: Who invented Hamming codes?
mcqs.explanation: Richard W. Hamming invented hamming codes in Bell Telephone Laboratory to minimize the errors in punched card readers. Huffman invented huffman codes. Shannon invented Shannon-Fanno codes.

mcqs.question: What is the total block length ‘n’ of a Hamming code?
mcqs.explanation: Hamming codes are a class of binary linear codes, hence r>=2. For a hamming(7, 4) code, the block length ‘n’ is 2<sup>r</sup>-1 where r is the parity bit. Here, r=3.

mcqs.question: What is the message length ‘k’ of a Hamming(7,4) code?
mcqs.explanation: Hamming codes are a class of binary linear codes, hence r>=2. For a hamming(7,4) code, the message length ‘k’ is 2<sup>r</sup>-r-1 where r is the parity bit. Here, r=3.

mcqs.question: What is the rate of hamming codes?
mcqs.explanation: Rate of a hamming code is message length divided by block length (i.e.) 2<sup>r</sup>-r-1/2<sup>r</sup>-1 = 1-[r/(2<sup>r</sup>-1)]. It is the highest rate for a minimum distance of three.

mcqs.question: A two-out-of-five code consists of _________
mcqs.explanation: A two-out-of-five code consists of three 0s and two 1s. Hence, it contains ten possible combinations to represent digits from 0-9.

mcqs.question: Including a parity bit along with the data surely detects the errors.
mcqs.explanation: If error has occurred in a data string, parity will change inorder to indicate errors. However, if the error occurs in parity bit, the error goes undetected.

mcqs.question: ________ is the mechanism of sending data bits multiple times to ensure consistency.
mcqs.explanation: Repeating data bits multiple times is done to ensure consistency. If the data bit to be sent is a 1, a n=3 repetition code will send 111. If the bits are not the same, an error has occurred.

mcqs.question: An Extended hamming code is also called as __________
mcqs.explanation: An Extended Hamming code is also called as SECDED (Single Error Correction Double Error Detection). The most popular codes are (72, 64) code and (127,120) code.

mcqs.question: What is the code rate of a repetition Hamming code (3, 1)?
mcqs.explanation: The code rate of a repetition hamming code is the second number divided by the first number. Here, it is 1/3.

mcqs.question: For a hamming code of parity bit m=8, what is the total bits and data bits?
mcqs.explanation:
Total bits are computed as, 2m-1 = 28-1 =255.
Data bits are computed as 2m-m-1= 28-8-1= 247.

mcqs.question: What is the rate of the hamming code of parity bit m=8?
mcqs.explanation:
For a hamming code of parity bit 8, total bits = 255 and data bits = 247. Rate= data bits/ total bits
= 247/255 = 0.969 = 0.97.

links.text: P, NP, NP-hard, NP-complete Complexity Classes
links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “P, NP, NP-hard, NP-complete Complexity Classes”.

mcqs.question: The worst-case efficiency of solving a problem in polynomial time is?
mcqs.explanation: The worst-case efficiency of solving an problem in polynomial time is O(p(n)) where p(n) is the polynomial time of input size.

mcqs.question: Problems that can be solved in polynomial time are known as?
mcqs.explanation: Problems that can be solved in polynomial time are known as tractable. Problems that cannot be solved in polynomial time are intractable.

mcqs.question: The sum and composition of two polynomials are always polynomials.
mcqs.explanation: One of the properties of polynomial functions states that the sum and composition of two polynomials are always polynomials.

mcqs.question: _________ is the class of decision problems that can be solved by non-deterministic polynomial algorithms.
mcqs.explanation: NP  problems are called as non-deterministic polynomial problems. They are a class of decision problems that can be solved using NP algorithms.

mcqs.question: Problems that cannot be solved by any algorithm are called?
mcqs.explanation: Problems cannot be solved by any algorithm are called undecidable problems. Problems that can be solved in polynomial time are called Tractable problems.

mcqs.question: The Euler’s circuit problem can be solved in?
mcqs.explanation: Mathematically, the run time of Euler’s circuit problem is determined to be O(N<sup>2</sup>).

mcqs.question: To which class does the Euler’s circuit problem belong?
mcqs.explanation: Euler’s circuit problem can be solved in polynomial time. It can be solved in O(N<sup>2</sup>).

mcqs.question: Halting problem is an example for?
mcqs.explanation: Halting problem by Alan Turing cannot be solved by any algorithm. Hence, it is undecidable.

mcqs.question: How many stages of procedure does a non-deterministic algorithm consist of?
mcqs.explanation: A non-deterministic algorithm is a two-stage procedure- guessing stage and verification stage.

mcqs.question: A non-deterministic algorithm is said to be non-deterministic polynomial if the time-efficiency of its verification stage is polynomial.
mcqs.explanation: One of the properties of NP class problems states that A non-deterministic algorithm is said to be non-deterministic polynomial if the time-efficiency of its verification stage is polynomial.

mcqs.question: How many conditions have to be met if an NP- complete problem is polynomially reducible?
mcqs.explanation: A function t that maps all yes instances of decision problems D1 and D2 and t should be computed in polynomial time are the two conditions.

mcqs.question: To which of the following class does a CNF-satisfiability problem belong?
mcqs.explanation: The CNF satisfiability problem belongs to NP complete class. It deals with Boolean expressions.

mcqs.question: How many steps are required to prove that a decision problem is NP complete?
mcqs.explanation: First, the problem should be NP. Next, it should be proved that every problem in NP is reducible to the problem in question in polynomial time.

mcqs.question: Which of the following problems is not NP complete?
mcqs.explanation: Hamiltonian circuit, bin packing, partition problems are NP complete problems. Halting problem is an undecidable problem.

mcqs.question: The choice of polynomial class has led to the development of an extensive theory called ________
mcqs.explanation: An extensive theory called computational complexity seeks to classify problems according to their inherent difficulty.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Hamiltonian Path Problem”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following algorithm can be used to solve the Hamiltonian path problem efficiently?
mcqs.explanation: The Hamiltonian path problem can be solved efficiently using branch and bound approach. It can also be solved using a backtracking approach.

mcqs.question: The problem of finding a path in a graph that visits every vertex exactly once is called?
mcqs.explanation: Hamiltonian path problem is a problem of finding a path in a graph that visits every node exactly once whereas Hamiltonian cycle problem is finding a cycle in a graph.

mcqs.question: Hamiltonian path problem is _________
mcqs.explanation: Hamiltonian path problem is found to be NP complete. Hamiltonian cycle problem is also an NP- complete problem.

mcqs.question: There is no existing relationship between a Hamiltonian path problem and Hamiltonian circuit problem.
mcqs.explanation: There is a relationship between Hamiltonian path problem and Hamiltonian circuit problem. The Hamiltonian path in graph G is equal to Hamiltonian cycle in graph H under certain conditions.

mcqs.question: Which of the following problems is similar to that of a Hamiltonian path problem?
mcqs.explanation: Hamiltonian path problem is similar to that of a travelling salesman problem since both the problem traverses all the nodes in a graph exactly once.

mcqs.question: Who formulated the first ever algorithm for solving the Hamiltonian path problem?
mcqs.explanation: The first ever problem to solve the Hamiltonian path was the enumerative algorithm formulated by Martello.

mcqs.question: In what time can the Hamiltonian path problem can be solved using dynamic programming?
mcqs.explanation: Using dynamic programming, the time taken to solve the Hamiltonian path problem is mathematically found to be O(N<sup>2</sup> 2<sup>N</sup>).

mcqs.question: In graphs, in which all vertices have an odd degree, the number of Hamiltonian cycles through any fixed edge is always even.
mcqs.explanation: According to a handshaking lemma, in graphs, in which all vertices have an odd degree, the number of Hamiltonian cycles through any fixed edge is always even.

mcqs.question: Who invented the inclusion-exclusion principle to solve the Hamiltonian path problem?
mcqs.explanation: Andreas Bjorklund came up with the inclusion-exclusion principle to reduce the counting of number of Hamiltonian cycles.

mcqs.question: For a graph of degree three, in what time can a Hamiltonian path be found?
mcqs.explanation: For a graph of maximum degree three, a Hamiltonian path can be found in time O(0.251<sup>n</sup>).

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity for finding a Hamiltonian path for a graph having N vertices (using permutation)?
mcqs.explanation: For a graph having N vertices traverse the permutations in N! iterations and it traverses the permutations to see if adjacent vertices are connected or not takes N iterations (i.e.) O(N! * N).

mcqs.question: How many Hamiltonian paths does the following graph have?
mcqs.explanation: The above graph has only one Hamiltonian path that is from a-b-c-d-e.

mcqs.question: How many Hamiltonian paths does the following graph have?
mcqs.explanation: The above graph has no Hamiltonian paths. That is, we cannot traverse the graph with meeting vertices exactly once.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Subset Sum Problem”.

mcqs.question: Under what condition any set A will be a subset of B?

options.a: a) if all elements of set B are also present in set A
options.b: b) if all elements of set A are also present in set B
options.c: c) if A contains more elements than B
options.d: d) if B contains more elements than A

mcqs.answer: b) if all elements of set A are also present in set B
mcqs.explanation: Any set A will be called a subset of set B if all elements of set A are also present in set B. So in such a case set A will be a part of set B.

mcqs.question: What is a subset sum problem?

options.a: a) finding a subset of a set that has sum of elements equal to a given number
options.b: b) checking for the presence of a subset that has sum of elements equal to a given number and printing true or false based on the result
options.c: c) finding the sum of elements present in a set
options.d: d) finding the sum of all the subsets of a set

mcqs.answer: b) checking for the presence of a subset that has sum of elements equal to a given number and printing true or false based on the result
mcqs.explanation: In subset sum problem check for the presence of a subset that has sum of elements equal to a given number. If such a subset is present then we print true otherwise false.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about the time complexity of the recursive solution of the subset sum problem?

options.a: a) It has an exponential time complexity
options.b: b) It has a linear time complexity
options.c: c) It has a logarithmic time complexity
options.d: d) it has a time complexity of O(n2)

mcqs.answer: a) It has an exponential time complexity
mcqs.explanation: Subset sum problem has both recursive as well as dynamic programming solution. The recursive solution has an exponential time complexity as it will require to check for all subsets in worst case.

mcqs.question: What is the worst case time complexity of dynamic programming solution of the subset sum problem(sum=given subset sum)?
mcqs.explanation: Subset sum problem has both recursive as well as dynamic programming solution. The dynamic programming solution has a time complexity of O(n*sum) as it as a nested loop with limits from 1 to n and 1 to sum respectively.

mcqs.question: Subset sum problem is an example of NP-complete problem.
mcqs.explanation: Subset sum problem takes exponential time when we implement a recursive solution. Subset sum problem is known to be a part of NP complete problems.

mcqs.question: Recursive solution of subset sum problem is faster than dynamic problem solution in terms of time complexity.
mcqs.explanation: The recursive solution to subset sum problem takes exponential time complexity whereas the dynamic programming solution takes polynomial time complexity. So dynamic programming solution is faster in terms of time complexity.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true about subset sum problem?

options.a: a) the recursive solution has a time complexity of O(2n)
options.b: b) there is no known solution that takes polynomial time
options.c: c) the recursive solution is slower than dynamic programming solution
options.d: d) the dynamic programming solution has a time complexity of O(n log n)

mcqs.answer: d) the dynamic programming solution has a time complexity of O(n log n)
mcqs.explanation: Recursive solution of subset sum problem is slower than dynamic problem solution in terms of time complexity. Dynamic programming solution has a time complexity of O(n*sum).

mcqs.question: Which of the following should be the base case for the recursive solution of subset sum problem?
mcqs.explanation: The base case condition defines the point at which the program should stop recursion. In this case we need to make sure that, the sum does not become 0 and there should be elements left in our array for recursion to happen.

mcqs.question:
What will be the output for the following code? 
#include <stdio.h> 
bool func(int arr[], int n, int sum) 
{ 
    if (sum == 0) 
	return true; 
    if (n == 0 && sum != 0) 
	return false; 
    if (arr[n-1] > sum) 
	return func(arr, n-1, sum); 
 
    return func(arr, n-1, sum) || func(arr, n-1, sum-arr[n-1]); 
} 
int main() 
{ 
    int arr[] = {4,6, 12, 2}; 
    int sum = 12; 
    int n = sizeof(arr)/sizeof(arr[0]); 
    if (func(arr, n, sum) == true) 
	printf("true"); 
    else
	printf("false"); 
    return 0; 
}
mcqs.explanation: The given code represents the recursive approach of solving the subset sum problem. The output for the code will be true if any subset is found to have sum equal to the desired sum, otherwise false will be printed.

mcqs.question:
What will be the output for the following code? 
#include <stdio.h> 
bool func(int arr[], int n, int sum) 
{ 
	bool subarr[n+1][sum+1]; 
	for (int i = 0; i <= n; i++) 
	subarr[i][0] = true; 
	for (int i = 1; i <= sum; i++) 
	subarr[0][i] = false; 
	for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) 
	{ 
	    for (int j = 1; j <= sum; j++) 
	    { 
		if(j<arr[i-1]) 
		subarr[i][j] = subarr[i-1][j]; 
		if (j >= arr[i-1]) 
		subarr[i][j] = subarr[i-1][j] || 
		subarr[i - 1][j-arr[i-1]]; 
	    } 
	} 
	return subarr[n][sum]; 
} 
 
int main() 
{ 
    int arr[] = {3, 3, 4, 4, 7}; 
    int sum = 5; 
    int n = sizeof(arr)/sizeof(arr[0]); 
    if (func(arr, n, sum) == true) 
	printf("true"); 
    else
	printf("false"); 
    return 0; 
}
mcqs.explanation: The given code represents the dynamic programming approach of solving the subset sum problem. The output for the code will be true if any subset is found to have sum equal to the desired sum, otherwise false will be printed.

mcqs.question:
What will be the worst case time complexity for the following code? 
#include <stdio.h> 
bool func(int arr[], int n, int sum) 
{ 
    if (sum == 0) 
	return true; 
    if (n == 0 && sum != 0) 
	return false; 
    if (arr[n-1] > sum) 
	return func(arr, n-1, sum); 
    return func(arr, n-1, sum) || func(arr, n-1, sum-arr[n-1]); 
} 
int main() 
{ 
    int arr[] = {4,6, 12, 2}; 
    int sum = 12; 
    int n = sizeof(arr)/sizeof(arr[0]); 
    if (func(arr, n, sum) == true) 
	printf("true"); 
    else
	printf("false"); 
    return 0;

mcqs.explanation: The given code represents the recursive approach solution of the subset sum problem. It has an exponential time complexity as it will require to check for all subsets in the worst case. It is equal to O(2<sup>n</sup>).

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Vertex Cover Problem”.

mcqs.question: Vertex covering can be a good approach to which type of the problems?

options.a: a) Where all the vertex in the graph need to be included
options.b: b) Where all the edges in the graph need to be included
options.c: c) Only half edges in the graph need to be included
options.d: d) Only half of the total vertices need to be included

mcqs.answer: b) Where all the edges in the graph need to be included
mcqs.explanation: A vertex cover is a subset of the vertex set of a given graph G, such that every edge in G is incident to at least one endpoint in the set. Hence, the vertex covering can be a good approach, where all the edges in the graph need to be included.

mcqs.question: The greedy algorithm can find a minimal vertex cover in polynomial time for which among the following?
mcqs.explanation: Despite the NP-completeness of the problems, the konigs theorem allows the bipartite vertex problem to be solved in polynomial time, for bipartite graphs. Hence, the greedy algorithm can find a minimum vertex cover in polynomial time for bipartite graphs.

mcqs.question: What is the minimum vertex cover for the following graph given below?
mcqs.explanation: According to the given graph, the greedy approach can be followed: First, find a vertex v with maximum degree. Add the vertex to the solution and remove the vertex and its incident edges from the graph. Repeat for all the edges present in the graph. Hence, we can observe that node A has a maximum degree, so it can cover maximum edges. It covers the edge {A, B}, {A, D} and {A, E} and the rest {B, C} can be covered by including B or C in the resultant set. Hence, {A, B} or {A, C} is the minimum vertex cover for the following graph

options.b: b) add every edge incident on u

mcqs.answer: a) remove every edge incident on either u or v

While E is not empty, pick any random edge from the set E and add it to the resultant set A. If any edge is incident on either u or v, remove that edge and return the resultant set.

mcqs.question: In a complete bipartite graph K<sub>m, n</sub>, the minimum vertex cover is of the size max{m, n}.
mcqs.explanation: In a complete bipartite graph Km, n, all the vertices of one side are connected to all the vertices of another side. Hence, the minimum number of edges can be covered by selecting the minimum number of vertices present on any of the sides.

mcqs.question: Consider a simple graph G with 18 vertices. What will be the size of the maximum independent set of G, if the size of the minimum vertex cover of G is 10?
mcqs.explanation: By removing the vertex cover vertices from the graph it results in an isolated graph, and so the remaining vertices would be the independent set in the original graph. Hence, size of maximum independent set = 18 – 10 = 8.

mcqs.question: If the complement of a graph is an independent set, then the set of vertices itself is a vertex cover.
mcqs.explanation: An independent set is a vertex subset such that no edge exists between any two in the subset. Whereas a vertex subset is a vertex cover if and only if its complement is an independent set. Hence, the given statement is true.

mcqs.question: Which among the following problem uses the vertex cover approach?
mcqs.explanation: A traveling salesperson problem refers to the problem where salespersons visit all the cities to sell their goods. They know the distance between all the cities. Hence, to decide the order in which they should visit the cities to minimize their travel time, a vertex cover approach can be used.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Independent Set Problem”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following refers to the set of non-adjacent vertices?
mcqs.explanation: In a graph G with V vertices and E edges, there exists a set of vertices, in which no two vertices are adjacent. This set of non-adjacent vertices is called an independent set i.e. no two vertices share a common edge.

mcqs.question: Which of the following refers to the independence number of a graph?

options.a: a) Smallest size of a maximal independent set
options.b: b) Largest size of a minimal independent set
options.c: c) Smallest size of a minimal independent set
options.d: d) Largest size of a maximal independent set

mcqs.answer: d) Largest size of a maximal independent set
mcqs.explanation: In a graph G=(V, E) a subset S is an independent set if no two vertices in the S are adjacent. The independence number of graph G is the cardinality of the largest size of an independent set of vertices.

options.b: b) temp to true and break

options.d: d) temp to false and continue

mcqs.answer: c) temp to false and break
mcqs.explanation: The given pseudocode is for solving the independent set problem. First, initialize a temporary variable as true. Now, check that each pair of vertices belong to the set are adjacent or not, by checking if there exists any edge between them.

mcqs.question: What is the maximal independent set for the graph given below?
mcqs.explanation: The maximal independent set S of a graph G contains the set of vertices, such that no two vertices should be adjacent and no vertex can be further added to the set. If we start with vertex A, we can’t select vertex B. Select vertex C and D, hence we can’t select E. Now, select any vertex from F and G according to the given options. Hence, the set contains the vertex {A, C, D, F}.

mcqs.question: In a graph, an independent set is maximal if no further vertex can be added to the stay independent.
mcqs.explanation: In a given graph G=(V, E), an independent set of G is a subset S of the vertices present in the graph G, such that no two vertices of S are adjacent in G. Hence, a maximal independent set of graph G is a set where it is impossible to add another vertex and stay independent.

mcqs.question: What is the independence number of the graph given below?
mcqs.explanation: The independence number of the graph is given by the largest size of an independent set. If we start with vertex A, we can’t select vertex B. Select vertex C and vertex E. The maximal independent set of the graph will be {A, C, E}. Hence, the independence number of the graph is 3.

mcqs.question: What is the size of the smallest maximal independent set of a chain of 7 nodes?
mcqs.explanation: In a graph G, a set of vertices is an independent set if there is no common edge between them. A maximal independent set of graph G is a set where it is impossible to add another vertex to make it independent. Here, we can select the 2nd, 5th and 7th node to get the smallest maximal independent set (1—2—3—4—5—6—7). Hence, the size of smallest maximal independent set of a chain of 7 nodes is 3.

To check whether the given subset of vertices of a given graph is an independent set, we need to check that all the vertices present in the set are non-adjacent. This can be done by confirming that they don’t share any edge. This can be performed in polynomial time. Hence, the time complexity is O(V + E).

mcqs.question: A dominating set of graph G, is the subset D of vertices, if each vertex not in D is adjacent to how many vertices?
mcqs.explanation: In a graph G=(V, E), a dominating set is subset D, such that if we take any vertex from the set of vertices, either that vertex belongs to D or its adjacent belongs to D. Hence, if each vertex not in D, is adjacent to at least one vertex of D.

mcqs.question: Which of the following refers to the domination number of a graph?

options.b: b) Largest size of minimal dominating set
options.c: c) Smallest size of minimal dominating set
options.d: d) Largest size of maximal dominating set

mcqs.answer: c) Smallest size of minimal dominating set
mcqs.explanation: In a graph G=(V, E) a subset S is a dominating set if each vertex V of G is adjacent to some vertex u!= v, of S. The domination number of G, is the cardinality of the smallest size of a minimal dominating set.

options.a: a) delete all the edges connected to X
options.b: b) add all the edge connected to X

mcqs.answer: a) delete all the edges connected to X
mcqs.explanation: The given pseudocode is an approximation algorithm for solving the dominating set problem. First, initialize an empty set D, which will store the results. Pick up any edge connecting to the vertices X and Y. Add one vertex between X and Y to the set D and delete all the edges connected to it. Repeat this for all the edges and return the resultant set D to get the dominating set of the graph.

mcqs.question: What is the minimal dominating set for the graph given below?
mcqs.explanation: The minimal dominating set D of a graph G contains the smallest number of vertices, such that the vertex belongs to D or its adjacent belongs to D. Following the greedy approach, select the vertex with the maximum number of the degree to cover maximum vertices i.e. E. E is adjacent to the vertex C, B, D, F, G. Hence, along with E, A can be added to the dominating set D to cover all the vertices of the graph. The minimal dominating sets of the graph are {A, E}, {B, E}, {B, F} and {B, G}.

mcqs.question: In a graph, a maximal independent set is also a dominating set.
mcqs.explanation: In a given graph G=(V, E), an independent set of G is a subset S of the vertices present in the graph G, such that no two vertices of S are adjacent in G. Hence, a maximal independent set of graph G is also a minimal dominating set.

mcqs.question: What is the domination number of the graph given below?

Following the greedy approach for the given graph, vertices A and B have the maximum degree and cover all the adjacent vertices of the graph. The minimal dominating set of the graph will be {A, B}. mcqs.question: All the graphs have a dominating set of vertices.
mcqs.explanation: A dominating set is subset D, such that if we take any vertex from the set of vertices, either that vertex belongs to D or its adjacent belongs to D. The graphs with a minimum degree of k – 1, have a k-tuple dominating set, only these graphs have a k-dominating set.

mcqs.question: What is the minimum dominating set of the binary tree given below?
mcqs.explanation: To find the minimum dominating set of a binary tree, a dynamic programming approach can be used. First of all, choose the node and mark its children which are covered. Then check and update if its children are covered or not. Do this for all the nodes. Hence, if we select node B and node C, they cover all the nodes except H and I. links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Set Partition Problem”.

mcqs.question: What is meant by the power set of a set?
mcqs.explanation: Power set of a set is defined as the set of all subsets. Ex- if there is a set S={1,3} then power set of set S will be P={{},{1},{3}{1,3}}.

mcqs.question: What is the set partition problem?

options.a: a) finding a subset of a set that has sum of elements equal to a given number
options.b: b) checking for the presence of a subset that has sum of elements equal to a given number
options.c: c) checking whether the set can be divided into two subsets of with equal sum of elements and printing true or false based on the result
options.d: d) finding subsets with equal sum of elements

mcqs.answer: c) checking whether the set can be divided into two subsets of with equal sum of elements and printing true or false based on the result
mcqs.explanation: In set partition problem we check whether a set can be divided into 2 subsets such that the sum of elements in each subset is equal. If such subsets are present then we print true otherwise false.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about the time complexity of the recursive solution of set partition problem?

options.a: a) It has an exponential time complexity
options.b: b) It has a linear time complexity
options.c: c) It has a logarithmic time complexity
options.d: d) it has a time complexity of O(n2)

mcqs.answer: a) It has an exponential time complexity
mcqs.explanation: Set partition problem has both recursive as well as dynamic programming solution. The recursive solution has an exponential time complexity as it will require to check for all subsets in the worst case.

mcqs.question: What is the worst case time complexity of dynamic programming solution of set partition problem(sum=sum of set elements)?
mcqs.explanation: Set partition problem has both recursive as well as dynamic programming solution. The dynamic programming solution has a time complexity of O(n*sum) as it as a nested loop with limits from 1 to n and 1 to sum respectively.

mcqs.question: Set partition problem is an example of NP complete problem.
mcqs.explanation: Set partition problem takes exponential time when we implement a recursive solution. Set partition problem is known to be a part of NP complete problems.

mcqs.question: Recursive solution of Set partition problem is faster than dynamic problem solution in terms of time complexity.
mcqs.explanation: The recursive solution to set partition problem takes exponential time complexity whereas the dynamic programming solution takes polynomial time complexity. So dynamic programming solution is faster in terms of time complexity.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true about set partition problem?

options.b: b) there is no known solution that takes polynomial time

mcqs.answer: d) the dynamic programming solution has a time complexity of O(n log n)
mcqs.explanation: Recursive solution of set partition problem is slower than dynamic problem solution in terms of time complexity. Dynamic programming solution has a time complexity of O(n*sum).

bool func (int arr[], int n) 
{

	if (sum%2 != 0)

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Optimal Page Replacement Algorithm”.

mcqs.question: __________ has the lowest fault rate of all the page replacement algorithms.
mcqs.explanation: Optimal page replacement algorithm has the lowest fault rate as it has the knowledge of all the pages beforehand.

mcqs.question: Optimal page replacement algorithm is also called as __________
mcqs.explanation: Optimal page replacement algorithm is also called a Clairvoyant replacement algorithm or Belady’s optimal replacement algorithm.

mcqs.question: In a optimal page replacement algorithm, when a page is to be replaced, which of the following pages is chosen?

options.c: c) Frequently occurred page in the future
options.d: d) Not frequently occurred page in the future

mcqs.answer: d) Not frequently occurred page in the future
mcqs.explanation: The page which doesn’t occur more frequently in the future is chosen to be replaced with the page in the frame.

mcqs.question: A page that is not going to be used for the next 7 seconds will be swapped out over a page that is going to be used within the next 0.7 seconds.
mcqs.explanation: In an optimal page replacement algorithm, the page that is to be used later in the future is swapped out over a page that is to be used immediately.

mcqs.question: Analysis of the optimal paging problem has been done through___________
mcqs.explanation: Analysis of the optimal paging algorithm is done through an online algorithm. Efficiency is calculated through amortized analysis.

mcqs.question: Optimal page replacement algorithm is implemented in __________

options.c: c) In any kind of operating system

mcqs.explanation: Optimal page replacement algorithm is used in special-purpose operating system because it is impossible to compute time before which a page is used.

mcqs.question: Optimal page replacement algorithm is said to satisfy __________
mcqs.explanation: Optimal page replacement algorithm is said to satisfy the stack algorithm. It is also called as inclusion property.

mcqs.question: In a stack algorithm, the set of pages in a k-frame memory is always a subset of pages in a __________ frame memory.
mcqs.explanation: Stack algorithm is satisfied if the set of pages in a k-frame memory is always a subset of pages in a k+1 frame memory.

mcqs.question: Which page replacement strategy uses referenced bits and modified bits to replace the page?
mcqs.explanation: The not recently used algorithm is one of the page replacement algorithms. Page replacement algorithms in operating systems are used to decide which page should be evicted to make room for the upcoming pages. Not recently used algorithm is a page replacement strategy that uses referenced bits and modified bits to replace the page.

mcqs.question: Not recently used page replacement algorithm uses a counter.
mcqs.explanation: The not frequently used algorithm is a page replacement algorithm that uses a counter to keep track of how frequently the page has been used. Here, the page which has the lowest count may be swapped out. The not recently used algorithm doesn’t use a counter, it uses only referenced bit and modified bit.

mcqs.question: In the not recently used algorithm, what do the R bits and M bits refer to?

options.b: b) R – not referenced, M – modified
options.c: c) R – read/write, M – not modified
options.d: d) R – referenced, M – not modified

mcqs.explanation: After every memory reference, the bits are set by hardware but are cleared only by the software. The R bit is set when the page is referenced by performing read or write. M bit is set when the page is modified.

mcqs.question: Consider the given page reference string 3, 1, 0, 2, 1, 5, 6, 2, 8, 6, 9, 1. How many page faults will occur if the program has 4-page frames available to it and it uses the not recently used algorithm?

When 5 came, 3 wasn’t used recently, replace it → 1 page fault When 6 came, 0 wasn’t used recently, replace it → 1 page fault 2 is already present → 0 page fault When 8 came, 1 wasn’t used recently, replace it → 1 page fault 6 is already present → 0 page fault When 9 came, 5 wasn’t used recently, replace it → 1 page fault When 1 came, 2 wasn’t used recently, replace it → 1 page fault Hence, total 9 page faults.

mcqs.question: In the not recently used algorithm, which page is to be replaced when the new page comes in?
mcqs.explanation: Not recently used page replacement algorithm, as the name suggests, evicts the page that hasn’t been used recently. Whenever a page is referred, it is marked by setting a referenced bit. It randomly picks up the page from the lowest numbered nonempty class. Hence, the page which is not referenced and not modified will be replaced first.

mcqs.question: Consider the given page reference string 2, 6, 1, 2, 0, 1, 5, 3. What will be the page fault rate, if the program has 3-page frames available to it and it uses the not recently used algorithm?

When 0 came, 6 wasn’t used recently, replace it → 1 page fault 1 is already present → 0 page fault When 5 came, 2 wasn’t used recently, replace it → 1 page fault When 3 came, 0 wasn’t used recently, replace it → 1 page fault Total 9 page faults. Now, page fault rate = page fault / total pages = 6 / 8 = 3 / 4.

mcqs.question: The page which is referenced and not modified is less important than the page which is modified but not referenced.
mcqs.explanation: In the not recently used algorithm, instead of removing the page that is recently used, we remove a modified page, which is not referenced in one clock tick. Hence, a page that is referenced and not modified is more important than the page which is modified but not referenced.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is a disadvantage of the not recently used algorithm?

options.b: b) It uses a queue data structure for implementation

mcqs.explanation: In the not recently used algorithm to decide which page is to be evicted when the new page comes in, we have to scan through the reference bits and modified bits. Hence, the performance is not that good, as it takes time to classify.

mcqs.question: ________  is a typical online problem from the competitive analysis to determine the optimal solution.
mcqs.explanation: Page replacement is a typical online problem from the competitive analysis. They determine which pages to page out or write to disk.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the simplest page replacement algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: FIFO is the simplest page replacement algorithm since LRU and optimal replacement algorithms require past and future data patterns respectively.

mcqs.question: __________ algorithm associates with each page the time when the page was brought into memory.
mcqs.explanation: FIFO algorithm associates with each page the time when the page was brought into memory. The new page is inserted at the tail of the queue.

mcqs.question: As the number of frames available increases, the number of page faults decreases.
mcqs.explanation: One of the rules of the page replacement algorithm is that, as the number of frames available increases, the number of page faults decreases.

mcqs.question: Which of the following page replacement algorithms return the minimum number of page faults?
mcqs.explanation: Though FIFO is the simplest of all algorithms, optimal page replacement algorithm returns the minimum number of page faults.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the main drawback of FIFO page replacement algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: The main drawback of FIFO page replacement algorithm is that it reduces the level of multiprogramming and also causes Belady’s anomaly.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is required to determine the number of page faults in FIFO?

mcqs.question: In a FIFO algorithm, when a page is to be replaced, which of the following page is chosen?

options.c: c) Frequently occurred page in past
options.d: d) Frequently occurred page in future

mcqs.explanation: In FIFO page replacement algorithm, when a page is to be replaced, the oldest page is chosen and replaced at the tail of the queue.

mcqs.question: The cost required to execute a FIFO algorithm is expensive.
mcqs.explanation: The cost of a FIFO algorithm is cheap and intuitive and it is used in poor practical applications.

mcqs.question: FIFO algorithm is used by __________ operating system.

mcqs.question: What is the competitive analysis of the FIFO algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: The competitive analysis of a FIFO algorithm is mathematically found to be k/(k-h+1) where k and h are some constants used in page replacement and always, h<=k.

mcqs.question: Under which of the following scenarios is page replacement algorithm required?

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Least Recently Used Algorithm (LRU)”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a page replacement algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: A page replacement algorithm in operating systems, is used to decide which page should be evicted when the new page comes in. The least recently used (LRU) algorithm is a page replacement algorithm, which evicts the page that hasn’t been used for the longest time.

mcqs.question: Which type of exception is raised by computer hardware when a code tries to access a block of memory that is not stored in physical memory?
mcqs.explanation: A page fault is an error that occurs when a program requests a page in the main memory and the page cannot be found at the requested location. Page faults are indicators, that tell you to increase the amount of memory available to processes.

mcqs.question: Which data structures can be used to implement least recently used cache?

options.a: a) Doubly linked list and a hash map
options.b: b) Singly linked list and a hash map
options.c: c) Triply linked list and a hash map
options.d: d) Unrolled linked list and a hash map

mcqs.answer: a) Doubly linked list and a hash map
mcqs.explanation: Least recently used cache is implemented by pairing a doubly linked list with a hash map. Hash map holds the key and refers to the nodes of the linked list. When the cache is full, this caching strategy evicts the elements which are not used for the longest period of time, to make room for new elements.

mcqs.question: Consider the given page reference string 6, 1, 0, 3, 1, 2, 1, 5, 3, 2, 0, 1, 3. How many page faults will occur if the program has 4-page frames available to it and it uses the least recently used algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: All the slots are empty initially, 6 1 0 3 are allocated → 4 page faults. 1 is already present → 0 page fault. When 2 came, the least recently used was 6, hence 2 will take its place → 1 page fault. 1 is already present → 0 page fault. When 5 came, the least recently used was 0, hence 5 will take its place → 1 page fault. 3 is already present → 0 page fault. 2 is already present → 0 page fault. When 0 came, the least recently used was 1, hence 0 will take its place → 1 page fault. When 1 came, the least recently used was 5, hence 1 will take its place → 1 page fault. 3 is already present → 0 page fault. Hence, total 8 page faults.

mcqs.question: In the least recently used algorithm, if the current page doesn’t exist in the set then it is replaced with the recently used page.
mcqs.explanation: In the least recently used algorithm, the page that has not been used for the longest period of time is evicted. It looks for the pages which are already page faulted. Hence, if the current page doesn’t exist in the set, it is replaced by the page that hasn’t been used for the longest time.

mcqs.question:
What will be the output of the following code in java? 
import java.util.ArrayList;
public class LRU {	
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int page_frame = 3;
        int page_ref_string[] = {1, 2, 4, 1, 0, 3, 2, 0, 5, 4};
	ArrayList<Integer> s=new ArrayList<>(page_frame);
	int count=0;
	int page_faults=0;
	for(int i:page_ref_string)
	{
	    if(!s.contains(i))
	    {
	    if(s.size()==page_frame)
	    {
	        s.remove(0);
		s.add(page_frame-1,i);
	    }
	    else
		s.add(count,i);
		page_faults++;
		++count;
	    }
	    else
	    {
		s.remove((Object)i);
		s.add(s.size(),i);		
	    }
	}
		System.out.println(page_faults);
    }
}

The following java code is the implementation of the least recently used algorithm. All the slots are empty initially, 1 2 4 are allocated → 3 page faults. 1 is already present → 0 page fault. When 0 came, the least recently used was 2, hence 0 will take its place → 1 page fault. When 3 came, the least recently used was 4, hence 3 will take its place → 1 page fault. When 2 came, the least recently used was 1, hence 2 will take its place → 1 page fault 0 is already present → 0 page fault. When 5 came, the least recently used was 3, hence 5 will take its place → 1 page fault. When 4 came, the least recently used was 2, hence 1 will take its place → 1 page fault. Hence, total 8-page faults.
Output: 8

mcqs.question: Least recently used cache has the space complexity of O(n).
mcqs.explanation: Least recently used cache can be implemented by pairing a doubly linked list with a hash map. For tracking n items in the least recently used cache, a hash map holding n elements and a linked list of length n is required. Hence, it has the space complexity of O(n).

mcqs.question: Which of the following best represents the time complexity to access an item in the least recently used cache?
mcqs.explanation: In the least recently used cache, the elements are stored from most recently used to least recently used. It takes constant time to access both the elements. Hence, it takes O(1) time to access an element in the least recently used cache.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is an application of the least recently used algorithm?

The least recently used is one of the page replacement algorithms which is used to reduce the number of page faults.

mcqs.question: Which among the following algorithms can be used to decide which page should be replaced when the new page comes in?
mcqs.explanation: The page replacement algorithm in operating systems, is used to decide which page should be evicted when the new page comes in. The basic idea of these algorithms is to reduce the number of page faults that occur.

mcqs.question: The random page replacement algorithm may suffer from Belady’s anomaly.
mcqs.explanation: Belady’s anomaly depicts that with the increase in the number of page frames, the number of page faults also increases. It is in context with the FIFO page replacement policy. mcqs.question: The random page replacement algorithm fares better than which of the following algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: The random page replaces a page randomly from the frame. Here, we cannot predict the future at all. The best case, worst case and average case are all same for this algorithm. It is also easy to implement. Hence, it fares better than FIFO.

mcqs.question: Consider the given page reference string 0, 1, 3, 7, 1, 7, 0, 3, 6, 8. How many page faults will occur if the program has 4-page frames available to it and it uses the random page replacement algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: All the slots are empty initially, 0 1 3 7 are allocated → 4 page faults. 1 is already present → 0 page fault. 7 is already present → 0 page fault. 0 is already present → 0 page fault. 3 is already present → 0 page fault. When 6 came, randomly replace it with any of the page → 1 page fault. When 8 came, randomly replace it with any of the page → 1 page fault. Hence, total 6 page faults.

mcqs.question: In the random page replacement algorithm, if the current page doesn’t exist in the frame then it is replaced with which of the following page?

options.d: d) The first page of the frame

mcqs.explanation: In the random page replacement algorithm, as the name suggests replaces any random page from the set. Hence, if the current page doesn’t exist in the set, then it is replaced with any random page.

options.d: d) the first page of the frame

mcqs.explanation: In the random page replacement algorithm, while traversing the pages, if the pages are less than the capacity, keep adding the pages until the set reaches the capacity. Increment the page fault. If the current page is present in the set, gives 0 page fault. Hence, do nothing, else replace the page randomly with any page of the set and increment the page fault.

mcqs.question: Random page replacement algorithm may behave like any other page replacement algorithms.
mcqs.explanation: In the random page replacement algorithm, if the page doesn’t exist in the set then it is replaced by any of the pages from the set. Hence, it may behave like FIFO, LIFO, LRU, Optimal, etc. any of the page replacement algorithm.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of random page replacement algorithm?

options.a: a) It replaces the page that has been present in the main memory for the longest
options.b: b) It uses a queue data structure for implementation
options.c: c) It eliminates the overhead cost of tracking page reference

mcqs.answer: c) It eliminates the overhead cost of tracking page reference
mcqs.explanation: In FIFO page replacement algorithm, the page that has been in the memory for the longest amount of time is replaced and it uses queue data structure for implementation. Optimal page replacement algorithm cannot be implemented because the future cannot be predicted. In random page replacement algorithm, the memory page is replaced randomly and hence we do not need to track the page reference.

links.context: This set of Data Structure Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Topological Sort”.

mcqs.question: Topological sort can be applied to which of the following graphs?
mcqs.explanation: Every Directed Acyclic Graph has one or more topological ordering whereas Cyclic and Undirected graphs can’t be ordered topologically.

mcqs.question: Most Efficient Time Complexity of Topological Sorting is? (V – number of vertices, E – number of edges)
mcqs.explanation: The topological sort algorithm has complexity same as Depth First Search. So, DFS has a complexity O(V+E).

mcqs.question: In most of the cases, topological sort starts from a node which has __________
mcqs.explanation: Topological sort starts with a node which has zero degree. If multiple such nodes exists then it can start with any node.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an application of topological sorting?

options.a: a) Finding prerequisite of a task
options.b: b) Finding Deadlock in an Operating System
options.c: c) Finding Cycle in a graph

mcqs.explanation: Topological sort tells what task should be done before a task can be started. It also detects cycle in the graph which is why it is used in the Operating System to find the deadlock. Ordered statistics is an application of Heap sort.

mcqs.question: Topological sort of a Directed Acyclic graph is?

options.c: c) Sometimes unique and sometimes not unique
options.d: d) Always unique if graph has even number of vertices

mcqs.answer: c) Sometimes unique and sometimes not unique
mcqs.explanation: The topological sort of a graph can be unique if we assume the graph as a single linked list and we can have multiple topological sort order if we consider a graph as a complete binary tree.

mcqs.question: Topological sort can be implemented by?

options.c: c) Using Depth and Breadth First Search

mcqs.answer: c) Using Depth and Breadth First Search
mcqs.explanation: We can implement topological sort by both BFS and DFS. In BFS, we use queue as data structure and in DFS, we use Linked list (if recursive) or Stack (if not recursive) as data structure.

mcqs.question: Topological sort is equivalent to which of the traversals in trees?
mcqs.explanation: In pre-order traversal of trees, we process the root first and then child from left to right.

mcqs.question: A man wants to go different places in the world. He has listed them down all. But there are some places where he wants to visit before some other places. What application of graph can he use to determine that?
mcqs.explanation: As the definition of topological sorting suggests, it is the way to do tasks in prescribed order. So, if he does topological sorting, it will be easy for him to recognize what should be the order to visit different places.

mcqs.question: When the topological sort of a graph is unique?

options.a: a) When there exists a hamiltonian path in the graph
options.b: b) In the presence of multiple nodes with indegree 0
options.c: c) In the presence of single node with indegree 0
options.d: d) In the presence of single node with outdegree 0

mcqs.answer: a) When there exists a hamiltonian path in the graph
mcqs.explanation: A hamiltonian path exists in a Directed Acyclic Graph when all pairs of consecutive vertices are in sorted order and are connected by edges. In such a case, there exists a unique topological sorting order.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Flooding Algorithm”.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is a property of the flooding algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: In the flooding algorithm, all the upcoming packets on a router are sent to all the connected nodes except the one on which it has arrived. Even in case of any failure, it can deliver all the packets via the shortest route. Hence, it is robust.

mcqs.question: In which layer of the computer networks is the flooding algorithm implemented?
mcqs.explanation: The network layer is responsible to transfer packets from source to destination. It must determine the best route so that the packets can be delivered through the shortest path. Hence, it uses a flooding algorithm to transmit packets quickly to every node in a large network.

mcqs.question: Consider the figure given below. If a message is flooded from node A, it will reach to which of the following nodes?

options.a: a) A, B, C, D, E, F
options.b: b) A, B, C, D, E,
options.c: c) A, B, C, D, E, F, G

mcqs.explanation: A message flooding from node A, will be transmitted to node B and node C. After that, it will be transmitted to node D via node B. Node E, F, G is not connected to any of the nodes A, B, C or D. Hence, the message will reach to node A, B, C and D only.

mcqs.question:
Given below is the pseudocode of the flooding algorithm. Node and message are denoted by n and m respectively. Which of the following best suits the blank? 
if m.id was seen before, discard
else, add m.id to list of seen messages and ______

options.b: b) forward the message in the direction from where it came.
options.c: c) forward the message to all neighbors of n
options.d: d) forward the message to the left neighbor of n

mcqs.answer: c) forward the message to all neighbors of n
mcqs.explanation: If a node receives a message that it has previously seen, it simply discards the message. However, if that is not the case, the node adds the message to the list of received messages and forwards it to all the neighboring nodes.

mcqs.question: Flooding algorithm shouldn’t be used if only a single destination needs the packet.
mcqs.explanation: In the flooding algorithm, the packets are sent to all the outgoing lines which creates a vast number of duplicate packets. Due to this, the network traffic is high with unwanted and duplicate data packets. Hence, the flooding algorithm shouldn’t be used if only a single destination needs the packet.

mcqs.question: Consider the figure given below, a message is sent from A to D with a maximum hop count of 3. What will be the total number of packets sent, if the flooding algorithm is applied on node A?
mcqs.explanation: If the flooding algorithm is applied on node A, the message will be transmitted to node B, I and J. Similarly, node B will transmit the packet to node C and F, node I will transmit to node J and K, and node L will transmit it to node M and P. We can observe that, each edge contains at most one copy of the message. Hence, the total number of packets flooded will be equal to the total number of edges which is 17.

mcqs.question: Flooding algorithm requires all the network information before implementation.
mcqs.explanation: The flooding algorithm follows the brute force approach and sends every incoming packet on every outgoing line it is connected to. Hence, flooding algorithms do not require network information like the cost of all the paths, load conditions or the topology before implementation.

mcqs.question: What will be the maximum number of rounds required to reach all nodes in the flooding algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: The diameter of the graph is the maximum distance in a graph between any two arbitrary nodes in it. Hence, it will take at most diameter of the graph rounds for the message to reach all nodes of the graph in the flooding algorithm.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is the message complexity for the flooding algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: In the flooding algorithm, the message is sent to all the connected edges. It floods the message to all the neighbors. Every node sends the message to its neighbor once, so each edge carries a maximum of one copy of the message. Hence, the message complexity is the lower bound of the total number of edges, which is O(|E|).

mcqs.question: Which type of flooding doesn’t send every incoming packet on every outgoing line?
mcqs.explanation: Selective flooding transmits the packet only in the direction of the destination, instead of sending all the incoming packets to all the outgoing lines. It is a variant of flooding. Due to this, the number of duplicate packets generated is less in number compared to the normal flooding.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Quickselect”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an alternative name of the quickselect algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: Quick select is a selection algorithm. It was developed by Tony Hoare, thus it is also known as Hoare’s selection algorithm.

mcqs.question: Quickselect is an example of ___________
mcqs.explanation: Quickselect is an example of a selection algorithm. It finds the kth smallest element from the given list.

mcqs.question: What will be the output if quickselect algorithm is applied to the array arr={1,5,4,3,7} with k given as 4?
mcqs.explanation: Quickselect algorithm finds the kth smallest element from the given list. So as here the given value of k is 4 so we need to find the fourth smallest element which is 5 in the given array.

mcqs.question: What is the auxiliary space requirement of the quickselect algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: Quickselect algorithm requires no extra space in order to calculate the desired result. It performs manipulations in the given array itself so its auxiliary space requirement will be O(1).

mcqs.question: Quickselect is an in-place algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: Quickselect’s auxiliary space requirement is O(1). So quickselect qualifies as an in-place algorithm.

mcqs.question: What is the best case time complexity of quickselect?
mcqs.explanation: Best case time complexity of quickselect is O(n). It is observed in the case where good pivots are chosen consistently then the array size decreases exponentially and thus the required element is found in linear time.

mcqs.question: Quickselect’s algorithm is similar to which of the following algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: Both quicksort and quickselect algorithms are closely related. They were developed by the same person. Like quicksort, quickselect also works by choosing a pivot and partitioning array.

mcqs.question: What is the worst case time complexity of quickselect?
mcqs.explanation: Worst case complexity occurs in the case where bad pivots are chosen consistently due to which the size of the array decreases in the steps of 1 only. This leads to a time complexity of O(n<sup>2</sup>).

mcqs.question: What is the average case time complexity of quickselect?
mcqs.explanation: In quickselect, we don’t recur for both portions of the array. Only that portion is considered where the smallest element lies. So this causes the average time complexity to be O(n).

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a disadvantage of quickselect?

options.b: b) Poor best case time complexity
options.c: c) Poor average case time complexity
options.d: d) Poor worst case time complexity

mcqs.answer: d) Poor worst case time complexity
mcqs.explanation: Quickselect has a poor worst case time complexity of O(n<sup>2</sup>). There are algorithms which have O(n) time complexity in the worst case.

   Select a pivotIndex between left and right

mcqs.question: What is co-ordinate compression?

options.a: a) process of reassigning co-ordinates to remove gaps
options.b: b) inserting gaps in a co-ordinate system

mcqs.answer: a) process of reassigning co-ordinates to remove gaps
mcqs.explanation: Co-ordinate compression is the process of reassigning co-ordinates in order to remove gaps. This helps in improving efficiency of a solution.

mcqs.question: What is the need for co-ordinate compression?

options.c: c) for improving both time and space complexity

mcqs.answer: c) for improving both time and space complexity
mcqs.explanation: Co-ordinate compression is the process of reassigning co-ordinates in order to remove gaps. This helps in improving both time and space complexity of a solution.

mcqs.question: Co-ordinate compression reduces the number of squares in a graph.
mcqs.explanation: The idea behind co-ordinate compression is to reduce the number of squares in a graph by converting them into rectangles of viable size. This reduces the time complexity of traversal.

mcqs.question: Co-ordinate compression can only be applied in a co-ordinate system problem.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Square Root Decomposition”.

mcqs.question: What is the purpose of using square root decomposition?

options.a: a) to reduce the time complexity of a code
options.b: b) to increase the space complexity of a code
options.c: c) to reduce the space complexity of a code
options.d: d) to reduce the space and time complexity of a code

mcqs.answer: a) to reduce the time complexity of a code
mcqs.explanation: Square decomposition is mainly used in competitive programming to optimize code. It reduces the time complexity by a factor of √n.

mcqs.question: By what factor time complexity is reduced when we apply square root decomposition to a code?
mcqs.explanation: In square root decomposition a given array is decomposed into small parts each of size √n. This reduces the time complexity of the code by a factor of √n.

mcqs.question: What will be the worst case time complexity of finding the sum of elements in a given range of (l,r) in an array of size n?
mcqs.explanation: For a given array of size n we have to traverse all n elements in the worst case. In such a case l=0, r=n-1 so the time complexity will be O(n).

mcqs.question: What will be the worst case time complexity of finding the sum of elements in a given range of (l,r) in an array of size n when we use square root optimization?
mcqs.explanation: When we use square root optimization we decompose the given array into √n chunks each of size √n. So after calculating the sum of each chunk individually, we require to iterate only 3*√n times to calculate the sum in the worst case.

mcqs.question: Total how many iterations are required to find the sum of elements in a given range of (l,r) in an array of size n when we use square root optimization?
mcqs.explanation: After calculating the sum of each chunk individually we require to iterate only 3*√n times to calculate the sum in the worst case. It is because two of the √n factors consider the worst case time complexity of summing elements in the first and last block. Whereas the third √n considers the factor of summing the √n chunks.

mcqs.question: What will be the time complexity of update query operation in an array of size n when we use square root optimization?
mcqs.explanation: The time complexity of query operation remains the same in both square root optimized code and non optimized code. We simply find the chunk in which the update requires to be performed and then add the new updated value at the desired index.

mcqs.question: Square root decomposition technique is only applicable when the number of indices in an array is a perfect square.
mcqs.explanation: Square root decomposition technique can be applied to an array with any number of indices. It does not require this number to be a perfect square.

mcqs.question: What will be the worst case time complexity of code to find sum in given query range (l,r) in an array of size n with q number of such queries?
mcqs.explanation: For finding the result of one query the worst case time complexity will be n. So for q queries the time complexity will be O(q*n). This can be reduced by using square root optimization.

mcqs.question: What will be the worst case time complexity of code to find sum in given query range (l,r) in an array of size n with q number of such queries when we apply MO’s algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: Mo’s algorithm requires O(q*√n) + O(n*√n) time for processing all the queries. It is better than the naive solution where O(n*q) time is required.

mcqs.question: Mo’s algorithm can only be used for problems where the query can be calculated from the result of the previous query.
mcqs.explanation: Mo’s algorithm uses the result of the previous query in order to compute the result of the given query. It cannot be implemented where such a scenario is not possible.

mcqs.question: What will be the time complexity of the code to find a minimum element from an array of size n and uses square root decomposition(exclude pre processing time)?
mcqs.explanation: For finding the minimum element in a given array of size n using square root decomposition we first divide the array into √n chunks and calculate the result for them individually. So for a given query, the result of middle blocks has to be calculated along with the extreme elements. This takes O(√n) time in the worst case.
